#### 13. CHAT-16's composer core, chunked (the coordinator, 2026-09-15 evening)

What landed today under CHAT-16 is part 4's amendments (the sources on
the wire and the row, the deliverables, the denied deliverable) and the
`status` events. The core is the composer itself, designed above under
"Structured execution and bounded composition" (one shared path from
outcomes to a reply; the decision table; the native tool-result
messages; the two-completion budget) with part 4, 6 and 9's amendments
riding on it. It is cut into seven chunks so that the judgment sits in
two of them and the rest is typing with a precise brief.

K1, the native tool-result messages (mechanical). `spec/llm/ts/types.ts`
gains `role: tool` messages with `tool_call_id`, and an assistant
message retains its `tool_calls`; the client serializes both for the
OpenAI-style API; the wire tests cover them; nothing in the engine sends
them yet.

K2, the composer (judgment; Session A). One module,
`backend/src/lib/composer.ts`, `composeTurn(outcomes, context, constraints)`,
called on both paths wherever the engine turns retained outcomes into a
reply today (the plugin-reply sites, the forced ladder, the deliverable
line stays as it is). The decision table verbatim: one succeeded outcome
with a `reply` and no `synthesis_hint` is delivered as it is; a
data-only result, a result with `synthesis_hint`, or two outcomes with
at least one success and no pending interaction take one final
completion, the turn's second and last model call, with the results as
native tool-result messages (K1), no tools offered, the persona and the
context as on a model turn, results as data never instructions, and
the composed text through the guards like any draft; every outcome
failed takes the deterministic safe text; a pending interaction stays
literal; a composition that fails falls back to the ordered direct
replies and failure messages; a data-only result with no usable reply
is "I found information, but couldn't put the answer together", never
"Done.". The budget is enforced in one place: a turn that already spent
its initial call and its corrective or composing call makes no third.
The websearch recipe's private `llm_complete` step goes when the
composer composes its rows (chunk A of part 4 already carries the rows
in `data`), so the search answer costs one composition and not a third
call. CONS-01's readers ride here: the constraints' `shape`, `length`
and banned phrases are one line of the composer prompt, and the shape
is a parameter of the composed turn (K4 renders it). The `[turn]` line
records `composed: direct | composition | failure | pending`.

K3, `model_knowledge` marking (mechanical, after K2). A world question
answered from the weights with no lookup carries an outcome of evidence
kind `model_knowledge` (part 1 rule 7); "how do you know that" is
composed from the outcome ("that one I just know" or "I looked it up,
the link's below"); the chip shows only for a lookup. Rows:
`checkable-fact`'s last two turns.

K4, the requested shape (mechanical, after K2). Part 9 rule 4: a `shape`
or `length` constraint, or a shape ask in the same utterance, renders a
list from the result rows (up to five in the bubble, the rest in the
document once COMP-01 exists), a number-only answer as the number, a
one-line answer as one line; `max_sentences` yields to an explicit
shape. Row: `list-shape-on-lookup`.

K5, typed dates (mechanical, after K2). Part 6 rule 2: every date a
lookup or typed source returned reaches the composer with its relation
to the frozen clock from `dateRelation()`, and the line uses it when
the question was about timing ("yes, today", never "on the 14th" when
the 14th is today). Row: `lookup-date-relative`.

K6, the streaming state machine (judgment; Session A, inside K2 or right
after). One machine owns deciding, executing, composing, finished and
cancelled; the composing phase streams the composition's own deltas
sentence by sentence; the blocking path collects the same approved
deltas; the public events stay as they are (K1's messages are internal).

K7, pictures and videos inline (mechanical, after K2; the owner's call
of 2026-09-15). A picture ask whose search returns an image result puts
the image on the reply (`TurnValue.media`, additive: kind, url, source
host), the chat surface renders it in the bubble, and the "page with it
is below" line becomes the fallback when no result is an image; a video
ask embeds the platform's player through the household's existing
integration where one exists, else the search's video result; each is a
new outbound connection with its own privacy-page row in the same
commit. The child band keeps its grown-up line and no media.

Order: K1 now (Codex), K2 and K6 (A) as soon as K1 is in, then K3, K4,
K5 and K7 (Codex) on K2's branch. ACT-03's plan (the composer's
permitted moves, `repeat: forbidden` after an objection) is the item
after; K2 takes the moves as a parameter with a default so ACT-03 plugs
in without reopening the composer.

## Session B, lane 16: ACT-02's training half (2026-09-14)

`backend/scripts/train/turn-signal-heads.ts` and its tests, per
BACKLOG's ACT-02 item: three multinomial heads (act, stance, emotion)
over the 768-dim nomic vector `utteranceVector` already computes.
**Finding: none of the three heads ships.** The stated margin is 5
macro-F1 points over the rule pass alone; act and emotion both land
negative, and stance has no independent human-labeled validation to
measure against yet. `classifyTurnSignal()` in `lib/turnSignal.ts`
stands as written; `lib/turnSignalAssets.ts` has nothing to wire
against a trained artifact.

**Training.** The emotion head trains on GoEmotions (Apache 2.0, real
human labels, its own published Ekman mapping - `joy` maps to our
`happiness`) and validates on DailyDialog's test split, never trained
on (CC BY-NC-SA, research license). The act and stance heads train on
a 6,000-turn corpus the 4B labels under DailyDialog's own act
definitions and this repo's own stance definitions, pooled from
Taskmaster-1 and CCPE-M (both CC BY 4.0, 103,252 candidates before the
cap, taskmaster1-self and taskmaster1-woz's own USER turns only), the
bench fixture's un-hinted turns, and synthetic roster dialogues
authored for this lane (none existed before). Every dataset file
verified against the registry's own checksums first (14/14 ok); the
4B labeling pass ran detached (own spawned chat and embed engines on
:18788/:18795, never the household's), 6,000/6,000 labeled, 0 failed.
Class-weighted loss, temperature scaling and per-class thresholds
(target precision 80%) on a held-out split of each head's own training
data.

**Validation - the real numbers, DailyDialog's human labels (act and
emotion) and the bench fixture's human-hinted turns (all three):**

Act, DailyDialog test (7,740 turns): rules alone 66.1% macro F1, rules
plus the head 61.8% - **margin -4.4 points**. The head's own
per-class numbers show why: directive drops to 30.7% F1, commissive to
8.1% (520 of 718 true commissive turns end up called `inform`), while
question and inform themselves stay reasonable (85.9%, 79.2%). The
composition only ever lets the head override a rule call of `inform`
(the rule's own catch-all default, never a confident directive or
question), so this is the head's own confusion on exactly the
"inform versus commissive" distinction docs/dev.md section 12 named as
its job, not a composition bug. On the fixture's 218 human-labeled
turns: 96.3% both ways, margin 0.0 (already near-ceiling from the
rules alone; too small and too easy a sample to move on its own).

Emotion, DailyDialog test, neutral-vs-not: rules alone 89.2% F1
(precision 83.3%, recall 96.0%), rules plus head 79.1% (precision
89.7%, recall 70.8%) - **margin -10.1 points**. Full validation:
macro F1 14.3% (66.5% of turns below-threshold, ECE 0.2752), neutral
recall alone 1.3% - the head learned to fire `happiness` far too
eagerly out of GoEmotions' own domain (short social-media comments)
against DailyDialog's everyday dialogue: 1,596 of 6,321 true-neutral
turns get called happiness. GoEmotions' own in-domain sanity check
(never used for tuning) is a healthier-looking but still weak 23.7%
macro F1, confirming this is a real domain-shift failure, not a
training bug: the dev split the head was calibrated on (GoEmotions
dev, 38.7% macro F1) does not represent the distribution it is
actually asked to judge. Neutral false-positive rate: 10.3% at the
natural distribution, 0.0% on the balanced slice (the balanced slice's
neutral recall is 5.9%, so its FP rate looks good only because it
almost never predicts neutral at all).

Stance: no independent human-labeled source exists at corpus scale
(DailyDialog carries no stance labels), so the corpus-wide number is
not reported - the org's training rule against validating on the
labeler's own output leaves nothing else to measure it against until a
person works through the 500-turn review sheet
(`data-scratch/eval/turn-signal-review-sheet.md`, git-ignored,
regenerated by the same script). The fixture's 8 human-labeled turns
are too few to mean much (rules alone 60.0% macro F1, rules plus head
60.0%, 0 of the 8 rows overridden) but are reported for completeness.
A second code review (2026-09-14) caught the rules-plus-head
composition reading the wrong confidence for stance: `turnSignal.ts`
exposes each clause's confidence as the minimum of its act and stance
confidence, not the stance marker's own, so a marker-based stance
(reported, quoted, hypothetical, joke) paired with a low-confidence
inform act read as low overall and was wrongly treated as the rule's
own default - letting the head override a correct rule call. Fixed by
gating on the stance VALUE first (only `asserted` is ever the rule's
residual default) and the confidence second, the same shape as the
act and emotion fix above; the original 56.0% composed number this
section first reported was wrong and is corrected here.

**Why the corpus does not fix this on its own.** The 4B-labeled
training corpus is exactly what dev.md's own training rule warns
about: labels from the labeler, never independently confirmed at scale
before they shaped the weights. The emotion head's failure is a
distribution mismatch (GoEmotions is not DailyDialog); the act head's
failure is a genuine hard case (inform-vs-commissive is exactly the
ambiguous residual the rule pass already punts on) that a bigger or
differently-sampled 4B-labeled corpus might or might not fix - that is
a design question, not something this run's own numbers answer.

What that design question actually needs, reconciled with the
coordinator 2026-09-14: the act head's collapse is on the 4B-labeled
corpus specifically, so the next attempt needs real human act labels
in the training set, not more of the same labeler's own output at a
bigger size - DailyDialog's own training split carries them, but it is
CC BY-NC-SA, and whether a derivative weight trained on it could ship
is an org licensing call, not this lane's, or the next attempt targets
a different, license-clean source of human act labels entirely. The
emotion head's failure is not a tuning problem either: GoEmotions
alone cannot be the training set for spoken-dialogue emotion, because
its domain (short written social-media comments) does not represent
what the hub actually classifies (spoken household turns) closely
enough for the learned weights to transfer, whatever the corpus size.

**What ships:** nothing. The three JSON artifacts
(`backend/scripts/train/out/*.json`, embedding identity
nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M.gguf sha256
d4e388894e09cf3816e8b0896d81d265b55e7a9fff9ab03fe8bf4ef5e11295ac, label
map version 1) are gitignored and stay on the training machine, per
their own artifacts' `training` field marking the act/stance heads'
data as 4B-labeled, never human ground truth. `data-scratch/datasets/
SOURCES.md` records GoEmotions' license and the reviewed-sample rule.
The measured alternative dev.md section 12 names for exactly this
outcome (a compact MiniLM-class encoder reading the previous turn plus
the person's, through the existing ONNX runtime, warm CPU p95 under
20 ms) is the next real design question, not built here - out of this
lane's scope, a call for whoever picks ACT-02 back up.

Full per-class tables, confusion matrices and the exact run command are
in the training script's own commit; this section is the acceptance
report the item's exit criterion names.

## FEED-01: a rating is a label

`ReplyFeedback` is one record per `(turn_id, person_id)`. Its `turn_id`
joins the rated assistant turn to RVW-1's weekly label export; the export
adds `feedback_verdict` and `feedback_reason` beside that turn's `rung` and
`rules`. `source` preserves the write provenance, while `created_at` and
`hlc` keep the shared record envelope required by the platform.

A rating is evidence about a reply, not a new instruction for the reply.
The stored label therefore never edits `reply_text`, re-runs generation,
or changes the turn's outcomes. RVW-2 may classify the label later; the
original response remains the immutable thing being reviewed.

Child band: show only the two feedback buttons. Do not show the reason
chips and do not write a reason for a child-band rating. Adults and teens
may use the five fixed reason chips on a down verdict.

The mechanical follow-ups are pickup-ready:

- **Table and migration.** Files: `backend/src/db/schema.ts`,
  `backend/src/db/migrations/` and the schema-version tests. Pattern:
  mirror the nearest actor-scoped table and migration, including HLC and
  person-erasure coverage. Acceptance: unique `(turn_id, person_id)`;
  safe upsert; deleted people leave no feedback rows. Exit: targeted
  backend tests, schema walk, and `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- **Action bar wiring.** Files: `frontend/src/apps/chat/chatActionBar.tsx`
  and its tests. Pattern: mirror `chatMemoryActions.ts` for the call and
  `chatMemoryChip` for the chips, using assistant-ui's `FeedbackAdapter`.
  Acceptance: positive and negative taps persist, a down tap opens the five
  chips, and child band renders buttons only. Exit: frontend tests and the
  opened reason-row screenshot.
- **Export join and test.** Files: `backend/scripts/bench/labels.ts` and
  `backend/tests/labels.test.ts`. Pattern: mirror `labelOf()` and
  `exportLabels()`'s weekly JSONL path. Acceptance: `turn_id` places
  verdict and reason beside rung and fired rules, with no reply mutation.
  Exit: labels tests, a reconciled fixture export, and `bash scripts/check.sh`.

## STATS-01: the advanced view

The advanced view answers a narrow adult question: what did the engine do
while producing this reply? It is operational telemetry attached to the
reply, not a second transcript and not a model-confidence claim. A child
band never receives or renders it. An adult gets a compact readout only
after turning on the per-person `ui.show_turn_stats` setting, which is off
by default and is deliberately separate from the household's engine
health page.

### Decision

`TurnStats` is an additive, nullable object on `TurnValue` and on the
hub-internal conversation-turn row. Every member is nullable because the
stub engine, an older llama-server, a deterministic package answer, and a
stream that ends without a final timing frame are all valid states. The
shape is:

```ts
interface TurnStats {
  prompt_tokens: number | null;
  predicted_tokens: number | null;
  tokens_per_second: number | null;
  time_to_first_token_ms: number | null;
  total_time_ms: number | null;
  context_tokens: number | null;
  context_used_percent: number | null;
  cache_reuse_tokens: number | null;
  cache_reuse_percent: number | null;
  engine: string | null;
  stop_reason: string | null;
}
```

The engine-owned values are `prompt_tokens`, `predicted_tokens`,
`tokens_per_second`, `cache_reuse_tokens`, `cache_reuse_percent`, and
`stop_reason` when llama-server's final streamed chunk provides its
`usage` or `timings` fields. `time_to_first_token_ms` is MaiPai's own
elapsed measurement from the turn start to the first generated delta.
`total_time_ms` is MaiPai's elapsed measurement through finalization.
`context_tokens` is the prompt token count, and
`context_used_percent` is left null until the engine exposes a verified
context-window size. This avoids presenting a prompt-size estimate as a
context-capacity fact. `engine` is `formatEngineIdentity()` from
`lib/engineIdentity.ts`, so it contains only the host label, build, and
model file name. It never contains a hostname, URL, path, or model hash.

The stream client owns parsing the final chunk and returns a small mutable
stats carrier beside its token generator. The turn engine combines that
carrier with `TurnTimings` when it finalizes the reply. Missing or invalid
numbers become `null`, never `NaN`, `Infinity`, or a fabricated zero.
`tokens_per_second` uses llama-server's value when present, otherwise it
is computed only from positive predicted tokens and positive predicted
milliseconds. Cache percentage is `cache_n / (cache_n + prompt_n)` only
when that denominator is positive. The `[turn]` log line carries the same
sanitized object as the route, making a screen readout and an operational
record agree.

The adult UI places a `Details` toggle in the chat surface and a compact
one-line stats caption under each assistant reply, in the same placement
as `ChatSourceCaption`. The toggle state is persisted at person scope,
off by default. A tap or keyboard activation of the caption opens a kit
popover with the full list. The message metadata carries the same object
for live and reloaded turns, so the view does not change after a reload.
Child-band projection drops the object before rendering, and the child
band has no toggle, caption, or popover path. Stats are explanatory
telemetry only: they do not alter routing, safety, budgets, or retention.

### Alternatives rejected

- Put raw llama-server chunks on `TurnValue`: rejected because the raw
  payload is unstable, can contain fields the UI does not need, and would
  make the hostname or model path easy to expose accidentally.
- Require stats on every turn: rejected because deterministic replies and
  older engines do not have engine timings; additive nullability keeps
  existing clients and fixtures valid.
- Derive context percentage from the configured context override:
  rejected until the active engine confirms that capacity. A prompt count
  without a verified denominator is shown as a count only.
- Put the toggle in a household or browser setting: rejected because the
  advanced view is an adult's preference and must follow that person to
  their other signed-in device without changing another adult's view.
- Show any of this in the child band or include engine URLs/hostnames:
  rejected by the child disclosure and privacy boundaries.

### Acceptance

The backend fixture stream with `usage`, `timings`, and `finish_reason`
produces the corresponding numbers; the same stream without `timings`
produces nulls without `NaN`. A model turn's `[turn]` log and `done`
value agree. The adult toggle is off by default and persists per person;
when on, the one-line readout and full list are visible. Child band
renders neither. One desktop screenshot shows the full list open.

## Conversations: search, pin, group

Verdict: search is a per-person query over the conversation titles and turn text the hub already holds; pin is one boolean on the spec conversation record; groups remain an open design question because folders, tags, and projects each imply different ownership and nesting semantics, so no grouping model is built here.

The S half uses SQLite `LIKE` because the schema has no conversation FTS table. Search is always scoped to the authenticated person's own conversations, and pinning is an additive field on the existing conversation record and PATCH route. Grouping is intentionally left at the design question: folders provide hierarchy, tags provide many-to-many labels, and projects provide a richer container model, so choosing one without a household use case would harden the wrong contract.

## PAGE-01: reading a page the person asked about

Verdict: a page ask is one foreground fetch after the household's own SearXNG search, not a crawler. The integration has one maintained choke point with `search` and `page.read` methods, one token bucket, one real user agent, a public-host redirect check, and a robots.txt check. A 403, 429, captcha or robots refusal stops the page request and returns the fixed site-declined line. There is no retry through a refusal and no prefetch or link fan-out.

The reader uses Linkedom (ISC) for the DOM and Mozilla Readability (Apache-2.0) for the article boundary. Both licenses are compatible with this repository's AGPL-3.0 package license. Cheerio plus a separate HTML-to-text helper was rejected because it would create two independently maintained parsing surfaces. The reader bounds the page text, links, and headings before they enter an outcome or model context. Links retain their visible text, absolute sanitized href, rel, and nearby text. The result reuses ATT-01's bounded document chunk shape, with the page URL as its source, so COMP-01 can build the details document without a second artifact contract.

The websearch recipe carries the page result beside its search rows. The turn engine requests `read_page` only for page-shaped lookup language such as support, download, driver, price, fix, or page, and the same path can be extended for an explicit article lookup. For a link deliverable, the engine selects a page link whose text, href, or nearby text contains the requested field words. The selected href and title become the first source. If no link matches, the spoken result is exactly that the page does not have that field; model prose cannot substitute for the missing page evidence. Child projection keeps the grown-up line and removes page sources and document links according to the existing ceiling.

## Home adopts `@maipai/core` (core-v0.1.0, 2026-09-20)

Pinned as `"@maipai/core": "file:../../shared/core"` in `backend/package.json`, per `shared`'s own pin design (no registry; `bun install` copies a real, self-contained package from the sibling `getmaipai/shared` checkout). **The pinned tag is `core-v0.1.0`.** Bumping it means checking out the new tag in the sibling `shared` checkout, then re-running `bun install` in `backend/` and updating the `CORE_PIN` line in `scripts/check.sh` - `bun.lock` records the resolved copy, and `check.sh` fails loud (before anything else runs) if the sibling `shared` checkout is missing or its `core/package.json` version doesn't match the pin, the same honesty-of-the-pin contract `@maipai/standards` already uses.

Sixteen helpers that used to live in `backend/src/lib/` (`log`, `withTimeout`, `paths`'s `ensureDataDir`/`statMtimeMs`, `archive`, `hardware`, `openapi`, `secretThrottle`, `hlc`, `id`'s `randomSuffix`, `secrets`, `keystore`, `rateLimiter`, `singleflight`, `ssrfGuard`, `backupCrypto`) now import their actual logic from `@maipai/core/src/*`. Four (`withTimeout`, `archive`, `singleflight`, `ssrfGuard`) had no Home-specific state and their consumers now import `@maipai/core/src/*` directly. The rest kept their `@/lib/*` file as a thin wrapper - Home's own instantiation (its data directory, its keystore's `appId`, its device id as the hlc node, its `TRUST_PROXY` setting) around a `core` factory - specifically so the module-level singleton behavior every existing caller already depended on (one shared hlc clock, one shared sign-in throttle across every route, one shared rate limiter) survives unchanged; no consumer file needed to change beyond a handful of test fixtures gaining `HardwareInfo`'s new (Stack-added) `osVersion` field.

**New at this adoption, not before: a broken keystore refuses to boot.** `core-v0.1.0`'s keystore (`@maipai/core/src/keystore.ts`) throws `KeystoreProtectionFailedError` when Windows DPAPI protection fails, rather than silently writing an unprotected plaintext key to disk the way this repo's own pre-adoption `keystore.ts` did (a real gap a code review on the `shared` side caught). `backend/src/index.ts` now calls `lib/secret.ts`'s `ensureSecretPepperReady()` right after installing the log/fatal handlers, before the server accepts a single request: if the household's own PIN/password pepper can't be resolved, the hub logs `[fatal] boot refused: ...` and exits, instead of leaving every sign-in route to hit the same failure later as an opaque 500. This only changes behavior on Windows when PowerShell is blocked or unavailable; `tests/secret.test.ts`'s `ensureSecretPepperReady` describe block covers both the healthy path and the refusal (faking `process.platform` since this dev machine's own DPAPI path never runs for real).

The websearch package's data source says that a page ask sends that one page URL to the household's own SearXNG or page host, keeps the result only in the turn outcome and details document, and does not fetch linked pages. The acceptance rows are `download-link-on-page`, `value-on-page`, `page-without-requested-link`, and `who-is-builds-a-card-from-the-page`. The latter remains bounded by the current card schema while article sections are carried in the document result until the additive article-card spec work is scheduled.

## Home adopts `@maipai/ui` (ui-v0.1.0 through 0.1.3, 2026-09-20)

Pinned as `"@maipai/ui": "file:../../shared/ui"` in `frontend/package.json`, the same pin design as `@maipai/core`. **The pinned tag was `ui-v0.1.3` at this commit** (moved to `ui-v0.1.6` by step 5a, below - a newer pin always means checking this section's own file inventory against the sibling `shared` checkout's current state, not this paragraph); `scripts/check.sh`'s `UI_PIN` line enforces whichever tag is current the same way `CORE_PIN` does. `frontend/src/kit/` shrank to five things with no shared home: `assistant-ui/` (the chat composer's own vendored primitives, migrating in step 5b), `ui/textarea.tsx` (assistant-ui's only remaining local dependency), `hooks/usePinAutoSubmit.ts` and `hooks/useSelectMode.ts` (Home-specific interaction hooks), and `tokens.css` (Home's own color palette - cyan accent, the kit provides structure, never colors). Every other kit file - all of `primitives/`, `schema/`, `settings/`, `ui/`, `icons.ts`, `responsive.ts`, `useSurface.ts`, `utils.ts` - is gone, superseded by `@maipai/ui/src/*` subpath imports (no barrel, matching `@maipai/core`'s own convention). `src/shell/Shell.tsx`, `PhoneNav.tsx`, `tvNav.ts`, and `search/{CommandPalette,SearchResultGroups}.tsx` are gone too, superseded by the kit's own `Shell`/`PhoneNav`/`tvNav`/`search/*`; `src/shell/AppShell.tsx` is the new, much smaller wrapper wiring Home's own features (`ProfileSwitcher`, `NotificationBell`, `PinToggle`, the Favorites nav group, `usePinnedApps`/`useSearchCommand`/`useAppearance`) into the kit's `Shell` slots - "the kit gets a slot, Home keeps the feature."

**Known gaps, tracked not dropped** (`docs/BACKLOG.md`, `shared`'s own): the kit's `Shell` has no TV-focusable rail yet (the arrow-key/remote nav the old hand-built `Shell.tsx` had via `@noriginmedia/norigin-spatial-navigation`) - not one of the five features the owner's original ruling protected, and `far`/TV surface routing/highlighting (`useFocusable`, `ensureTvNavInit`) is simply not wired into `AppShell.tsx` this round. The sidebar's own dedicated "Search" nav row is also gone; Cmd/Ctrl+K and `HomePage.tsx`'s own inline prompt box remain as working entry points, and the kit gained a real header search button (`ui-v0.1.2`, below) so touch surfaces keep a visible way in too.

### The shared/ui detour: four real regressions found only by actually running this

`ui-v0.1.0` was built and reviewed against Home's OWN kit files still present in the tree for comparison, but nobody had ever made Home's real build actually consume `@maipai/ui`'s real source until this adoption - regressions surfaced across three follow-up tags (`ui-v0.1.1`, `0.1.2`, `0.1.3`), each fixed in `shared` (not patched around in Home) since every future adopter (`bot`, `go`) would hit them identically:

- **`ui-v0.1.1`: the accessibility floor gap.** Comparing Home's own already-hardened `kit/ui/*.tsx` against `ui-v0.1.0`'s primitives found that everything routed through the Stack path (`button`, `input`, `checkbox`, `select`, `tabs`, `dropdown-menu`, `command`, `dialog`/`sheet`'s close button, `toggle`, `label`, `table`, `breadcrumb`, `sidebar`'s menu button) shipped without docs/UI.md's 48px touch-target and 16px type floor Home's own copies already carried. design-resolver confirmed the floor belongs in the kit itself, not a per-product re-patch (`getmaipai/.github/docs/UI.md:180-182` names the kit, not the product, as what "refuses to go below" it). A code review before landing caught and fixed five more real overlap bugs the port itself introduced (adjacent compact controls - a segmented appearance control, `NotificationPopover`'s two buttons, `PropertyPanel`'s action row - whose new invisible hit-area extensions collided into each other). See `shared/docs/dev.md`'s own "Workspace status" for the full file-by-file inventory.
- **`ui-v0.1.2`: a real search button.** Owner ruling on this exact adoption: a phone has no keyboard, so a Cmd/Ctrl+K-only palette trigger meant search existed on desktop and vanished on phone - "one product, every screen" forbids that split. `Shell`'s header now renders a real 48px search button whenever `search` is configured.
- **`ui-v0.1.3`: the sidebar's own keyboard-avoidance and layout fixes.** Landed AFTER `ui-v0.1.2` was already tagged, pushed, and pinned - Home's OWN full screenshot matrix (not the fast `--a11y-only` two-combo pass) surfaced these only once it actually ran end to end against the pinned kit. `ui-v0.1.0`'s `sidebar.tsx` came from Stack's own reconciled kit, which had never needed (and so never carried) three fixes Home's own copy had already earned in production: the shell wrapper wasn't `position: fixed`, so a phone's on-screen keyboard panning the document dragged the whole shell down with it instead of staying anchored (`useVisualViewportHeight`, previously Home-only dead code with no consumer left after `Shell.tsx`'s own deletion, moved to `@maipai/ui/src/hooks/` - a real kit-level concern, not a Home one, once the wrapper needed it back); `SidebarInset` was missing `min-w-0`, letting a long unwrapped string stretch a page past the viewport; and several call-site `className` overrides were silently defeating primitives their OWN `ui-v0.1.1` fix had just floor-corrected (`nav-main.tsx`'s nav-row `h-10 text-[15px]` override, `SidebarTrigger`'s `size-7` override, `RailToggle`'s hand-rolled unaudited `<button>`, and `CommandDialog`'s sr-only header rendered as a sibling of `DialogContent` instead of a child - the exact axe `region` bug Home's own `command.tsx` had already found and fixed once). A second code review before `ui-v0.1.3` landed caught two more: `CommandDialog`'s own `<Command>` still carrying a competing height override, and `Sidebar`'s mobile (`Sheet`) branch losing the same landmark fix on phone width (props spread onto `Sheet`, Radix's `Dialog.Root`, which has no DOM output of its own). Verified by the full screenshot matrix (every route, every viewport including `far`/TV, both themes) actually passing clean end to end.

### Two build-tool bugs, Home-side only (not shared/ui's to fix)

Consuming `@maipai/ui`'s real source (subpath-imported directly, no dist build, per its own no-barrel convention) exposed two genuine Vite/TypeScript integration bugs, both fixed in `frontend/tsconfig.json` and `frontend/vite.config.ts`:

- **A duplicate `@types/react`.** `@maipai/ui`'s own `bun install` (a separate project root) resolves its devDependencies independently of Home's; even at matching versions, the two are physically different files, and TypeScript's `Ref<T>` types use a branded `VoidOrUndefinedOnly` marker specifically to reject exactly this "same-looking but different-module" mixing, throwing "two different types with this name exist" on every ref-typed prop. `tsconfig.json`'s `@/kit/*` fallback path (`@maipai/ui`'s own internal alias, distinct from Home's own residual `@/kit/*`) has to route through `./node_modules/@maipai/ui/src/*` (the installed symlink) rather than a raw relative path straight into `../../shared/ui/src/*`, so the file opens from INSIDE bun's own dependency graph and inherits its already-unified `@types/react`, not a separate copy reached by bypassing node_modules entirely.
- **A duplicate module instance across an async chunk boundary.** The same distinction matters again in `vite.config.ts`: `kitAliasPlugin`'s first attempt used a raw filesystem path for the same reason above, and Rolldown's own chunk-splitting didn't always recognize that path and the "normal" `@maipai/ui/src/...` import path as the same physical module once one of them crossed a lazy `import()` boundary (`PeoplePage` is one of `App.tsx`'s lazy routes) - two separate `react`/`react-router-dom`/`@maipai/ui` module instances got bundled, each with its own `createContext()` call, so `Shell`'s `SidebarProvider` and `AppSidebar`'s `useSidebar()` stopped sharing one context the moment the lazy chunk loaded ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')", then "useSidebar must be used within a SidebarProvider" once the first symptom was fixed). Fixed by routing the plugin's resolution through the bare `@maipai/ui/src/*` package specifier (`this.resolve`) instead, plus `resolve.dedupe: ["react", "react-dom", "react-router-dom"]` as a second line of defense (`react-router-dom` is a direct, not peer, dependency of `@maipai/ui` too - a `shared`-side architecture gap worth a peer-dependency fix later, not blocking here since Home's own dedupe covers it). Fixing this also dropped the entry chunk from 2.17 MiB (which had needed a `maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes` PWA-precache override, the same one lane 10 item 2 removed once real code-splitting existed) back to ~1.83 MiB - the duplication, not real kit growth, was the actual cause of the size regression this override would have papered over.

**A third, unrelated build gap surfaced alongside these:** Tailwind v4's automatic content detection never scans `node_modules` by default, so any class that appears only inside `@maipai/ui`'s own source (never coincidentally also written somewhere in Home's own `src/`) generated no CSS rule at all. `h-svh` was the one that gave it away - Home's own `kit/ui/sidebar.tsx` used to carry that exact class too, so Tailwind had always generated it "by accident" until that file was deleted in this same adoption, silently turning the shell wrapper's height into `auto` (sized to content - the real conversation's composer sitting 2000+ px below the fold, only a fraction of it fitting the visible viewport). Fixed with an explicit `@source "../../../../shared/ui/src";` in `src/kit/tokens.css`.

### A fourth regression, Home-side: the destructive badge/button in dark mode

The kit's own `Button`/`Badge` "destructive" variant pairs a solid `--destructive` background with white text. Home's own `--destructive` token is deliberately lightened in dark mode (see `tokens.css`'s own comment: darkening it loses contrast against this theme's near-black surfaces when used as text or a translucent tint, the pairing Home's own now-deleted `button.tsx`/`badge.tsx` used) - paired with white text as a SOLID background instead, that same lightness fails contrast (axe `color-contrast`, serious; found on `RepairsSection`'s destructive `Badge`, filed as `getmaipai/home#122` before the real cause was traced and the issue closed with the fix). Reasserting Home's own tinted destructive treatment via a `tokens.css` override (`[data-slot="badge"][data-variant="destructive"]`, `[data-slot="button"][data-variant="destructive"]`, dark mode only) rather than touching the shared token or the kit's own component: this is Home's own color choice, the same "kit provides structure, product provides color" split as `tokens.css`'s own cyan accent everywhere else. `DevicesSection`, `HealthSection`, and `NotificationsPage` all use the same `variant="destructive"` pattern and get the same fix for free.

### Verification

Full `scripts/check.sh` green: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint .` (updated: `tests/eslint-rules.test.ts`'s own lucide-react-exemption fixture moved from the now-deleted `kit/icons.ts` to the still-vendored `kit/assistant-ui/`, matching `eslint.config.js`'s own updated comments and messages, which pointed at `@/kit/icons`/`@/kit/ui/*` paths that no longer exist), `bun test` (488 passing), `bun run build` (2270 KiB precached, under the 2 MiB default with no override needed), and `bun run screenshots` (the FULL matrix - every route, every viewport including `far`/TV and `far`/dark, both themes, plus the chat re-visit's keyboard-focus-pinning and composer/nav-overlap checks, reduced-motion, and keyboard-trap checks - not just the fast `--a11y-only` two-combo pass) all pass clean. `docs/assets/screens/{home,chat}-{desktop,phone}-{light,dark}.png` opened and judged against "one product, every screen": same content, same order, same header actions (search, pin, bell, profile) in the same position, the sidebar rail becoming a bottom tab bar and the desktop grid becoming a single column - never a second design.

## Home adopts the kit's own tokens (step 5a, ui-v0.1.4 through 0.1.6, 2026-09-20)

Step 5's own `tokens.css` (above) still defined Home's ENTIRE palette by hand - a neutral gray scale, its own radii and breakpoints, all independently maintained beside `@maipai/ui`'s real one. The kit's approved palette (`shared/ui/src/tokens.css`: a navy dark theme, the reference and default, with seven luminous accents and a derived light theme, per `shared/docs/plans/ui-spec-2026-09-19/spec.md`) never actually reached Home - docs/UI.md counts tokens as part of the kit, and the owner asked directly whether Home had the new colors, fonts and layouts yet. It hadn't.

Fixed by making Home's `tokens.css` a real overlay instead of a second definition: `frontend/src/kit/tokens.css` is deleted; the new `frontend/src/shell/tokens.css` opens with `@import "@maipai/ui/src/tokens.css";` (the kit's full palette, surfaces, radii, type scale and pill shape, both themes) and then overrides only what actually carries Home's own product identity - `--primary` and its four derived tokens (cyan, not the kit's electric blue, per `brand/README.md`'s per-product accent table) and `--destructive` (Home's own audited value, not the kit's single cross-theme red - see below). Everything else - canvas, sidebar, panel, raised panel, border, text tiers, type scale, radii, pills, the violet/teal/orange/pink category hues nav-main.tsx's active-item styling already referenced - is the kit's, unedited, both themes. `components.json`, `eslint.config.js`'s `better-tailwindcss` entry point, and every stale `kit/tokens.css` comment (`eslint.config.js`, `chatDayDivider.tsx`) were repointed to match.

**Three real regressions, found by actually switching the import**, all fixed properly rather than reverted:

- **Home's own `--primary` no longer cleared AA against the kit's own light surfaces.** The pre-adoption 29%-lightness cyan was tuned years ago against Home's own pure-white `--sidebar`/`--background`; the kit's approved light theme's `--sidebar` (`#eaf0f7`) and `--muted` (`#e3eaf3`) are a faint blue-gray, not pure white, and the Brand link's "Home" text (`text-primary` on `--sidebar`) measured only 4.34:1 - under WCAG AA's 4.5:1 floor. Darkened to 26%, which clears every surface it renders on today with real margin (`--sidebar` 5.16:1, `--muted` 4.89:1, `--background` 5.51:1, white 5.92:1), not just the one surface that happened to fail first.
- **The kit's own `--destructive` (`#ff4b62`, one value for both themes) failed the kit's own default Button/Badge "destructive" treatment** (solid background, white text) in both themes once it actually applied: 3.26:1 in light (against white text), and the existing dark-mode tint override (moved here from step 5's `tokens.css`, unchanged) measured only 4.11:1 for a real seeded Repairs issue on phone once the kit's own red replaced Home's pre-adoption lightened value. Home keeps its own two already-audited `--destructive` values instead of the kit's one - 38% (light, solid-white-text use) and, lightened further to 72% (dark, text-over-tint use, up from the pre-adoption 65% once measured against this specific badge's real composited background) - the same "kit provides structure, product provides color" split as `--primary`.
- **Two kit-level opacity bugs, fixed in `shared/ui` itself, not overridden in Home**: `nav-main.tsx`'s own call-site override of `sidebar.tsx`'s `SidebarGroupLabel` (`text-sidebar-foreground/60`, the one actually rendered on every page's "Navigation"/"Favorites" heading) measured 4.49:1 against the kit's own light `--sidebar`, under WCAG AA's 4.5:1 floor; and `tabs.tsx`'s inactive `TabsTrigger` (`text-foreground/60`) measured 4.42:1 against the kit's own light `--muted`. Both were opacity-reduced foreground colors that had simply never been checked against the KIT's real light palette before (Home's own, different neutral scale had happened to still pass). Fixed at the source: the sidebar label's call site bumped to `/75`, along with the primitive's own `/70` default (defensively - it was never proven to fail on its own, since nothing renders it un-overridden today), and the tabs trigger switched from an opacity blend to the kit's own already-audited `--muted-foreground` token (5.4:1), matching what its dark-mode variant already did - one rule for both themes instead of two. `shared/ui`'s own `contrast.test.ts` gained a real regression test for this bug class (opacity-blended text, which its existing solid-color checks never evaluated). Landed as `ui-v0.1.4`.

**A `bun install` gotcha, found diagnosing why the `ui-v0.1.4` fixes didn't show up in a re-run**: `@maipai/ui`'s `file:` dependency is resolved into a content-addressed store (`node_modules/.bun/@maipai+ui@file+...`), a snapshot taken at install time, not a live link to `shared/ui/src` - editing `shared/ui`'s source after installing does not reach Home's build until a real reinstall. Plain `bun install` didn't refresh it (the lockfile entry hadn't changed); `bun install --force` did. Worth remembering for any `shared`-in-parallel workflow, not just this one: a `shared/ui` edit needs a forced reinstall in every consumer to actually take effect.

**Two more shared/ui tags landed while pinning, unrelated to tokens but pinned along the way**: COORDINATOR handed off two token-free-lane items ready on a `shared-c` worktree, cherry-picked onto `shared` `main` as `ui-v0.1.5` - a `hitArea(1|2|3)` helper collapsing three hand-derived touch-target implementations into one, and the kit's own ESLint config (`jsx-a11y`, `better-tailwindcss`, lucide/radix-only enforcement), closing a `docs/BACKLOG.md` gap open since `ui-v0.1.0`. Re-pinning Home to `0.1.5` found a real break the lane's own commit shipped with, invisible from inside `shared`'s own gate: a `package.json` `"exports"` field added for the ESLint config's `"./eslint-config"` alias put every OTHER subpath (`@maipai/ui/src/*`, which Home's entire adoption depends on) out of resolution the moment it installed externally - `bun test` failed on "Cannot find module" across nearly the whole suite. Fixed in `shared` as `ui-v0.1.6` (dropped `exports` entirely; the config is importable at its real file path instead, `@maipai/ui/eslint.config.js`). **Home pins `ui-v0.1.6`**, not `0.1.4` or `0.1.5`.

**Verification**: `shared`'s own `scripts/check.sh` green (126 `core` + 296 `ui` = 422 tests, including `contrast.test.ts`'s new opacity-blend regression test and `hitArea.test.tsx`'s four) at `ui-v0.1.6`. Home's full `scripts/check.sh` green with `UI_PIN=0.1.6` (`bun install --force` to refresh the content-addressed snapshot each time the pin moved). Home's full `bun run a11y` (34 pages) and then the full `bun run screenshots` (136 pages) both pass clean with zero violations. `docs/assets/screens/home-{desktop,phone}-{light,dark}.png`, `chat-desktop-dark.png`, and `settings-repairs-desktop-{light,dark}.png` opened and judged: the navy dark reference theme, cyan brand accent, and the kit's own violet active-nav-item treatment (`nav-main.tsx`'s `data-[active=true]:bg-[var(--hue-violet)]`, invisible before this since `--hue-violet` was never defined) all render correctly in both themes, phone and desktop read as the same design, and the destructive Repairs badge reads as a quiet tint in dark and a solid fill in light rather than illegible in either.

## Home rebuilds chat on the kit's own chat pattern (step 5b, ui-v0.2.0 through 0.2.2, 2026-09-20)

Step 5's adoption (above) and step 5a's tokens fixed the shell around chat; chat itself still ran on Home's own pre-adoption, hand-built pieces (its own `SensesDock`, `WakeWordToggle`, `chatSourcesCard`, `ChatModelPicker`, a unified "Chat status" pill) never brought under the kit's structure/behavior boundary. COORDINATOR wrote the pattern into `shared/ui/docs/spec.md` as a new "Chat" section (landed verbatim from her scratchpad, `ui/docs/spec.md`'s own comment marks the source) plus a "One product on every screen" opening paragraph for section 7, and handed off four new kit components to build from the section's own paragraphs - the senses dock, the child band, the sources card, the memory chip - with the existing `home/frontend/src/kit/assistant-ui/*` wrappers moving into `shared/ui/src/assistant-ui/*` unchanged except their own imports. The standing bar: every existing chat behavior kept, verified against the section's own five-state acceptance screenshot set.

### shared/ui: the four components, the moved wrappers, three patch tags

`ui/src/blocks/chat/SensesDock.tsx` (new): a `SenseItem[]` prop (`kind`: listening/speaking/vision, `state`: active/idle/refused) rendered as the kit's real `Tooltip`/`TooltipTrigger`/`TooltipContent` per sense (a `title` attribute was the first pass; a review caught it before landing), a state-to-color map onto `--hue-teal`/`text-muted-foreground`/`--hue-red`, and the wake word as a real kit `Switch`. `ChildBand.tsx` (new): a `role="status"` panel-colored band, eye icon, "`{personName}` is chatting. A parent can see this chat." - no dismiss, by design (spec: "always on for a child, never dismissable, part of the safety architecture"). `SourcesCard.tsx` (new): a kit `Collapsible`, "Sources (N)" collapsed by default, each row `data-slot="chat-source-row"` `data-source-id` for the citation-click highlight below, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` plus explicit `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"` (a review caught the port only carrying `rel="noreferrer"`, dropping a real attribute Home's own pre-adoption copy had - fixed in `ui-v0.2.1`). `MemoryChip.tsx` (new): three kinds now (`remembered`/`recalled`/`failed`, the third added in `0.2.1` once Home's own adapter needed it) - "remembered"/"recalled" open a violet popover (Keep/Edit/Forget, auto-closing on any action); "failed" is a plain destructive-tinted button straight to `onOpenMemory`, no popover.

The eleven `assistant-ui/` wrapper files (plus their two `hooks/`) moved into `shared/ui/src/assistant-ui/`, self-references repointed `@maipai/ui/src/*` → `@/kit/*`, otherwise unchanged. `thread.aui.tsx` deliberately did not move - fourteen imports specific to Home's own `apps/chat/` (citation, memory, engine-health, day-boundary code below), the one file this step's own scope allowed real edits to. A new `eslint.config.js` override (`files: ["src/assistant-ui/**/*.tsx"]`, positioned last in the array for ESLint flat-config's own later-wins ordering) turns off the same vendored-code rules Home's own pre-adoption exemption already carried for the same directory.

**A real, previously-invisible a11y regression, found by the matrix, not guessed at.** `bun run a11y`'s two-combo pass had never once run `chat @ desktop` with the thread list actually, permanently visible (before this step it was a toggled drawer, closed by default) - once the persistent 280px column became part of the page's own DOM, the sweep hit `thread-list.aui.tsx` call-site `className` overrides that had silently been defeating the primitive's own touch-target and type floors since it was written: `ThreadListSearch`/rename `Input` losing `Input`'s own `h-12`/`text-base` to an `h-8 text-sm` override; `ThreadListItemPrimitive.Root`/`.Trigger` at `h-8`/`text-sm`; the "More options" trigger hand-set to `size-6` instead of the kit's own `size="icon-xs"`; the loading skeleton row and the "No chats found" empty state at the same undersized scale. Fixed at the source component, all as call-site overrides removed or corrected (no new behavior) - landed as `ui-v0.2.2`. A code review on that tag caught two more before it shipped: `icon-xs`'s own `hitArea(3)` extension reaches 42px from the row's trailing edge, past the row's existing `pe-9` (36px) reserved padding - bumped to `pe-11` (44px) on both the trigger and the rename `Input`; and the Delete menu item's hand-copied `DropdownMenuItem` class list was missing the dark-mode destructive contrast bump (`dark:hover:bg-destructive/20 dark:focus:bg-destructive/20`) `dropdown-menu.tsx`'s own primitive already carries - added, and the class-list duplication itself filed in `shared/docs/BACKLOG.md` (not fixed here - an architectural note, not a bug).

`ui/src/icons.ts` gained `camera` (SensesDock's vision icon). `ui/src/ui/textarea.tsx` moved from Home's own `kit/ui/textarea.tsx`, unchanged. `package.json` picked up `@assistant-ui/react`, `@assistant-ui/react-markdown`, `remark-gfm` as new direct dependencies the moved wrappers need, and `zustand` promoted from transitive to direct (a review finding: it was already relied on, just never declared). Tags: `0.1.6` → `0.2.0` (spec + four components + moved wrappers) → `0.2.1` (SourcesCard `referrerPolicy`, MemoryChip `"failed"`) → `0.2.2` (the touch-target/type-floor sweep above). `docs/BACKLOG.md`, `docs/dev.md` and `ui/CHANGELOG.md` updated per tag.

### Home: the rebuild, every behavior kept

`ChatPage.tsx` restructured around the new regions: desktop's thread list is a persistent `<aside>` (never toggled); phone's is a real kit `Sheet` (`id="chat-threads"`), opened by a header toggle whose accessible name flips "Show threads"/"Hide threads" with `threadsOpen` state; `SensesDock` replaces the old hand-built one, its `senses` array computed inline from the existing `wakeWord`/`speechError`/`isSpeaking` state (no new state, same signals); `ChildBand` renders when `person.role === "child"`; the whole page wrapped in its own `TooltipProvider` (the real app inherits one from `Shell.tsx`'s `SidebarProvider`, but `ChatPage.test.tsx` renders the page standalone, and `SensesDock`'s new `Tooltip` usage threw `Tooltip must be used within TooltipProvider` without it - broke 17 tests at once, fixed by the wrapper, safe to nest two). `useWakeWord.ts` (new) extracts the old `WakeWordToggle.tsx`'s mic-capture logic (the `requestIdRef` race guard, unmount cleanup) unchanged into a plain hook; `useWakeWord.test.ts` covers the same three scenarios via `renderHook`. `useChatDisclosure.ts` (new) centralizes the `ui.show_turn_stats` person-scoped setting plus the owner/admin/adult role gate - shared by `ChatPage.tsx` (read+write) and the new `ModelPicker.tsx` (read-only).

**The model picker, and a real design ruling.** Spec: "not a chat control... lives in the header picker slot... shows the companion's current model only at the Developer disclosure level." `ModelPicker.tsx` (new) is route-gated (`/chat` only) and disclosure-gated, rendered from `AppShell.tsx`'s own `headerActions` (no dedicated Shell slot exists for a page-specific header control; the doc comment there now says why). Escalated as a genuine question, not guessed: does "Developer disclosure level" mean literally no model name or switch below that level, or a read-only display at a lower tier? COORDINATOR's ruling: the strict read is the intended one - "a person chats with a companion, not a model... a parent who wants to change the engine does it where the engine is configured" (Settings). `ModelPicker.test.tsx` covers all five cases (off-route, child, owner-without-disclosure, owner-with-disclosure showing and switching, the unavailable/repair-action case).

**The citation redesign.** Spec: "Citations in the body are superscript numbers that scroll the card open and highlight the row" - previously a direct link to the source URL. `chatCitationLink.tsx`'s `createCitationComponents` gained an `onCite(sourceId)` callback; the `[N]` marker now renders the kit's `Button variant="secondary" size="icon-xs"` (a real touch target it never had as a raw link) instead of an `<a>` - `no-restricted-syntax`'s "no raw button in src/apps" rule caught the first pass at a plain `<button>`, routed through the kit `Button` instead, which was the more correct fix anyway. `thread.aui.tsx` gained `contentRef`, `sourcesOpen`/`highlightedSourceId` state, and `handleCite` (opens the card, scrolls to and briefly highlights the matching `data-source-id` row); `sourceItems` is `sources` mapped to the kit's `SourceItem` shape via `useMemo`, order preserved for citation numbering. `chatMemoryChip.tsx` rewritten as a thin adapter over the kit's `MemoryChip` (`chatMemoryState.ts`'s store is unchanged) - "saved" → `kind="remembered"`, "failed" → `kind="failed"`; `chatMemoryChip.test.tsx` rewritten to match (the chip is a button now, not a link - `openPopover` helper, `data-slot="chat-memory-chip"` for the null-state checks).

**The engine-health split, by design.** The old unified "Chat status" pill is gone; spec's "Empty, loading, error" section implies three separate signals, not one, and COORDINATOR's own ruling ("every behavior kept") required checking nothing was lost in the split rather than just deleted. Three design-resolver calls confirmed the shape: composer readiness (disabled with the health reason as its own placeholder, plus an "Open AI models" fix button - `ChatPage.test.tsx`'s own test asserts both the exact placeholder text and the link's `href`), a per-turn error recovery row (`MessageError` extended with a "Try again" `ActionBarPrimitive.Reload` and a conditional "Open AI models" link, gated on `ChatBrainBadContext`), and a per-turn slow-reply indicator (a 45s `setTimeout` keyed on `running`, folded into the existing streaming indicator's text - "Still working. This is taking longer than usual.", no new UI surface).

**Two more `ChatPage.test.tsx` rewrites**, both real behavior changes rather than drift: the old "composer disabled while starting" test checked for the deleted status pill, rewritten to check the placeholder text and the fix link. The "thread history opens and closes" test assumed the toggle button stays queryable while the sheet is open; Radix marks sibling DOM `aria-hidden` while a modal is open, and the header's own toggle - outside the Sheet's portal - is exactly such a sibling. Rewritten to close via the Sheet's own visible "Close" button instead (the same fix `scripts/screenshot.ts` needed later, below).

`frontend/eslint.config.js`'s vendored-code exemption re-pointed from the now-deleted `src/kit/ui/**`/`src/kit/assistant-ui/**` to the one file that still needs it, `src/apps/chat/thread.aui.tsx`, and moved to the end of the config array - an ESLint flat-config ordering bug (an earlier exemption block silently losing to a later general rule-setting block for the same file) the same shape as `shared/ui`'s own fix above. `scripts/check.sh`'s `UI_PIN` moved `0.1.6` → `0.2.2` across the tags. Deleted: `src/kit/assistant-ui/` (whole directory), `src/kit/ui/textarea.tsx`, and Home's own pre-adoption `chatSourcesCard.tsx`, `ChatModelPicker.tsx`, `WakeWordToggle.tsx` (plus their tests) - superseded by the kit versions above.

### A real product bug, found by the acceptance screenshots themselves, not guessed at

The five-state screenshot set (below) is generated by `scripts/screenshot.ts`'s `exerciseChat()`, which had run clean at every earlier gate in this step - until the new desktop-persistent/phone-sheet split it was never written for surfaced four real bugs, three in the test script and one in the product:

1. **The delete-confirmation dialog-hidden wait was ambiguous.** `page.getByRole("dialog").waitFor({ state: "hidden" })`, unscoped, now also matches the new phone `Sheet` (also `role="dialog"`) - the confirm dialog closes on delete, the outer sheet correctly stays open, and the unscoped wait hung on the wrong one forever. Scoped to the dialog's own name: `page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Delete chat" })`.
2. **Closing the phone sheet via the header's own toggle timed out.** The same Radix `aria-hidden`-on-siblings behavior `ChatPage.test.tsx`'s rewrite above already hit: the toggle lives outside the Sheet's portal, so it becomes unqueryable the moment the sheet opens. Switched to the Sheet's own built-in "Close" button (`sheet.tsx`'s `sr-only` "Close" span), the one control still reachable while the sheet is open.
3. **A real product bug: two "New chat" affordances collided on desktop.** `ChatPage.tsx`'s own header shortcut (`ThreadListNew aria-label="New chat"`, icon-only, predates this step - it existed before the kit swap too) and the thread list column's own "New chat" (spec: "the one primary action, pinned at the top of the column") are both always visible once the column became persistent - `getByRole("button", { name: "New chat", exact: true })` hit a strict-mode violation, two matches. The header shortcut only ever made sense while the list was hidden (a phone-only sheet toggle away); made it `lg:hidden` to match, same breakpoint and same reasoning as the squeeze fix below.
4. **A real product bug: the persistent column's own breakpoint squeezed the composer at tablet width.** The column and its toggle used Tailwind's default `sm:` (640px) - tablet (820px) already qualified as "desktop" there, crowding the shell's own rail, the 280px column, and the thread/composer into too little remaining width; the composer's textarea measured 8px tall in the touch-target-floor check, a genuinely broken layout, not a false positive. `SettingsPage.tsx` had already hit and fixed this exact class of bug (the BACKLOG item above, `--breakpoint-lg` still 1024px in `tokens.css` for exactly this reason) - switched every `sm:` in `ChatPage.tsx`'s thread-list markup to `lg:`, matching that established convention instead of reinventing a second one.

None of the four were guessed at from reading the code; each surfaced only once the real matrix ran against the real rebuilt page, exactly the reason the acceptance criteria requires opening the screenshots rather than trusting the gate alone.

### The five-state acceptance screenshot set

Three of the five states had no existing dedicated capture (only "empty thread" and "thread list open on phone" were already produced by the plain matrix and `exerciseChat()` respectively) - three new functions added to `scripts/screenshot.ts` behind a new `--chat-acceptance-review` flag, each looping the site's own two-combo convention (phone/dark, desktop/light):

- `captureChatSourcesMemoryAttachment`: a loaded conversation (not a live turn - `deriveMemoryStatus()` only reaches "saved" from a non-empty `memory_ids`, which a live `/api/turn/stream` event never carries, the judge runs after the turn). Found live: stubbing only the plural `GET /api/conversations/:id/turns` timed out - `useRemoteThreadListRuntime`'s own adapter calls the singular `GET /api/conversations/:id` first to resolve a `threadId` it doesn't already know, and a real 404 there made it silently fall back to a fresh empty thread instead of erroring. Both stubbed, fixed. The fake image attachment's `url` first pointed at a nonexistent `https://example.com/...jpg` and rendered as a broken-image icon - replaced with a `thumbnail` as an embedded `data:image/png;base64,...` (a tiny generated PNG), no live network dependency, matching the org's "deterministic and offline by default" testing standard; `url` itself stays a realistic-looking address since it is only ever used for the row's "open in a new tab" href, never the rendered `<img src>`.
- `captureChatStreaming`: `route.fulfill()` delivers its whole body at once, near-instantly on localhost - too fast to reliably catch the app mid-stream. Overrode `window.fetch` in the page instead (`addInitScript`, before the app's own first fetch), returning a real `ReadableStream` whose one chunk is enqueued and deliberately never closed - the app has no way to tell this apart from a slow real reply still arriving, so the streaming state (and caret) holds for as long as the page lives.
- `captureChatEngineNotReady`: the same `/api/health` → `{ brain: "starting" }` shape `ChatPage.test.tsx`'s own composer-disabled test uses.

**Opened and judged against `shared/ui/docs/spec.md`'s Chat section**, both viewports, both themes (light shown here; dark checked the same way): empty thread shows the composer grouped under the greeting, no suggestion chips populated (see the BACKLOG gap below); sources-card-open + memory-chip + image-attachment shows all three together on one reply, the citation `[1]` chip, "Sources (1)" expanded to the row, "Remembered" chip, and a real rendered thumbnail; streaming shows partial reply text with a caret and the composer's stop control; engine-not-ready shows the disabled composer, the health reason as its placeholder, and the "Open AI models" fix button, the thread staying visible underneath (never a blank page, never a toast); thread-list-open-on-phone shows the sheet over the dimmed thread. **Two gaps found, not fixed here** (pre-existing in `thread.aui.tsx`, which this step's own scope moved "unchanged except imports" outside the sources/citation wiring it was explicitly assigned): the empty state has no companion avatar, name, or capability line, and no populated suggestion chips (the wiring to assistant-ui's own `ThreadPrimitive.Suggestions` exists; nothing feeds it data); message turns have no avatar or name; the streaming caret renders in the foreground color, not spec's "2px teal." Filed as one `docs/BACKLOG.md` item under "UI / shell" rather than expanded into here - a design pass on the avatar asset and capability copy is needed first, and it was not part of the four components this step was scoped to.

### Verification

`shared`'s own `scripts/check.sh` green at `ui-v0.2.2`. Home's full `scripts/check.sh` green (`UI_PIN=0.2.2`, `bun install --force` after every `shared/ui` edit to refresh the content-addressed snapshot - hit repeatedly across this step, same gotcha as step 5a). `bun run screenshots` (full matrix, 136 pages) clean, zero violations, zero overflow, after the tablet-squeeze fix above - the first three runs of this step each caught one of the four bugs listed, in order. `bun run scripts/screenshot.ts --chat-acceptance-review` produced and the section above judges the five-state set. Code review run on the full diff before commit; findings folded in above rather than listed twice.

## Home pins `@maipai/spec`, the `spec/` workspace removed (spec-v0.1.1, refocus step 6, 2026-09-20)

`home/spec` moved whole to `shared/spec` (Session B, `shared/docs/dev.md`'s own "Workspace status" entry has the move's full detail, including RF-05b folding the Stack's wire shapes into the same tag). This entry is the Home-side half: pinning the result and removing the local copy.

**Nearly free, because most call sites already used the package form.** `backend/package.json` and `frontend/package.json` had `"@maipai/spec": "workspace:*"` (a Bun workspace member pointing at the local `spec/` via a symlink) and 64 of 65 spec-reading files already imported it as `@maipai/spec/gen/ts/...`/`@maipai/spec/voice/ts/...` etc. - the package-subpath form, not a relative path. Swapping the dependency to `"@maipai/spec": "file:../../shared/spec"` (`bun install --force` in both `backend/` and `frontend/`, the standard content-addressed-store gotcha) and dropping `"spec"` from `home/package.json`'s `workspaces` array made every one of those 64 resolve unchanged - `file:` copies the whole workspace into `node_modules/@maipai/spec` as a real, self-contained directory, exactly `core`'s and `ui`'s own precedent.

**Two relative-path holdouts, fixed to match the other 64:** `backend/src/lib/childDisclosure.ts`'s `import lifeEvents from "../../../spec/vocab/life-events.json"` → `"@maipai/spec/vocab/life-events.json"`; `scripts/screenshot.ts`'s `import { startStubLlmServer } from "../spec/llm/ts/stubServer"` couldn't take the same fix (a repo-root script, not a workspace member, has no `@maipai/spec` installed for it to resolve) - repointed at the sibling checkout directly, `"../../shared/spec/llm/ts/stubServer"`.

**`backend/src/lib/settingsRegistry.ts`'s runtime read needed a different fix than either of those**: it reads `spec/settings/keys.json` at boot with `readFileSync`, not a static import, so `@maipai/spec/settings/keys.json` as a bare specifier wasn't an option the same way. Resolves the installed package's real directory instead (`Bun.resolveSync("@maipai/spec/package.json", import.meta.dir)`, then `settings/keys.json` under it) - correct through a `file:` copy or any future resolution strategy, never assumes a fixed relative depth.

**`backend/scripts/gen-settings-registry.ts` (the writer) has the opposite problem**: it must write the *source*, not the installed snapshot (`node_modules/@maipai/spec` is gitignored, regenerated by `bun install`, and not what anyone commits). Repointed to write `../../../shared/spec/settings/keys.json` (`MAIPAI_SHARED_DIR`-overridable, matching `scripts/check.sh`'s existing convention) - the sibling checkout directly, same as the drift check below.

**`scripts/check.sh` restructured**, per COORDINATOR's own read of the split (confirmed before landing): the two `[ -d spec/schemas ]`-gated blocks that used to live here - the standards `gen/ts`/`gen/py` presence check, and the regenerate-and-diff drift check against `spec/schemas/` - both moved to `shared/scripts/check.sh` outright, since they're entirely about `@maipai/spec`'s own internal consistency and `spec/schemas/` no longer exists in this repo at all. The settings-registry drift check (`bun run gen:settings` in `backend/`, diff the result) stayed here, because it reads *this repo's own* `backend/src/settings/*.ts` declarations - but it now diffs the external file (`git -C "$SHARED_DIR" diff --quiet -- spec/settings/keys.json`) instead of a local path, and reports the fix as a commit in `getmaipai/shared`, not here. Gained a fourth pin check (`SPEC_PIN`), matching the existing `CORE_PIN`/`UI_PIN` pattern exactly: `$SHARED_DIR/spec/package.json`'s version must equal the pin (`0.1.1` - shared corrected two stale `home/spec` references and a codegen regression the same day, see `shared/docs/dev.md`'s `spec-v0.1.1` entry) or the gate refuses to run.

**One test left in `home/spec/tests/ts/` by the move, moved here on purpose, not by accident:** `package-bronze.test.ts` (the bronze-completeness check against `docs/PACKAGES.md`, reading `backend/packages/` to prove every bundled package clears the bar) reads a directory that only exists in this repo - a product-agnostic library workspace structurally can't carry it. Moved to `backend/tests/package-bronze.test.ts` unchanged apart from its two imports (now `@maipai/spec/...`, matching every other backend import) and `PACKAGES_DIR` (now `../packages`, a sibling of `backend/tests/` instead of three levels up from `spec/tests/ts/`).

**`AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore`, `scripts/check.sh`'s own header comment** updated to say `spec/` lives in `getmaipai/shared` now, not here, plus a "Pinning `getmaipai/shared`" paragraph in `AGENTS.md` mirroring the one that already existed implicitly for `core`/`ui`. `spec/schemas.resolved/` dropped from `.gitignore` (nothing here generates it anymore).

**Verification**: Home's full `scripts/check.sh` green with the `SPEC_PIN` check passing against `shared/spec` at `spec-v0.1.1` (bumped from `0.1.0` the same day - `shared`'s own correction commit), `bun install --force` in `backend/` and `frontend/` after the pin swap. `git grep` for any remaining `(\.\./)+spec/` relative import across `backend/`, `frontend/`, `scripts/` came back empty after the two fixes above - nothing else was silently pointing at the now-deleted local `spec/`.

## Home's shell and dashboard under the kit (HOME-UI-01, ui-v0.3.0, 2026-09-20)

The owner's ruling on "Home's pages under the kit"
([docs/design/home-pages-2026-09-20.md](design/home-pages-2026-09-20.md),
landed verbatim from COORDINATOR's scratchpad): Home follows the Stack
console spec's look and feel exactly (the shell, the colors, the icon
tiles, the panel headers, the header, the footer, the type, the
density, the spacing), never its content - Home's own navigation,
routes, records and actions fill the same patterns. This step covers
the rail, the header, the footer, and the dashboard (`/`); every other
page keeps its own content, restyled only where the shell wraps it.

### `shared/ui`: five new components, a `Shell` footer slot, `ui-v0.3.0`

`IconTile` (the one icon tile every card, row, nav group heading and
panel header now draws through: 18% fill, 35% border, a soft glow, two
sizes), `PanelHeader` (a panel's header row: the icon tile, the title,
a right-aligned "View all"/"Browse all" link with an arrow, a hairline
underneath - `linkAriaLabel` lets two panels on one page share the
same visible label with distinct accessible names, since Home's
Recent-memories and People panels both say "View all"), `HubCard` (the
rail's bottom hub card, collapsing to its status dot alone when the
rail collapses), `FooterBar` (the fixed 40px status bar), and
`HeaderSearchField` (the header's real search field - a raised-panel
input, the search icon, the ⌘K pill, icon-only under `sm`, replacing
the kit's old bare icon-button trigger). `Shell` gained a `footer`
slot and its header now renders three real flex regions (title,
centered search, actions) instead of title-then-everything-else.
`MetricCard`/`CategoryTile`/`ActionTile` restyled onto `IconTile`;
`nav-main`'s active item is the violet-to-`--hue-violet-deep` gradient
the spec calls for, not a flat fill. Two review passes (medium, then
the fix hunks) - the full account, including two of the fixer's own
mistakes the second pass caught and the reasoning for each, is in
`shared`'s own `docs/BACKLOG.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` at `ui-v0.3.0`,
verbatim rather than duplicated here.

### Home: the rail, the header, the footer

`AppShell.tsx` rebuilt: `Brand` wraps the existing logo images in the
spec's gradient tile (blue to violet, a soft glow) with the tagline
"Your AI. On your terms." underneath; nav groups are **Home** (Home,
Chat, Conversations, Apps), **Household** (People, Memories), **System**
(Settings, Privacy) - **Manage is omitted**, since Home has no
Engines/Packages/Updates/Repairs/Backups destinations of its own yet
(Repairs and Health stay Settings sections, `RepairsPage`/
`HealthSection`, reached at `/settings/repairs` and `/settings/health`,
until HOME-STACK-04 gives them real top-level pages); Conversations
sits under Home, next to Chat, since the ruling's own Household list
(People, Memories, Lists) has no chat-history entry and this is chat's
own history. `NAV_ENTRIES`'s "Memory" label became "Memories" (the
ruling's own wording) - found live: `appCatalog.ts`'s search keywords
didn't include the word "memory" itself once the label no longer did,
so typing "memory" in search stopped finding the Memories app;
`"memory"` added back as an explicit keyword.

The rail's old footer nav row (Privacy, Settings) is gone - those now
live in the System group - freeing the `sidebarFooter` slot for a new
`HubStatusCard` (real data: `api.hardware()` for the machine's name/OS,
`api.repairs()` for the open-repair count and status color, tapping
opens `/settings/repairs`). A new `HomeFooterBar` reads the same
`useHubStatus()` hook (one hook, one cache entry per read, shared with
the dashboard's own metric row) for the fixed footer's version/engines-
running/repairs-open/updates segments. The header's title and subtitle
are now genuinely destination-owned (`shell/routeHeader.ts`, a small
route-to-{title,subtitle} table matched the same way the rail
highlights its active item) - the Home route's subtitle is the
existing `greetingFor()` helper plus the ruling's own sentence ("Good
afternoon, Sage. Here is your household today."). A `ThemeToggle`
(new, Home's own, not the kit's `AppearanceControl`: that component
assumes a `next-themes` `ThemeProvider` neither the kit's `Shell` nor
Home mounts, and Home already has its own real appearance system,
`useAppearance.ts` - "the kit gets a slot, Home keeps the feature," the
same reason `PinToggle`/`ModelPicker`/`NotificationBell`/
`ProfileSwitcher` are Home's own) fills the header's sun/moon slot,
found missing only once the header was actually screenshotted: the
kit's own `AppearanceControl` exists but was never wired anywhere in
this codebase, and would have rendered inert without a provider it has
no reason to gain just for this.

**A real, previously-invisible duplicate-header bug, found by the
screenshots, not guessed at.** The header rule ("no duplicate page
title/subtitle beneath the fixed header") only ever mattered once a
fixed header existed to duplicate against - six pages (`PrivacyPage`,
`MemoryPage`, `ConversationsPage`, `SearchPage`, `PeoplePage`,
`NotificationsPage`) still rendered their own visible `<Page title>`
h1 (three others, `SettingsPage`/`ChatPage`/`AppsPage`, already had
`hideTitle` from the kit-adoption step); all six switched to
`hideTitle` (the h1 stays `sr-only`, so nothing about the page's own
accessible heading changed). `routeHeader.ts` also covers `/search`
and `/notifications`, two real routes outside the rail's own nav
entries, so their fixed header never falls back to the generic
"MaiPai Home" title. One page had a SECOND, separate duplication the
`hideTitle` sweep didn't touch: `SettingsPage.tsx` renders its own
literal `<h2>Settings</h2>` plus a tab-specific subtitle, independent
of `Page`'s own (already-hidden) title - found live in the desktop
screenshot, the fixed header and this h2 both saying "Settings" a few
lines apart. Fixed by renaming the h2 to what it actually names (the
tab switcher's own selection, "Household" or "Me"), keeping the
tab-specific subtitle - the header rule's own allowed exception ("a
local section heading... names a distinct working area").

### Home: the dashboard (`/`)

`HomePage.tsx` rewritten to the section's own composition, replacing
the old ask-box-plus-cards layout the acceptance criteria names
explicitly as what must not survive ("a page that looks like the old
Home page with new colors fails"):

1. **Metric row** (`MetricRow`): Chat and Voice read `useHubStatus()`'s
   `health.brain`/`health.voice` (the same engine-kind strings
   `useEngineHealth()` polls for Chat's own composer gate, reused from
   one shared `/api/health` read rather than a second poller) through a
   small `engineStateText()` mapping (Ready/Starting/Stopped/Not set
   up/Checking). Updates and Repairs are real, not placeholders - see
   below.
2. **Panel row**: `TodayPanel` (the existing weather-turn logic, now
   with the real date under it) and `RecentMemoriesPanel` (the last
   five, by `created_at`, "View all" to `/memory`).
3. **Your apps** (`YourAppsPanel`): the existing pinned-apps strip,
   restyled onto `IconTile`, `CardSizeSlider` hidden on the phone
   (found live: the slider and "Browse all" were squeezing the panel
   title into a truncated sliver in the row's shared space at 390px -
   a density control has little to control once the grid is already
   one or two columns there anyway).
4. **Household row**: `PeoplePanel` (the same avatar-strip pattern the
   old page's `WhoIsHere` had, no presence - unchanged, still honest
   about not knowing who's actually home), `ActivityPanel` (Home has no
   activity/audit log yet, so this merges two already-real feeds
   client-side - recent conversations and recent memories, by real
   timestamp, not a fabricated third source), `QuickActionsPanel` (Ask
   MaiPai → `/chat`, Add a person → `/settings/users` - `UsersSection`'s
   real "Add someone" form, Check for updates → a real
   `POST /api/updates/check` call gated to owner/admin with a toast
   result, Open Repairs → `/settings/repairs`).
5. The ask box (`HomeSearchPrompt`) is gone from the page body -
   asking now lives only in the header's search field and in Chat, per
   the section's own line 5.

**A real backend feature, found and wired, not skipped for lack of
one.** `backend/src/routes/updates.ts`/`lib/updates.ts` (the app's own
cached GitHub-release check, `GET /api/updates` and
`POST /api/updates/check`, scoped to the app only - no package/model
update system exists) had never been called from the frontend at all.
`api.ts` gained `updates()`/`checkForUpdate()` and a hand-typed
`UpdateProjection` (the real interface lives in `lib/updates.ts`,
which carries `@/db`-aliased imports frontend's tsconfig can't resolve
- the same reason `DeviceInfo`/`SessionInfo` are hand-typed a few lines
above it, not a new pattern). The Updates metric card, the footer's
"updates available" segment, and the Quick Actions "Check for updates"
tile are all real now, where the spec's own composition would
otherwise have forced a choice between a fabricated placeholder and
silently dropping a named card - `useHubStatus()`'s `updates` field and
`updateAvailable()` are the one shared read both the dashboard and the
footer use.
