## Pins moved to per-tag worktrees (SHARED-PIN-01, 2026-09-20)

Found live: `scripts/check.sh`'s pin check and every `file:` dependency
in `backend/package.json`/`frontend/package.json` read whatever tag the
sibling `getmaipai/shared` checkout happened to have checked out - one
mutable directory shared by every session on the machine. A session
gating Home at `ui-v0.2.4` ran `git checkout ui-v0.2.4` in `../shared`,
which silently detached every other consumer and session reading that
same directory underneath it. `getmaipai/shared`'s own
`scripts/ensure-tag.sh` (landed the same day, `shared/docs/dev.md`) is
the fix: it resolves a `<workspace> <tag>` pair to an immutable
`../shared-tags/<workspace>-<tag>` `git worktree`, created once and
reused after, refusing a tag `shared` doesn't have.

Adopted here: `backend/package.json` and `frontend/package.json`'s
`@maipai/core`/`@maipai/ui`/`@maipai/spec` `file:` paths now name a
worktree directly (e.g. `file:../../shared-tags/core-core-v0.1.0/
core`) instead of the shared sibling checkout; `scripts/check.sh` calls
`ensure-tag.sh` for each pin before `bun install` and checks the
resolved worktree's own `package.json` version against the tag (the
same honesty-of-the-pin contract as before, just reading a worktree
instead of the mutable checkout). `AGENTS.md`'s "Pinning" section
rewritten to match: bumping a pin is now two edits - the tag string in
`scripts/check.sh` and the matching `file:` path - then
`scripts/check.sh` (creates the new tag's worktree if needed) and
`bun install --force`.

`scripts/screenshot.ts`'s `import { startStubLlmServer } from
"../../shared/spec/llm/ts/stubServer"` got the same treatment,
COORDINATOR calling out that a script the release skill runs is a gate
in practice even though `check.sh` doesn't wire it in directly: that
fixed relative path read whatever `shared/` had checked out, the exact
bug this item exists to fix, and A lost an hour to it live the same
day. Resolved dynamically instead - `resolveSpecWorktreeDir()` reads
`backend/package.json`'s own `@maipai/spec` `file:` path (backend and
frontend pin the same tag, so either would do) and the actual
`import()` is a computed path built from it; only a `typeof import(...)`
type reference stays a fixed path, erased at compile time and never
read at runtime. `bun run a11y` (part of `check.sh`) exercises this
same code path on every gate run.

Also found along the way, not part of this item's own worktree
mechanism but the reason it was blocked at first: `ui-v0.3.1`,
`ui-v0.3.2` and `ui-v0.3.3` were never git-tagged in `shared` despite
their commit messages and this repo's own `UI_PIN` already naming
`0.3.3` - `ensure-tag.sh` correctly refused the unknown tag until
COORDINATOR had them cut (verified against each commit's own
`package.json` version and `CHANGELOG.md` entry first; hashes in
`shared`'s own dev doc).

**A medium-effort review of this diff found two real issues, both
before commit:**
1. The first version of the settings-registry drift check pointed
   `gen:settings`'s own `MAIPAI_SHARED_DIR` straight at the resolved
   `spec` worktree and let it write `spec/settings/keys.json` there -
   silently reintroducing SHARED-PIN-01 inside its own fix, since that
   worktree is a cache every consumer pinning `spec-v0.1.1` shares
   (`bot` included), not this repo's private scratch space. Fixed:
   the drift check now seeds a private `mktemp -d` scratch directory
   with the worktree's own committed `keys.json` (`git show
   HEAD:spec/settings/keys.json`, read-only), generates into the
   scratch copy, diffs the two, and removes the scratch directory
   after - the worktree's working tree is never written to. Verified
   live: `git status` inside `../shared-tags/spec-spec-v0.1.1` stayed
   clean through a full `scripts/check.sh` run.
2. `@maipai/ui`'s own `package.json` depends on `@maipai/spec` via a
   bare relative `file:../spec`, resolved from wherever `ui` itself is
   checked out. Before this item, `ui` and `spec` were always read
   from the same single mutable `shared/` checkout, so that nested
   dependency and this repo's own direct `@maipai/spec` pin were
   mechanically guaranteed to be the same commit. After this item,
   they resolve from two independently-pinned tags' worktrees, and
   nothing keeps them in sync going forward - a real duplicate-
   instance risk (two physically separate `@maipai/spec` copies is not
   new, `bun`'s `file:` dependencies already always copy rather than
   link; a version divergence between the two copies is new). Checked
   live: `ui-v0.3.3`'s own nested `spec/` and this repo's directly
   pinned `spec-v0.1.1` currently match byte-for-byte except one
   docs-only file, so there's no live break today. Not fixed here -
   the fix belongs in `shared`'s own tagging discipline (should `ui`
   pin an exact spec tag internally instead of a bare relative path?),
   not in a consumer's pin adoption - flagged to COORDINATOR as a
   `shared`-repo follow-up.

**Verification**: `scripts/check.sh` green end to end (backend install,
settings/API-docs drift checks including the scratch-dir `spec` diff,
backend and frontend test/lint/build, the `a11y` step exercising the
new dynamic stub-server import, standards core) with the new pin
resolution live - not just typechecked. The `spec` tag worktree
confirmed clean (`git status --short`) before and after the run.

## Two looks, one setting, and the collapsed rail fix (HOME-UI-02c, ui-v0.4.0/spec-v0.1.2, 2026-09-20)

The owner placed Home beside the reference and judged it "nice, not a
match" - his ruling, "Two looks, one setting"
([docs/design/home-pages-2026-09-20.md](design/home-pages-2026-09-20.md)):
keep what shipped as one look, **Calm**, and build a second, **Studio**,
that matches the reference exactly; a person picks the look in Settings
> Me > Appearance ("Look": Calm or Studio, per person, remembered), the
hub's own default is Studio. Both looks are the same components - the
difference is a theme, never a second component. Same day, a second
finding, "The collapsed rail" (both looks): the collapsed rail as
shipped had a second toggle inside it, an oversized circular product
mark, off-center icons, an active fill wider than the icon column, and
a hub card reduced to a lone dot.

### The mechanism: `data-look`, a `studio:` variant, look-scoped tokens

`shared/ui` (`ui-v0.4.0`): a `data-look` attribute on `<html>`, applied
the same way `.dark`/`.light` already are - `@custom-variant studio
(&:is([data-look="studio"] *))` in `tokens.css`, so any component can
write `studio:` prefixed classes; `--tile-radius` (999px/circle at the
zero-attribute default, matching what `IconTile` already rendered via
`--radius-xl`'s own emergent math - 12px rounded square under
`[data-look="studio"]`) and `--canvas-background` (the dashboard's own
page background, a flat color in Calm, the reference's subtle radial
wash in Studio) as look-scoped tokens independent of light/dark, so a
person's look and theme choices combine freely. `IconTile` and Home's
own product-mark tile draw their radius through the token instead of a
fixed `rounded-xl`. `ActionTile` and `MetricCard`'s label stopped
truncating (owner finding: "nothing inside a card ever truncates" -
found live as "Add a pers…"/"Open Repa…" on the dashboard's own quick
actions, a defect in both looks, fixed in both).

A handful of the rail's own look-conditional rules (the collapsed
active item's gradient-in-Studio/flat-in-Calm fill, the group label's
Studio-only 11px size, the expanded divider) ended up as plain
attribute-selector CSS against the kit's own stable `data-slot`/
`data-collapsible`/`data-active` attributes, not `studio:`/`group-
data-[collapsible=icon]:` Tailwind classes - two different, unrelated
causes, both worth recording since they cost real time:

1. Several classes appeared to compile to nothing mid-session
   (confirmed missing from the built `dist/assets/*.css`, present
   neighbors on the same class string). The actual cause: `shared` is
   a `file:` link, and `bun install --force` snapshots its source into
   bun's content-addressed store at install time - a consumer's build
   silently keeps building an *older* snapshot of `shared` until
   reinstalled, and several rounds of edits landed between installs.
   Fixed by reinstalling before trusting a build again.
2. A real one, caught by a code review: `sidebarMenuButtonVariants`
   merges its classes through `cn()` (tailwind-merge) at every call
   site, which collapses same-utility conflicts and does not reliably
   read `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:` as scoping `overflow-visible`
   away from the base `overflow-hidden` it would otherwise conflict
   with - the override was winning everywhere, not just when
   collapsed. Plain CSS never goes through that merge, so it was kept
   even once cause 1 stopped being a live risk.

### The collapsed rail fix

`RailToggle` deleted - the header's own `SidebarTrigger` is the rail's
one and only toggle now (it gained the deleted component's own
`aria-expanded`/state-aware label, caught missing by the same review).
`SIDEBAR_WIDTH_ICON` 72px → 64px. Every collapsed nav row a true 40x40
centered target (`size-10`, not the 48px `size-12` this used to force;
`justify-center` and a 20px icon, both `group-data-[collapsible=icon]`-
scoped so the expanded row is untouched) - `hitArea(1)` (the kit's own
touch-target helper, `button.tsx`/`toggle.tsx`/`HubCard.tsx`'s own
pattern, not a hand-copy of its three classes) still floors the real
tappable region at 48px, `overflow: visible` (see cause 2 above)
making that extension actually hit-testable rather than clipped by the
row's own `overflow-hidden`. The active item's collapsed fill: a flat
`background-color` under everything, a Studio-only gradient
`background-image` layered over it - two different CSS properties, so
Studio's gradient always paints over Calm's flat color with nothing to
override. `HubCard`'s collapsed state: a 40px tile with the hub icon
and the status dot at its corner (the same `right-0 bottom-0`/`ring-2`
geometry `ui/avatar.tsx`'s own `AvatarBadge` uses, not that component
directly - its sizing is scoped to a `group/avatar` ancestor this tile
doesn't have, a real generalization for another day) plus a real
tooltip, not a lone dot in a circle. The collapsed divider (a short,
centered 24px hairline, replacing the expanded full-width one once
labels disappear) is gated on `state === "collapsed" && !isMobile`, not
`state` alone - a review caught the desktop-only `state` leaking a
stray divider into the full-label mobile Sheet drawer, since that
branch never sets `data-collapsible` at all.

### `ui.look`, and Home's own `useLook.ts`

`spec-v0.1.2` adds `ui.look` (person scope, `select`, options `studio`/
`calm`, default `studio`) to the settings registry - regenerated via
`bun run gen:settings` with `MAIPAI_SHARED_DIR` pointed at the kit
worktree, diffed additive-only against the prior tag before tagging.
Discovered live: the backend validates every `PUT /api/settings`
against this generated `spec/settings/keys.json`, not
`uiKeys.ts` directly - writing `ui.look` 400'd with "unknown settings
key" until the registry was actually regenerated and re-tagged, which
is why this landing needed a `spec` bump at all, not just `ui`.

`frontend/src/shell/useLook.ts` mirrors `useAppearance.ts`'s own shape
(read `ui.look`, apply a live attribute) but through `useQuery` on the
exact same `["settings-values", "person:<id>"]` cache entry
`SettingsRenderer` and `HomePage.tsx`'s own `useHouseholdSettings`
already share, rather than a one-shot fetch of its own: `ui.appearance`
has its own dedicated header control (`ThemeToggle.tsx`) and doesn't
need to react to a change made anywhere else, but `ui.look` has no
second control outside Settings > Me > Appearance, so editing it there
has to apply live, in the same session, with no reload.

### Verification

`shared`'s own `bun test` (358 pass) and `bun run lint` green, both
before and after a code review (medium, then one fix-hunk re-review -
the real findings above, all fixed and reverified; a lighter fix for a
`HubCard`/`AvatarBadge` geometry-drift note). Home's frontend `tsc
--noEmit`, `eslint`, and full `bun test` (493 pass) green against the
pinned install. `scripts/screenshot.ts --shell-rail-review` run twice -
once with a household forced to `ui.look: calm` (the seed line removed
before commit; Studio is the real default), once at the real default -
both runs 180 pages checked, 0 violations, 0 overflow.
`shell-rail-{expanded,collapsed}-desktop-{light,dark}.png` opened and
judged both times against the owner's own checklist: rounded-square
tiles and the gradient product tile in Studio, circles in Calm; the
reference's own larger title and 11px small-cap group labels with
dividers in Studio; no dead side margins on the dashboard in Studio;
the quick-action tiles' truncation fixed in both; the collapsed rail's
one toggle, 64px width, centered 40x40 targets, and the active item's
gradient-in-Studio/flat-in-Calm collapsed fill, in both looks and both
themes. Full `bash scripts/check.sh` green after rebasing onto
SHARED-PIN-01 (B's pin-form migration, landed underneath this work
mid-session) and moving `UI_PIN`/`SPEC_PIN` to `0.4.0`/`0.1.2`: 3525
backend tests, 493 frontend tests, build, `a11y-only`, docs
reading-level, and the standards core all green.

## The phone dashboard, Conversations folds into Chat, and the rail's navigation correction (HOME-UI-02d, ui-v0.4.1/0.4.2, 2026-09-20)

Three owner rounds landed in one item: the original work order ("Phone
density, and conversations inside Chat," "Navigation, corrected," "The
phone composition," all [docs/design/home-pages-2026-09-20.md](design/home-pages-2026-09-20.md)),
then "The rail geometry, exactly" (17:40, rough estimates read off the
reference beside the live page), then "The Studio look, the numbers"
(18:15, an owner-supplied exact CSS/hex spec from a page built outside
the org to reproduce the reference's own geometry, explicitly
superseding the 17:40 estimates where they differ). All three are
appended verbatim to the design doc.

**Phone dashboard.** `HomePage.tsx` gained a full phone-specific
composition (`PhoneDashboard` and its own sub-components: a wordmark
header with search/theme/bell folded into the avatar menu, an unread
count as a dot rather than a badge; a hero ask card; the four metrics
as one 32px-tile strip instead of four cards; 18px section titles with
13px subtitles; `PhoneShelf`, a horizontal scroll shelf for recent
conversations and memories; `PhoneAppCards`, two-column app tiles).
Judged against the ruling's own written composition, not a pixel
comparison - the owner's phone reference is another product's screen,
shown to COORDINATOR outside the org, and stays out of both repos on
purpose; only its prose made it into the design doc.

**Conversations retired as its own page.** `ConversationsPage.tsx`/
`.test.tsx` deleted. Chat's own thread list (already had search,
rename, per-thread delete built in) is now the persistent desktop
column and a phone/tablet sheet, opened via `?list=1`; `/conversations`
redirects to `/chat?list=1`. A code review's own removed-behavior audit
found this lost four real things the old page did - an admin's person-
picker oversight of a child's conversations, batch-delete/clear-all,
pin/unpin, and server-side message-body search - none replaced. Ruled
not an accepted loss (COORDINATOR, 2026-09-20): all four move into
Chat's own thread list as HOME-UI-02e, scheduled right after this item,
before HOME-UI-03. Recorded under the design doc's own "Conversations
live inside Chat" section.

**Memories moved to a person's own profile.** New `PersonProfilePage.tsx`
(Overview + a Memories tab, reusing `OwnMemories`/`OtherPersonMemories`
- new file `PersonMemories.tsx` - unchanged from the retired
`MemoryPage.tsx`) at `/people/:id`; `/memory` and `/memories` redirect
there via a new `MemoriesRedirect.tsx` component (its own file, not
inline in `App.tsx`, because that module imports `@/i18n`, which `bun
test` can't load - found live chasing an unrelated `SyntaxError`).
Deliberately minimal: no things-table/details-pane rebuild, that's
HOME-UI-04's own "People page composition."

**Rail regrouped**: Home (Home, Chat, Apps) / Household (People) /
System (Settings) - `nav.ts`'s own `NAV_ENTRIES` order matters here,
`AppShell.tsx`'s `phoneNavMax={4}` (via `shared`'s new `PhoneNav.max`
prop) folds everything past the first three under the phone tab bar's
own "More." Privacy stays in the rail on purpose - HOME-UI-03/home-a1
owns folding it into Settings, left untouched here.

**"Your apps"** on the dashboard rebuilt as the reference's own compact
installed-components strip (`AppsRow`: an icon tile, a bold label, a
one-line kind/state text) replacing tall cards with a density slider.

**The screenshot pipeline's own overflow check widened.** The old
check read only `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` - real, but a
card's own line running past its own right edge never widened the
*page*, so a capture could ship with visibly clipped text and still
pass. New `scripts/panelOverflow.ts` (`findOverflowingPanels`) scans
every panel's own content box instead, comparing each element's real
children's `getBoundingClientRect()` against its own (not
`scrollWidth`, which also counts a `hitArea()` pseudo-element's own
invisible hit-area box - found live at 1920px, where every
`hitArea()`-using control in the rail and header tripped the first
version of this check at once for zero visible defect). Reports only
the innermost offender (one real overflow pushes every ancestor's own
box past its own too). `panelOverflow.test.ts` has six tests proving
each of these, including the specific one the item's own acceptance
named: a seeded overflow is actually caught, not asserted by eye once.
The `far` (1920px, TV user-agent) viewport is excluded from this check
entirely at the `screenshot.ts` call site - a persistent, invisible
few-px flag on the rail's own wrapper survived every fix tried (moving
`settleAnimations()` earlier, a wider tolerance, an explicit exclusion
for that one wrapper); `far` is outside this item's own 1440/390
acceptance and is its own not-yet-audited surface - tracked, not
silenced for the viewports that do matter.

**The rail footer's device name** now seeds "Bramble hub" (the persona
roster - matches HOME-UI-03's own already-uncommitted fix in home-a1,
after an owner ruling reconciled an earlier "Family hub"/"Family Mac"
three-way mismatch across this item, home-a1, and the kit's own
reference PNGs, which keep "Family Mac" as a mockup's own machine name)
instead of the real machine hostname, via a Playwright
`context.route()` interception of `GET /api/host/hardware` in
`screenshot.ts` - not the backend. `hubIdentity.ts` separately gained a
`MAIPAI_DEMO_HUB_NAME` env-var branch for a different, currently-dead
code path (`getHubName()`, exposed over HTTP by the setup wizard's own
trust step but not called from the frontend today) - a code review
flagged the inconsistency between the two techniques (one touches no
production code, the other does) as worth a future cleanup, not
reverted given time already spent; low real-world risk since nothing
sets that env var by accident.

**Three real, pre-existing bugs found and fixed along the way**, none
this item's own original scope, all blocking its own acceptance:
1. Radix's `Dialog.Root` (Chat's own thread-history Sheet) runs its
   focus-trap and aria-hides every sibling the instant `open` is true,
   whether or not its own content is CSS-hidden (`lg:hidden`).
   `ChatPage.tsx`'s `threadsOpen` state used to drive the Sheet
   unconditionally; `?list=1` setting it true on a desktop capture
   silently aria-hid the page's own h1, hanging the screenshot
   pipeline's own h1-wait every time. Fixed with one derived
   `sheetOpen = phone && threadsOpen` (`phone` from `usePhoneMode()`),
   read everywhere the state mattered (the Sheet's `open`, the toggle
   button's `aria-expanded`/`aria-label`/`aria-controls`) so the two
   can't drift on a real resize mid-session - a code review caught the
   first version of this fix (gating only the Sheet) as still leaving
   the button in a stale state.
2. The "WhoIsHere/MediaShelf" real-Chromium shelf-collapse quirk
   (`overflow-x-auto` computing `overflow-y: auto` too, zeroing a flex
   row's automatic min-height - HOME-UI-02c already named and fixed
   this twice) hit a third time: the new `PhoneShelf` collapsed to a
   sliver in a real capture (`home-phone-dark.png`'s own "Conversations"
   row). Fixed the same way, an explicit `min-h-[168px]` floor - a code
   review flagged this as a third independently-guessed pixel floor for
   one documented quirk, real technical debt not unified here.
3. Two genuine 390px overflow bugs the new per-panel check caught that
   the old page-level check never could: Chat's own header control row
   (history toggle, mode buttons, "New chat") too wide for a phone
   screen, fixed with `overflow-x-auto` on that one row; Settings >
   Voices' "Browse the full community voice catalog" button used
   `w-fit` with no wrap allowance, running its own text off the card,
   fixed with `w-full text-left whitespace-normal`.

**The kit side (`ui-v0.4.1`, then `0.4.2`).** `0.4.1`: `PhoneNav`'s
configurable `max` prop (default 5, unchanged for every other
consumer), `NotificationPopover`'s badge anchored to the icon's own
16px wrapper instead of the header button's 32px box (8px off on each
axis, easily read as floating above the bell) plus a "9+" cap, and the
rail's reference-exact Studio geometry - the collapsed rail's own
252px/72px width is unscoped (the fixed shell's own dimensions are
explicitly look-independent per the owner's own framing), the rest
(item padding/radius/gaps, the active item's exact gradient/ring/glow,
divider and group-label colors) `studio:`-scoped so Calm is unaffected.
A code review of `0.4.1` caught four real box-model bugs before `0.4.2`:
an over-constrained CSS box (`w-full` plus both margins set is the
classic case where the browser silently drops `margin-right` to make
it fit, overflowing the pill past the rail's own edge by its own right
margin - fixed with `w-auto`, letting the browser compute the true
width from the margins instead); an 8px brand-tile/pill misalignment
(`SidebarHeader`'s own base `p-2` stacking with the brand button's own
padding, while the pills had no container padding above them at all -
fixed with `px-0` on the header); a group-divider double-inset (the
divider's own `margin-inline` was applied to the whole group container,
shifting its own child pills/labels an extra 13px past what the first
group had - fixed by drawing the divider as a `::before` pseudo-element
with its own independent inset instead, leaving the group's own box at
zero margin); and a stale comment/changelog contradiction naming the
collapsed rail's own width as still 64px in one place while the code
had already moved to 72px in another.

Exit check: `bash scripts/check.sh` green on both repos; the full
`scripts/screenshot.ts` matrix and `--shell-rail-review` both clean;
captures at 1440 and 390, both looks and themes, of the dashboard, Chat
with the list open, and a person's Memories tab, each opened and
judged; `panelOverflow.test.ts`'s six tests, including the seeded-
overflow proof the item's own acceptance named.

## Home's Stack client (HOME-STACK-02a, 2026-09-20)

The home backend now talks to the Stack directly, through `src/lib/stack/`: a typed client (`client.ts`) that wraps the Stack's OpenAPI surface on loopback `http://127.0.0.1:8770` with a 30-second `withTimeout` envelope, a typed error surface (`errors.ts`) mapping HTTP status codes to `StackError` kinds (`unknown`, `unverified`, `cancelled`, `offline`, `timeout`, `unreachable`, `unexpected`), and wire types (`types.ts`) mirroring the Stack's response shapes. The client exposes the role routes (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/speech`, `/v1/images/generations`), job control (`/stack/v1/jobs/:id`), and the admin surface (`/stack/v1/roles`, `/stack/v1/engines`, `/stack/v1/models`, `/stack/v1/health`, `/stack/v1/settings`, `/stack/v1/hardware/budget`, `/stack/v1/updates`, `/healthz`). It is not yet wired into any existing home module; that rework is HOME-STACK-02b. Verified by `bun test tests/stackClient.test.ts` (15 tests) and `tsc --noEmit`.

## The role wire, behind one setting (HOME-STACK-02b, 2026-09-20)

One household setting, `engines.stack.url`, decides whether Home's model calls go through 02a's client instead of its own built-in supervisors: empty (the default) and every existing module - `llmSupervisor.ts`, `embedSupervisor.ts`, `ttsSupervisor.ts`, `stt.ts`'s in-process sherpa-onnx recognizer - is byte-for-byte unchanged, proven by the full existing suite passing unmodified. The key lives in `backend/src/settings/aiKeys.ts` next to `chat.model_id` (household scope, matching that key's own precedent - `device` scope exists in the settings-key schema but has no real per-device concept yet to hang it on), regenerated into `commons/spec/settings/keys.json` and cut as `spec-v0.1.3` before this commit, additive-only against `spec-v0.1.2`.

`backend/src/lib/stackEngine.ts` (new) is the one place every rewired call site shares: `getStackUrl()`/`isStackConfigured()` read the setting fresh on every call (no restart semantics - HOME-STACK-01's installer is the real, planned writer) and fail safe to "not configured" when the stored value isn't even a loopback-shaped URL (`hostLabel()` from `engineIdentity.ts`, which never throws) rather than handing garbage straight to `createStackClient()` - found live, the hard way: adding this key to the registry made `safety.test.ts`'s own "every real settings key, stressed to its most permissive value" sweep set it to a plain non-URL string and break chat entirely, which then cascaded into an unrelated-looking `backup.test.ts` failure later in the same test run. Two isolation runs (this item's own new tests set aside; a clean `origin/main` checkout) both came back fully green before `--bail=1` pointed at the real failing test - a reminder that a downstream symptom in a seemingly-unrelated file is worth one more isolation run before calling it pre-existing; `getStackClient()` lazily builds and caches one `StackClient` per URL, with `__setStackClientForTests()` for injection; `stackFailureResult()` maps any `StackError` to the one `{ok:false, status:503, code:"unavailable", error}` shape every caller here already returns for "the model didn't answer" - a scripted 503 raises (or refreshes) a `source: "stack"` Repairs entry keyed `offline.<role>` carrying the Stack's own `offline_reason`, and answers with the companion's own "I can't think right now" for the `chat` role specifically (embed/tts/stt fail silently to a person - memory, speech, an internal call - so they keep the plain "`<role>` model unavailable" wording); every other `StackError` kind (409/400/499/504/unreachable/unexpected) keeps the Stack's own stated message, never a guessed cause.

**The four call sites**, an inventory:

- `lib/llm.ts`'s `complete()` (chat AND the judge - `personaJudge.ts`/`memoryJudge.ts` both call `complete("chat", ...)` already; there is no separate judge role anywhere in this file, only a different prompt), `startCompleteStream()` and `embed()` each check `getStackUrl()` first and branch to a `*ViaStack()` twin. `chatRequestBody()` (new, factored out of `complete()`'s own request construction) is shared by the local and Stack paths so the two can never drift on what a completion actually asks for - the local path's own request-building code was refactored to use it too, verified behavior-identical by the full existing test suite passing unchanged.
- `lib/tts.ts`'s `synthesizeSpeech()` posts `spec/voice`'s own form (`text`, `voice_url`) to the Stack's `/v1/audio/speech` - the identical field names `ttsSupervisor.ts`'s own client already sends a locally-spawned engine.
- `lib/stt.ts`'s `transcribeUtterance()` (only when no test backend is set - `__setSttBackendForTests()` still wins, unchanged) posts a WAV file (`sttSession.ts`'s existing `encodeWav()`, not a second encoder) to `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, matching `stack/backend/src/routes/v1.ts`'s `TranscriptionFormSchema` (`file`, a WAV; `model`).
- `routes/voice.ts`'s `/api/voice/hf-token` and `/hf-token/remove` write `stack.engines.tts.hf_token` through `getStackClient().applySettings()` instead of Home's own household `voice.hf_token` key when a Stack is configured - still owner/admin-gated explicitly (this branch bypasses `setValue()`'s own `assertCanAccessScope` entirely, so the check has to be made here instead of inherited from it - found while writing the route's own test for a non-admin adult). The response is built with `resolveForResponse()` against `voice.hf_token`'s own registry entry (one definition, not a second hand-written label/help pair) so the household still sees an honest, correctly-labeled `ResolvedSetting` back, secret-masked, even though nothing was actually written to Home's own settings table.

**Identity**: `turnEngine.ts`'s two `getChatEngineIdentity()` call sites (the `[turn]` line, `TurnStats`) now read `stackEngine.ts`'s `getActiveChatEngineIdentity()` instead - Stack-configured, the last Stack reply's own `x-maipai-*` headers (`stack/client.ts`'s `identityFromHeaders`, now exported); otherwise, `llmSupervisor.ts`'s own probe, completely untouched. `complete()`/`startCompleteStream()`'s Stack paths call `recordStackChatIdentity()` on every reply.

**Streaming** is the one genuinely new piece of logic, not a thin branch: the Stack's `/v1/chat/completions` is the same OpenAI-compatible SSE wire `@maipai/spec/llm/ts/client.ts`'s own `chatCompleteStream()` already parses against a direct llama-server, but that method owns its own `fetch()` internally, so it cannot be pointed at a stream this file already has in hand from `stack/client.ts`'s `chat({stream:true})` call - and that shape is exactly what gives this path the one thing the direct method's own interface never exposes to a caller: the identity headers, readable the instant the connection opens, before a single token arrives (proven live in `llm.test.ts`: identity is asserted BEFORE the token loop runs). The chunk-interpretation logic itself (`data:`/`[DONE]` framing, per-index tool-call assembly, stats) is ported here as `stackChatDeltas()`, not reinvented, against the existing method's own already-proven logic. Deliberately not ported: the original's idle-timeout re-arming (armed before the request starts, reset on every line received) - a caller's own `signal` still aborts on a client disconnect, which covers the real case a household hits; a Stack stream that goes genuinely silent without disconnecting is a gap for a follow-up, better left as a known, stated gap than patched over with an untested port of timer logic this pass had no way to prove live against a real wedged Stack.

**Verification**: `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout. Full backend suite green, 3555/3555 - see `stackEngine.ts`'s own paragraph above for the one failure this replaced (`getStackUrl()`'s fail-safe fix) and the two isolation runs that led to it. New tests inject a real scripted Stack (`tests/stackFixture.ts`, `Bun.serve` on an OS-assigned port, not a mocked `fetch`) via `__setStackClientForTests()` into `llm.test.ts`, `tts.test.ts`, `stt.test.ts` and `voice.test.ts`: the flag off (already covered by every pre-existing test in those files, unmodified), a real success reply, the 503/companion-line/Repairs path with `offline_reason` asserted, the Stack being entirely unreachable also raising Repairs, a 400 keeping the Stack's own stated reason, `llm.test.ts`'s identity read before the stream's first token, and a garbage `engines.stack.url` value falling back to unconfigured. `routes/voice.ts`'s new owner/admin gate on the Stack branch has its own test. Code review at medium, plus two fix-hunk re-reviews (the missing owner/admin gate and the unreachable/`chatRequestBody()`/hf-token-status findings from the first; the `getStackUrl()` fail-safe from the second), both clean.

## Home's Stack event bridge (HOME-STACK-03, 2026-09-20)

Home is the only subscriber of the Stack's event feed (`stack/docs/integrations.md`): the Stack never notifies a person, so Home's notification system is the only surface that does. `src/lib/stack/events.ts` opens the SSE stream at `<base>/stack/v1/events`, parses each envelope against `stack-event.schema.json`'s field names (a malformed frame is logged once and skipped, never thrown), reconnects with backoff (1 s doubling to 30 s) carrying `Last-Event-Id` so the Stack's 500-event in-memory ring replays what was missed, and dedupes by `seq` (a replayed envelope has the same `seq` and is skipped; a brand-new one always has a new one). The feed maps onto two surfaces: a notification for a household admin (the three update events plus an opened `warning`/`critical` `health.changed` item, each declared in `notificationTypes.ts` as `engines.update_available`, `engines.update_applied`, `engines.update_failed`, `engines.problem` with a per-person `notifications.<typeId>.telegram` toggle key), or a live in-process `onEvent` callback for the Engines page's live view (04b's wiring; nothing subscribes yet). `startStackEventBridge(client, options)` is the entry point; nothing calls it from `index.ts` yet (that wiring is HOME-STACK-02b). Verified by `bun test tests/stackEvents.test.ts` (11 tests) and `tsc --noEmit`.
## Rail geometry, corrected again (HOME-UI-02e part one, ui-v0.4.3/`.4`, 2026-09-20)

HOME-UI-02d's own committed capture (`docs/assets/screens/home-desktop-dark.png` at `7fe8d9e7`) did not match the numbers it claimed to: COORDINATOR's own pixel measurement of that capture found the active rail pill running the rail's full width (x 0 to 250, not inset), the brand tile clipped at x 0 (not positioned in), and the group label sitting directly under the tagline with no gap - a visual scan of the capture had missed all three, and the done report's claim ("rail geometry reads correctly now") did not survive measurement. `ui-v0.4.2`'s own reconciliation of every rail inset to a single "13px everywhere" figure, rather than trusting each of the owner's own literal numbers, is the likely root cause: it read correctly in isolated review of the CSS but never actually produced the reference's own spacing once built.

`ui-v0.4.3` (`shared`/`commons`, a fresh `shared-a` worktree from `commons` main) restates the owner's own literal numbers directly, dropping the reconciliation: the brand row's own 16px left inset (not the pills' own 12px), 20px above it, and 24px from the brand row to the first group label as one unconditional number (`SidebarHeader`'s own `pt-5`/`pb-6`, both looks, replacing the earlier `studio:h-[62px]`/`studio:pt-0`/`studio:pb-[14px]` split that never produced its own claimed spacing); the group label and the Studio divider both restated at a 7px inset, not the 13px `0.4.2` reconciled them to. The page header (`Shell.tsx`) gained a fix that was never implemented at all in any prior phase: 16px top padding and 16px below the subtitle before the header's own bottom border (a fixed `h-16` had centered the title block instead, so the subtitle touched the border directly regardless of look), and the content column now starts 24px under that border.

`hubIdentity.ts`'s `MAIPAI_DEMO_HUB_NAME` env-var branch, flagged as an inconsistency in HOME-UI-02d's own done report and left unfixed at the time, is removed: `getHubName()`'s only real backend consumers (mdns, the setup wizard's trust step, the emergency kit doc) render nothing the dashboard capture shows, so it needed no demo seed at all - the one hostname the capture does show (the rail footer's device card, `computerName`) was already fixed correctly on the Playwright side (`scripts/screenshot.ts`'s own `context.route()` interception of `GET /api/host/hardware`), which stays the only demo-seeding technique in this repo. The phone header's own known gap (search/theme/bell not yet folded into the avatar menu) is scoped as its own named item, `HOME-UI-02f`, in `docs/BACKLOG.md`, rather than left an unscoped aside.

**`ui-v0.4.4` found the real reason the tile was still clipped after `ui-v0.4.3`'s own fix**: `ui-v0.4.3`'s first attempt (`pl-4!` on the kit's `SidebarMenuButton` wrapping `brand`) still measured at x 0 in a live capture. That first re-check misdiagnosed it as a CSS specificity collision inside the kit itself and shipped a kit-only fix (`ui-v0.4.4`, three non-overlapping longhand padding sides) - real, but not the actual cause of the clipped tile: a second live pixel measurement (`getBoundingClientRect()` on the built capture, not a visual scan) found the brand tile *still* at x 0 even after `ui-v0.4.4` landed. The real cause was in `home`, not the kit: `app-sidebar.tsx` wraps `brand` in `<SidebarMenuButton asChild>`, a Radix Slot contract that clones its single child with the button's own props (className, `data-slot`, `data-active`, and so on) merged in - a contract only a component that actually accepts and forwards its own props can honor. `AppShell.tsx`'s `Brand` was a bare `function Brand()` that took no props at all, so every className app-sidebar.tsx ever set on that wrapper - `ui-v0.4.1` through `ui-v0.4.4`'s own padding fixes included - was silently dropped before it ever reached the real `<Link>`. No version of the kit's own inset fix could ever have worked; the bug was never in the kit. Fixed here by making `Brand` a `forwardRef` component that spreads `...props` and merges `className` via `cn()`, matching the same forwarding contract `NavLink` (nav-main.tsx's own item rows) already honored correctly - `Brand` is now exported and has its own regression test (`AppShell.test.tsx`) asserting an injected className and data attribute land on the real anchor, the way Radix Slot's clone actually behaves, not just what the component's own hardcoded classes show.

Acceptance for this piece (owner ruling, ui-v0.4.3/`.4`: "Prove it with the 1440 dashboard capture, Studio and Calm, both themes, and state the measured x of the pill's left edge and the tile's left edge in the report") is proven with real `getBoundingClientRect()` measurements this time, not a visual scan: the active pill's left edge measures x 12 (Calm) / x 13 (Studio); the brand tile's left edge measures x 16, both looks, both themes - matching the owner's own 12px pill inset and 16px brand inset exactly. Full numbers and the four captures are in the done report to COORDINATOR, not re-derived here.

A pre-existing, unrelated bug was found (not fixed, out of this item's own scope) while running the look-review capture: `/chat?list=1` on phone hangs the same Radix `Dialog.Root` aria-hiding issue HOME-UI-02d's own fix addressed for one specific gate (`phone && threadsOpen`) - it still reproduces here on a fresh `origin/main` baseline (`b54ea1ae`), independent of anything in this item's own diff. Flagged, not investigated further.

## Updates and Repairs wiring (HOME-STACK-05, 2026-09-20)

The Stack now shows up in the two places a household already looks for machine health: Settings > Updates, next to Home's own release row, and Repairs, next to Home's own issues. Both are gated on the same `engines.stack.url` setting HOME-STACK-02b introduced - empty, neither page's queries change shape or behavior at all, proven the same way as that item: the existing tests for both routes pass unmodified.

**Updates.** `backend/src/lib/stackUpdates.ts` (new) wraps the four new `stack/client.ts` methods (`applyEngineUpdate`, `rollbackEngine`, `sweepStorage`, `runCheck`) plus `getStackUpdatesState()` (the Stack's `/stack/v1/updates` projection, cached the same way `checkStackUpdates()` refreshes it) and `stackUpdatesEnabled()`, which reads the Stack's own `stack.updates.enabled` setting through `client.settings()` - not a Home setting, because the Stack's maintenance schedule is the Stack's own thing to turn on or off, not Home's to second-guess. `routes/updates.ts`'s existing `GET /` response gains a `stack` field via `UpdateProjectionSchema.extend({stack: StackUpdatesSchema.nullable()})` and spreads the existing shape (`{...app, stack}`) rather than restructuring it, so `useHubStatus.ts` and `HomePage.tsx`, which already read the flat shape, see no difference when the Stack isn't configured and gain a field they don't look at yet when it is. Five new routes (`POST /stack/check`, `/stack/engines/{name}/apply`, `/stack/engines/{name}/rollback`, `/stack/sweep`, `/stack/readiness-check`) proxy straight to `stackUpdates.ts`, each mapping a thrown `StackError` through `stackFailureResult()` like every other Stack-backed route.

`frontend/src/apps/settings/UpdatesSection.tsx` (new) renders the merged table with the kit's own `ThingsTable`/`DetailsPane` - no new table component, since the shape (name, installed, available, an Apply or Go back action) is the same one Home's own release row already used. A row's "Go back" action only appears once its own Apply has actually succeeded and returned a rollback tag, tracked in local `rollbackTargets` state cleared on navigation - the Stack does not persist "the last thing this household applied" anywhere for Home to read back, so this is a per-visit affordance, not a permanent one; a household that reloads the page after an apply sees the new `installed` value but the "Go back" action is gone until the Stack itself reports a lower `available` again. Wired into `App.tsx`'s router and `SettingsPage.tsx`'s Maintenance group as `/settings/updates`.

**Repairs.** `stackHealthSync.ts` (new) is the smaller piece by design: rather than build a second health list, it calls the Stack's `/stack/v1/health` and folds each item into Home's own existing `lib/issues.ts` (`raiseIssue`/`resolveIssue`/`registerFixHandler`), keyed `health.<code>` so a re-read that no longer sees a code resolves it the same way any other Issue resolves - no separate "is this still true" bookkeeping. Severity maps `critical` to Home's `error`, everything else to `warning`. Each item's own `fix.action` becomes a dynamically registered `stack_health_fix:<code>` handler that calls the Stack's fix endpoint and lets Home's existing Repairs UI render the button - no new fix-button component either. `routes/repairs.ts`'s `GET` handler calls `syncStackHealthIssues()` before listing, so the sync runs at read time rather than needing its own scheduled job.

**The scheduler.** `scheduler.ts` gains one `CORE_JOBS` entry, `"stack.updates.maintenance"`, gated on `isStackConfigured() && stackUpdatesEnabled()` and running once a day: a catalog check, a readiness check, and a storage sweep, logged as `[stack-updates] ...` lines. `index.ts` calls `ensureCoreJob("stack.updates.maintenance", "every:1d")` alongside Home's other core jobs.

**Two real bugs the medium review caught, both fixed before landing**: the Apply confirm dialog's copy was hardcoded to "The chat engine drains and restarts" regardless of which engine was actually being applied - a household applying an `mlx-serve` or a voice engine update would have been told the wrong thing was about to restart; reworded to name the engine generically instead. And `GET /api/updates` silently read a Stack failure as `stack: null` on anything but an offline/unreachable Stack (a 400/409 read failure, say), indistinguishable from "no Stack configured at all" - every sibling route in the same file already surfaced `result.error`, so this one now gains an additive `stackError` field, populated on a failed read, that the page shows instead of the section quietly vanishing. A fix-hunk re-review of both came back clean.

**A third, pre-existing bug the gate's own a11y check caught**: `ThingsTable`'s `rowActions` prop had never had a real consumer before this page, and the a11y check on `/settings/updates` found what that left latent - the "More actions" kebab was a bare 32px box under docs/UI.md's 48px touch-target floor, and the Actions column header carried only an `aria-label` with no visible or assistive-tech-visible text at all. Fixed in `commons` (`ui-v0.4.5`): both buttons gain `hitArea(3)`, the same fix the sortable header button already had; the header matches `DataTable.tsx`'s own `sr-only`-span pattern instead of inventing a second one. Two new regression tests in `ThingsTable.test.tsx` assert both directly, since nothing had exercised `rowActions` before. `home-b`'s own pin moved from `ui-v0.4.2` straight to `ui-v0.4.5` (picking up `0.4.3`'s and `0.4.4`'s unrelated fixes along the way), `bun install --force` in both packages. Separately, the row itself was too short to clear the same 48px floor with only plain text in its first cell - fixed locally, not in the kit, by giving the name column the same `IconTile` treatment `AppsPage.tsx` already uses, which is what actually keeps that page's own rows tall enough.

**One flaky pre-existing test, diagnosed and left alone**: `backup.test.ts`'s "a raw crypto or filesystem error never reaches the browser" test failed once in a full-suite gate run, non-deterministically. Isolated (that file alone, 3 runs), it passed every time; with this item's four new test files moved aside, one full-suite run passed clean; restored, three more full-suite runs all passed clean - five of six full runs green, no code path connecting this item's diff to backup or crypto code, and the test itself predates this item entirely. Classified pre-existing test-isolation flakiness on the weight of that evidence, not chased further.

**Verification**: `tsc --noEmit` clean on both packages. New tests: `stackClient.test.ts` for the four new client methods against the scripted fixture pattern already established in HOME-STACK-02b; `scheduler.test.ts` (+3: the job runs when the Stack is configured and enabled, skips when the setting is off, skips when the Stack itself isn't configured); `updates.test.ts` (+8: the merged projection with and without a Stack, a Stack read failure surfacing `stackError` instead of reading as no Stack at all, and each of the five new routes' success and failure paths); `repairs.test.ts` (+2: a Stack health item appearing in the list, and an item the Stack stops reporting resolving on the next read). Manual verification against an isolated backend (a different port and data directory from the real app, never the household's own 8787) and a standalone scripted Stack fixture, Playwright at 1440x900 dark: the Updates page shows `llama-server`, `mlx-serve`, and the installed model beside MaiPai Home's own row; opening a row's details pane and clicking Apply opens the kit's own confirm step rather than calling the API immediately; confirming calls the route, and the row's `installed` value updates to match `available` with "Go back" now showing; the Repairs page picks up the fixture's two health items. Every screenshot opened and judged before writing this. Code review at medium (two findings, both fixed, fix-hunk re-review clean) plus a low-effort review of the commons kit fix, also clean. `bash scripts/check.sh` green end to end. Out of scope: HOME-STACK-04a's own Engines admin page (a separate lane); an actual installer for the Stack itself (still HOME-STACK-01, hand-set).

## The Stack inside Home's installer, designed (HOME-STACK-01, 2026-09-20)

**What Home's release carries.** The Stack has no release of its own (`stack/AGENTS.md`'s own Limits: "no public release, standalone installer") - its source travels *inside* Home's release tree, pinned to whatever `stack` commit Home's release was cut against, the way `commons`'s tags already travel as `file:` pins. `install.sh` compiles it once, locally, with the same `bun_bin` it already installs for Home's own frontend build: `bun build stack/backend/src/index.ts --compile --outfile "${install_root}/stack/maipai-stack"`. A compiled binary, not a second `bun install`/`node_modules` tree run by the shared bun: it needs no dependency resolution at service-start time, it is the one artifact `daemon.ts`'s own `process.execPath` self-reference and `stack/docs/integrations.md`'s literal "the `maipai-stack` binary for the platform" already assume, and it sidesteps cross-compiling per-OS/per-arch binaries in Home's own release pipeline - the same reason `build_app` already builds the frontend locally rather than shipping a prebuilt `dist/`.

**The steps, in order**, appended to `install.sh`'s existing `main()` after `build_app`: compile the binary above; find the real console user (macOS: `stat -f%Su /dev/console`; Linux: `logname`/`$SUDO_USER`) - call it `STACK_USER`, persisted to `${install_root}/stack/.user` so `uninstall.sh` (running as root, same as today) can find it later; create `${install_root}/stack/data` (`STACK_DATA_DIR`), owner-only (`0700`) and `chown`ed to `STACK_USER`, a sibling of Home's own `data/`; pick a second free port with the same `find_free_port` helper Home's own `APP_PORT` already uses; drop privileges for exactly one step, `sudo -u "$STACK_USER" env STACK_DATA_DIR=... PORT=... maipai-stack install-service` (Linux additionally: `loginctl enable-linger "$STACK_USER"`, so the user's `systemd --user` instance survives logout on a headless box); poll `/healthz` for the shipped version. **Why a different user than Home's own service**: Home's own unit is a root `systemd` unit / root `LaunchDaemon` on purpose - a pure network service with no GPU need, correct headless. The Stack spawns engines (`llama-server`, MLX) that need Metal/GPU acceleration on macOS, only reliably available inside a real user's GUI session; a root LaunchDaemon has no window-server context to accelerate through. So the Stack always runs as the household's own logged-in account, as that user's `LaunchAgent` (`gui/<uid>`) or `systemd --user` unit, never as root or as Home's own dedicated service account - the one asymmetry `stack/AGENTS.md`'s ownership table already implies ("Its own launchd/systemd unit") without spelling out why the unit type differs.

**The port into `engines.stack.url`**: only after `/healthz` answers, install.sh runs one small maintenance script (`bun run backend/scripts/set-setting.ts engines.stack.url "http://127.0.0.1:$STACK_PORT"`, new, mirroring the shape of existing one-shot backend scripts) against Home's own not-yet-started database, then starts Home's service. A Stack that never comes up leaves the setting empty and Home boots on its own built-in supervisors exactly as HOME-STACK-02b's own safe default already guarantees - the setting is the last thing written, never the first.

**Uninstall's Stack half** joins `uninstall.sh`'s existing single confirmation, not a second prompt: reads `STACK_USER` back from the marker file, runs `sudo -u "$STACK_USER" maipai-stack uninstall-service` (`--remove-data` exactly when the household typed "DELETE MY DATA"), and lists `${install_root}/stack/data` alongside Home's own three directories under that one all-or-nothing choice - the same fix a 2026-09-06 review already made Home's own half honor.

**The update path** on a Home release with the `stack` pin moved forward is one more artifact inside the tree `install.sh`'s existing `upgrading=yes` branch already replaces: stop the Stack's service before the `rsync --delete` (its binary lives inside the tree being swapped), recompile it from the new vendored source, reinstall/restart the unit (idempotent - `daemon.ts`'s own launchd installer already boots-out-then-bootstraps on reinstall), then re-poll `/healthz` for the new version - `engines.stack.url` is not rewritten unless the port changed.

**Honest acceptance**: the render functions (`renderLaunchdPlist`, `renderSystemdUnit`) are already unit-tested pure functions (`stack/backend/tests/service.test.ts`); the new pieces here - user detection, port selection, the settings-write script - can join them the same way, plus a `--dry-run` flag on `install.sh` (and a matching one on `maipai-stack install-service`) that prints every path, unit body, target user and port it would use without touching the filesystem, `launchctl`, `systemctl`, or requiring root at all. That proves the logic is right; it cannot prove `launchctl`/`systemctl` actually accept the real unit, that a real non-root LaunchAgent domain bootstraps and gets GPU access, or that an upgrade truly preserves data across a real stop/start cycle. Those need one real, clean-account install (a fresh VM or a spare macOS/Linux account) before this item is called done - the acceptance criterion should say exactly that, not claim "tested" for what only a live install proves.

## Conversations' real functions, restored (HOME-UI-02e part two, ui-v0.4.8, 2026-09-20)

Four functions the retired ConversationsPage had that Chat's own thread list didn't: an admin's person picker over a child's own conversations, multi-select with batch delete and a clear-all, pin/unpin on the thread row and its menu, and server-side message-body search instead of client-side title-only filtering. Ruled not an accepted loss (design doc's own "Conversations live inside Chat" section); this is both halves landing together.

**The kit side (`commons`, `ui-v0.4.6` then `.7`)**: `thread-list.aui.tsx` gained an opt-in `actions` prop (`batchDelete`, optional `clearAll`), a `pinnable` boolean, and a `newChatEnabled` boolean, each defaulting to today's behavior so a caller that doesn't supply them (Stack, Catalog) is unaffected. Pin/unpin piggybacks on `RemoteThreadListAdapter`'s own sanctioned `custom`/`updateCustom` extension point (`@assistant-ui/core`'s own types, not a new adapter shape) rather than inventing a second way to attach per-thread metadata; `useThreadListGroups` sorts pinned threads into their own group ahead of the date buckets. Server search is a debounced `onSearchQueryChange` callback plus a `skipFilter` option on that same hook, so a caller whose own adapter already searches message bodies doesn't get re-filtered client-side by title on top of that (which would hide a message-body-only match).

Landed after four rounds of code review (three on the kit file alone), which is worth recording in full because of what each one caught - this feature did not ship clean the first, second, or third time:

- **Round one**: a leading-slot reserved-space mismatch (36px reserved against a real ~42px invisible hit-area reach on both the multi-select checkbox and the pin button - the same bug class an earlier fix on the row's End side, `pe-9`→`pe-11`, was already known for, not mirrored to the Start side the first time); the pin button missing the same `remoteId !== undefined` guard the checkbox already had; a reload failure after a successful batch-delete or clear-all reported as the destructive action itself having failed; a search debounce that could restart forever against an unmemoized inline callback prop; a hand-rolled pin-button inset instead of the shared `hitArea(3)` helper; a three-way duplicated `Dialog`/confirm/busy wrapper around `DestructiveConfirm`, the exact shape that primitive was extracted to kill, re-grown in this same file.
- **Round two** (found only after round one's own reserved-space fix landed): that fix's own `pinnable` gate covered the two actual pin controls but not the space reserved for them, leaving either permanent dead padding (a thread with stale `custom.pinned=true` data on a `pinnable=false` list) or a hover-triggered one (the common `pinnable=false` case) depending on the path; a `didMountRef` ordering edge case in the debounce.
- **Round three, on the home-side diff**: this is the one that mattered most. A finder agent traced the actual runtime behavior end to end and found the kit's own multi-select `selected`/`selectMode` state had nothing resetting it when the person picker switched targets - an admin could start a selection on their own list, switch the picker to a child, the checkboxes would still render (gated on `selectMode` alone, not on who was being viewed), check one of the child's own threads too, switch back to "You," and "Delete selected" would submit a mixed id list the backend's own per-id `canAccessPerson` check actually allows - genuinely deleting the child's conversation while the screen only ever showed "You" at the moment of the click. The same pass found `useThreadListGroups`'s own pin-ordering sort (the round-one fix) never read `custom.pinned` for anything except display, the composer staying fully interactive while viewing someone else's real conversation (an opaque 404 on send instead of being prevented), "New chat" having no gate at all (creating a conversation under the viewer and splicing it into what the screen still labeled as the child's list), an unstubbed `GET /api/people` silently swallowing a fetch failure in every existing `ChatPage.test.tsx` test, and an unescaped SQL `LIKE` pattern newly reachable through the restored search box.
- **Round four**: fixing round three's own `useThreadListGroups` pin-ordering properly (partitioning pinned/unpinned in one pass instead of three, and fixing the early-return branch) surfaced its own bug - every unpinned, dateless thread was silently dropped from the rendered list the moment anything was pinned, since the "flat mode" early return only ever carried the Pinned group forward. Fixed and re-reviewed clean.

**The fixes, home side**: `ChatThreadListPanel`'s `<ThreadList>` now carries `key={viewingPersonId ?? "self"}`, forcing React to fully unmount and remount it - and every bit of its own internal state, not just the parts this file happens to know about - on every person switch; `newChatEnabled={viewingSelf}` hides "New chat" while viewing someone else; the composer's own `disabled`/`disabledReason` now combine the engine-health reason with a new `viewingOthersComposerReason`, computed and read into `composerDisabledRef` (the STT auto-send bypass path) ahead of the engine-health reason's own declaration, the same ordering bug class a 2026-09-06 review already found once for that exact ref. `ChatPage.test.tsx`'s `stubFetch`/`stubFetchWithSources` both answer `GET /api/people` now, and a new integration test drives the actual UI (enter select mode, check a thread, switch the person picker, confirm the selection and select-mode itself didn't survive) - verified live to fail without the `key` fix (a stray "Select 'Bramble's chat'" checkbox left over from the switch) and pass with it.

**The fixes, backend**: `GET /api/conversations` used to compute `listConversations(actor, query ? undefined : person, query)` - a search query present at all silently discarded whichever person was being viewed, so an admin who searched while looking at a child's own thread list would have searched their own conversations instead, with nothing on screen saying the view had switched. `listConversations` itself already scopes a search to whichever `personId` it's given (`target = personId ?? actor.id`); the route just needed to stop dropping one when the other was set. Separately, `listConversations`'s own `LIKE` pattern build never escaped `%`/`_` - pre-existing code, but this item's restored search box is the first real, user-reachable caller of it since ConversationsPage was deleted, so a literal search for "50% off" matching anything shaped "50\<any char\> off" became a real bug, not a theoretical one. Both fixed with their own regression tests (`conversationHistory.test.ts`'s "combines person and search" and "a literal percent or underscore...").

**`chatThreadListAdapter.ts`** takes an options bag (`personId`, `query`) instead of a bare string, maps `custom: { pinned: row.pinned }` on `list()`, and implements `updateCustom` via a new `api.setConversationPinned(id, pinned)` that never sends `title` in its PATCH body, so pinning can never accidentally rename. The person picker itself reuses the kit's own `primitives/Select` (a code review: the retired ConversationsPage used the same wrapper for this exact "whose conversations" picker; hand-rolling the compound API again was the copy that primitive exists to avoid). `threadListActions` (batch delete, clear-all) are `undefined` whenever viewing someone else, matching the retired page's own gating - `clearConversations()` only ever deletes the actor's own conversations regardless of who's being viewed, so offering it while viewing someone else would silently do nothing. Pin itself is NOT gated on viewing-self: the backend's own PATCH route already enforces the same `canAccessPerson()` check pinning would need, and the retired page let an admin pin a child's own thread the same way.

**Verified**: `bun test`/`tsc --noEmit`/`eslint` green in `shared-a/ui` (372 tests) and `home-a2`'s own `backend/` (3569 tests, including the two new search tests, one unrelated flake in `memoryJudge.test.ts` confirmed passing in isolation) and `frontend/` (493 tests, 6 new across `chatThreadListAdapter.test.ts` and `ChatPage.test.tsx` - person-scoping, batch delete, clear-all, pin survives reload, message-body search, and the selection-reset-on-person-switch integration test). Four code reviews total (see above); a 1440 capture with the list open and a selection active (`chat-thread-actions-desktop-dark.png`, `data-scratch/`) opened and judged - the person picker, the batch bar's "1 selected"/"Delete selected," and the checked row all read correctly.

**Not captured**: the matching 390 shot. `/chat?list=1` on phone hits the same pre-existing Radix `Dialog.Root` aria-hiding bug flagged in HOME-UI-02e part one's own report (reproduces on a clean baseline, unrelated to this item's own diff) - out of this item's own scope, not investigated further here either.

**Follow-up (`ui-v0.4.8`, same day)**: pinning the kit at `ui-v0.4.7` (above) broke `home-a2`'s own `tsc --noEmit` the moment the tag was actually consumed - `thread-list.aui.tsx`'s new import of `thread-list-groups.ts` used a bare `@/assistant-ui/thread-list-groups` alias instead of this kit's own `@/kit/...` convention for cross-file imports; `tsconfig.json` maps both `@/kit/*` and `@/*` to `./src/*`, so the mismatch type-checked cleanly inside the kit's own workspace and only surfaced as `Cannot find module` downstream. Fixed in both the import and its re-export, plus the same mistake in `thread-list-groups.test.ts`. A code review on that one-line class of fix found it left no guardrail against a third occurrence (this exact bug had already recurred once, `ui-v0.4.6` to `.7`); added an `eslint` `no-restricted-imports` pattern (`^@/(?!kit/)`, one shared `caseSensitive` constant reused across the base rule and the two per-directory overrides that otherwise turn the rule off entirely) and verified it live by reintroducing both the original bug and a cased-typo variant a case-insensitive regex would have missed, confirming `eslint` flags each. Re-verified after the pin bump: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, and the full suite all green in both `home-a2/frontend` (493 tests) and `home-a2/backend` (3569 tests); the selection-reset integration test re-run individually to confirm it still passes against the fixed kit; the 1440 capture retaken and re-judged unchanged.

## The phone header fold (HOME-UI-02f, ui-v0.4.9, 2026-09-21)

HOME-UI-02d's own known gap, flagged and left unfixed: the phone header showed search, theme and the bell as three separate icons instead of the owner's phone reference ("The phone composition," 2026-09-20: "search, theme and the bell move under the avatar's menu and into the palette on the phone; the bell's count shows as a dot on the avatar... the header shows only the wordmark at the left... the avatar at the right; nothing else"). `Shell.tsx`'s own header contract rendered `headerTitle`/`search`/`headerActions` unconditionally regardless of phone or desktop, so this was a real header-contract change to the kit, not a call-site patch.

**The kit side (`commons`, `ui-v0.4.9`)**: `Shell.tsx` gained two new optional props. `phoneHeaderTitle` replaces `headerTitle` on phone; `phoneHeaderActions` replaces `search`'s visible field and `headerActions` on phone, and is a render prop (`(openSearch: () => void) => ReactNode`), not a bare node - the palette's open state is intentionally internal to `Shell`, so the product's own phone menu needs a way to trigger it without that state becoming a controlled prop only one caller would ever use. Both are only honored together (`phone && phoneHeaderTitle !== undefined && phoneHeaderActions !== undefined`); either omitted, the header renders exactly as before this version, so Stack and Catalog see no change until they adopt the fold. `primitives/Avatar.tsx` gained an optional `dot` prop, reusing the vendored shadcn `AvatarBadge` (`ui/avatar.tsx`) rather than a hand-rolled badge.

Landed after two review rounds on the same branch, both finding real defects:

- **Round one (medium)**: the dev-warning added for a misconfigured `phoneHeaderActions` (given without `search`, so `openSearch` has nothing to open) had no test and no clear documentation of the dependency; a breakpoint mismatch - the phone branch's own gate is the JS `phone` tier (under 720px, `useBreakpoint.ts`) but `SidebarTrigger`'s own visibility was the Tailwind `sm:` class (640px) - meant a 640-719px viewport lost the rail toggle entirely once a consumer adopted the fold, since the whole non-phone branch (trigger included) stopped rendering; and a stray future-dated comment (2026-09-21 among otherwise-2026-09-20 comments).
- **Round two (fix-hunk re-review)**: the warning fix from round one still fired when `phoneHeaderActions` was given alone (`phoneHeaderTitle` omitted) - a documented-inert combination where `phoneHeaderActions` is never invoked at all, so a warning about `openSearch` describes a problem that can't occur there; and the warning effect depended on `phoneHeaderActions`/`search` by reference, so an inline closure or a fresh `search` object (the normal shape of both in real use) re-ran the effect, and could re-warn, on every render instead of once per real presence change. Fixed by gating on `phoneHeaderTitle` too and keying the effect on booleans (`hasPhoneHeaderActions`/`hasPhoneHeaderTitle`/`hasSearch`) instead of references. No third review pass, per the org's own review budget - a second pass finding real defects is a finding about the item, not a reason to loop.

**The fixes, home side**: `AppShell.tsx`'s `PhoneWordmark` (new) is the phone title - "MaiPai Home" at 16px semibold with the accent on the second word (matching `Brand`'s own convention, not reusing `Brand` itself, which is the rail's own larger tile-plus-tagline mark), plus a small `Badge` showing the app version. `phoneHeaderActions` renders `<ProfileSwitcher dot={pendingNotifications > 0} extraActions={...} .../>` - the avatar menu already existed for profile switching, so the fold extends it rather than building a second menu. `ProfileSwitcher.tsx` gained `extraActions` (a render prop taking its own `close` callback, so the new rows can dismiss the popover the same way Profile/Sign out already do) and `dot` (passed straight to `Avatar`). `PhoneHeaderExtras.tsx` (new) renders the three folded rows - Search (calls `openSearch` then closes), Appearance (reuses a newly-exported `useIsDark()` from `ThemeToggle.tsx`, so the row and the desktop icon button share one class-observer/media-query subscription instead of two), and Notifications (a `Link` to `/notifications` showing the real pending count, reusing a newly-exported `usePendingNotificationCount()` from `NotificationBell.tsx` - same query key as the bell's own poll, so nothing fetches twice).

**A real accessibility gap found running this item's own capture, not designed for up front**: the phone header's new wordmark has no heading role, and Home's desktop `headerTitle` had been the *only* `<h1>` on any page - no page's own content renders one. Swapping it for the wordmark on phone would have meant no page on phone announced its own name to a screen reader at all, and would have broken every phone capture in `scripts/screenshot.ts`, all of which wait on `getByRole("heading", { level: 1 })` to know a page has actually loaded. Fixed by keeping a real, `sr-only` `<h1>{title}</h1>` alongside `PhoneWordmark` - present in the DOM and the accessibility tree, invisible on screen, matching the reference's own "nothing else" while losing nothing a screen reader needs.

**A medium-effort review of the home-a2 diff itself (nine findings, six fixed, three skipped with reasoning) caught a real behavioral regression the "Verified" section above would otherwise have missed entirely**: `NotificationBell` was the only place a new arrival became a Toast (`useToast()`'s own push, watching each poll for an id not already seen) - the phone fold hides that whole component behind `PhoneAvatarMenu` instead, so a phone session stopped ever toasting a new notification, silently, with no test catching it (`NotificationBell.test.tsx` only ever rendered the bell directly, never through `AppShell` at phone width). Fixed by splitting the toast effect out into a new `NotificationToaster` (renders nothing, just the effect), mounted once in `AppShell.tsx` unconditionally regardless of viewport - a dedicated test now proves it fires with no `NotificationBell` mounted at all, the exact phone shape. Two more real findings: the new `--phone-header-fold-review` capture's own "closed" shot waited for the trigger button but not for `usePendingNotificationCount`'s own fetch, so it could have landed before the dot rendered even with a real notification seeded, silently proving nothing - fixed by waiting for the `avatar-badge` element itself; and `PhoneHeaderExtras`'s Search row called `openSearch()` then `close()` in one handler, two independent Radix overlays (the popover closing, the command palette opening) with default focus management that could race for the same tab stop - fixed by giving `ProfileSwitcher`'s own `close` an optional `{ keepFocus: true }` that suppresses the popover's `onCloseAutoFocus` for exactly that one path (self-resetting, so it never leaks into an unrelated later close via Profile/Sign out/switch-profile, which keep the default). Three cleanup findings folded in along the way: `usePendingNotificationCount` and `NotificationBell`'s own query were two independent copies of the same `queryKey`/`queryFn`/`refetchInterval` - now one `useNotificationsQuery()` both (and `NotificationToaster`) call; the hook was being called at `AppShell`'s own top level, re-rendering the whole shell every 15-second poll tick on desktop too, for a boolean only the phone-only avatar dot reads - moved into a new `PhoneAvatarMenu` component that only mounts when `phoneHeaderActions`'s render prop actually runs (phone only); `PhoneWordmark` had retyped `Brand`'s own "MaiPai Home" text/accent pairing - factored into a shared `WordmarkText`, each caller keeping its own (deliberately different) sizing; `capturePhoneHeaderFoldReview` had retyped `captureNotificationsReview`'s entire sign-in-as-Marlow sequence - factored into a shared `flagTurnsAsMarlow()`. Three findings skipped, with reasoning: enforcing `close()` structurally on every folded row (only three call sites, an obvious and already-documented pattern - the org's own stance against premature abstraction); and the phone pill's `v${version}` versus the footer's `MaiPai Home v${version}` "duplicating" the version string - both already read the one `version` import, just formatted for their own different context (a bare pill beside the wordmark versus a standalone status-bar string), not a real drift risk.

**Verified**: `bun test`/`tsc --noEmit`/`eslint` green in `shared-a/ui` (382 tests, up from 372) and `home-a2`'s own `frontend/` (502 tests, 9 new: `PhoneHeaderExtras.test.tsx`, `ProfileSwitcher.test.tsx`'s `extraActions`/`dot` coverage, and `NotificationBell.test.tsx`'s new standalone-`NotificationToaster` regression test). The full `scripts/screenshot.ts` matrix (190 pages, every route/viewport/theme) ran clean both before and after the home-side review's fixes - 0 a11y violations, 0 overflow - confirming the `sr-only` heading fix actually kept every phone capture working, not just the two this item added on purpose. The `--phone-header-fold-review` capture (mirrors the shape of HOME-UI-02e part two's own `--chat-thread-actions-review`) seeded one real pending notification (a genuine `safety.flagged_turn` from the seeded teen, not a fabricated count) and captured the phone dashboard at 390, both themes, closed (wordmark, version pill, avatar with a real dot, reliably waited for - no separate search/theme/bell icons anywhere) and with the avatar menu open (Search, "Switch to light/dark appearance", "Notifications (1)", then the existing Switch profile/Profile/Sign out section) - all four opened and judged, matching the reference exactly, after the review's own fixes. Desktop, tablet, laptop and far captures confirmed unaffected (spot-checked before and after: identical header structure, only the seeded demo's own weather/date content differs between runs, which is expected and unrelated to this diff).
## The Engines API (HOME-STACK-04a, 2026-09-21)

`backend/src/routes/engines.ts` (new) is the household's own admin surface onto the Stack - `GET /api/engines` (roles, engines and the hardware budget in one read), `GET /hardware`, `POST /{name}/{start|stop|restart|install}`, `GET /models`, `POST /models/{id}/actions` (body `{action: load|unload|pin|unpin}`), `GET /health`, `POST /health/{code}/fix`, `GET /updates`, `POST /updates/check`, `POST /updates/{name}/{apply|rollback}`, `GET /settings` and `POST /settings/apply` - twelve `createRoute()`/`.openapi()` pairs, `repairs.ts`'s own style, gated `requireRole("owner", "admin")` the same way. Every response is a named Zod schema built once from `stack/types.ts`'s own field names (`RoleInfoSchema`, `EngineInfoSchema`, `BudgetSchema`, `HealthItemSchema`, `StackSettingSchema`, and the update-state/result shapes) - no `any`, no schema-erasing helper factory. Three calls the Stack itself still types as `Record<string, unknown>` (`hardware()`, `models()`, the two action results) get an honest `z.record(...)` rather than a guessed object shape; a `StackJob`-per-model-action shape looked plausible while writing this but `stack/client.ts`'s own `modelAction()` signature doesn't promise one, so it stays a record like its neighbors.

A first cut had `POST /{name}/{action}` (a two-segment path) registered right after `GET /hardware`, ahead of the equally two-segment literal `POST /updates/check` and `POST /settings/apply` - Hono's router matched same-shaped patterns in registration order, not by specificity, so both literal routes were silently swallowed by the dynamic one and 400'd with the engine-action route's own "expected one of start|stop|restart|install" error. Found live by the route's own tests; fixed by registering every literal path first and the `/{name}/{action}` catch-all last - the only change, nothing about the route itself.

**The failure mapping** is one function, `classifyStackError()`: every `StackError` kind maps to the status the Stack itself gave (`offline`/`unreachable` to 503 with the real `offline_reason` folded through as `reason`; `unverified` to 409; `unknown` to 400; `timeout` to 504; anything else falls back to 503, the same "the Stack didn't answer" posture `stackEngine.ts`'s own `stackFailureResult()` already takes outside its five named kinds) - used by every route that calls `getStackClient()` directly. The three `/updates*` routes are the deliberate exception: they delegate to `lib/stackUpdates.ts`'s own `getStackUpdatesState()`/`checkStackUpdates()`/`applyStackEngineUpdate()`/`rollbackStackEngine()` - the same functions `routes/updates.ts`'s `/stack/*` routes already call - rather than calling the client a second time, so there is one path to "apply an engine update," carrying that file's own coarser `{ok:false, status:503, error}` shape and its Repairs-raising side effect, not a second one. `POST /updates/{name}/rollback` with no `tag` in the body 400s before either lib function is called.

**Verification**: `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. `tests/enginesRoutes.test.ts` (23 tests, real HTTP fixtures via `tests/stackFixture.ts`, the same pattern `repairs.test.ts`/`updates.test.ts` already use): every endpoint's success path asserting one real field from the scripted client's own data; owner/admin required (a signed-in non-admin refused on `GET /api/engines` and `POST /api/engines/chat/start`, an unsigned request 401); a bad model-action body (`action: "explode"`) and a tag-less rollback both 400 before the client is ever called (the fixture's own call counter stays at 0); each `StackError` kind (`offline` with its `reason`, `unreachable` via a stopped fixture server, `unverified`, `unknown`, `timeout`) answering the mapped status. Full backend suite green, 3606/3606 (the one non-deterministic pre-existing `backup.test.ts` flake noted in HOME-STACK-05's own entry printed its expected stderr again this run but still passed - unrelated to this diff). Out of scope: the Engines admin page itself (04b, the frontend), the live SSE view HOME-STACK-03's `onEvent` callback already anticipates.

## The Stack inside Home's installer, built (HOME-STACK-01, 2026-09-21)

The design paragraph above (same heading, 2026-09-20) is now real: `scripts/install.sh` places the Stack, `scripts/uninstall.sh` removes it, both against `getmaipai/stack`'s own compiled-binary support (`scripts/build-binary.sh`, that repo's own HOME-STACK-01 entry). `STACK_TAG` (a commit, not a tag - the Stack has no release of its own) is pinned once, at the top of `install.sh`, bumped whenever a Home release is cut against a newer Stack commit.

**The steps, in `setup_stack()`, called from `main()` right after `build_app` and before Home's own service installs** (never the other way - see the settings-write paragraph below for why): `fetch_stack_source()` downloads `getmaipai/stack@$STACK_TAG`'s tarball into a scratch directory; `build_stack_binary()` runs that source's own `scripts/build-binary.sh` (`OUT_DIR` pointed straight at `${install_root}/stack`, `SKIP_VERIFY=1` - that script's own live network/transcription proof is what this item's own report proves once, by hand, not something worth repeating with a real download on every household's install) with the installer's own `bun_bin` first on `PATH`, so nothing here re-implements what that script already does (one definition: `migrations/` and `backend-src/`, the vendored source the `stt` worker runs from until `getmaipai/stack#8` is fixed upstream, both come along automatically); the scratch source is then removed. `install_stack_service()` finds the real console user (`find_console_user()`: macOS `stat -f%Su /dev/console`, Linux `logname`/`$SUDO_USER`) - never root, since the Stack spawns engines that need a real GUI session's Metal/GPU access, the one asymmetry from Home's own root/system service; creates `stack/data` owner-only (`0700`) and chowns the whole `stack/` tree to that user; persists the username to `stack/.user` so `uninstall.sh` (running as root) can find it later; picks a second free port with the same `find_free_port()` Home's own `APP_PORT` already uses; drops privileges for exactly one step, `sudo -u "$STACK_USER" env STACK_DATA_DIR=... PORT=... STACK_BUN_BIN=... <binary> install-service` (Linux additionally: `loginctl enable-linger`); polls `/healthz` for the shipped version.
