Only once that answers does it write `engines.stack.url` through the new `backend/scripts/set-setting.ts` (a one-shot script in `restore-drill.ts`'s own shape, calling `setHouseholdSettingValue()` directly against the not-yet-started database, no HTTP) - the last thing this whole sequence does, never the first, so a Stack that never comes up leaves the setting empty and Home boots on its own built-in supervisors exactly as HOME-STACK-02b's own safe default already guarantees.

**Never fatal to the Home install itself**: every step above is checked explicitly and returns 1 on failure rather than being left to `set -e` - a real gotcha found live, since `-e`'s early-exit-on-failure is suppressed not just for a tested command's own exit status but for everything *inside* a function called under `if ! setup_stack ...; then`, including commands that are not the function's last one. `main()` wraps the whole sequence the same way, logging "Continuing without the Stack" rather than aborting Home's own install.

A rule for every installer script in this repo, not obvious from `set -euo pipefail`'s own man-page description, proven with the smallest repro that shows it rather than trusted from reading bash's own docs:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
inner() { echo "inner: before"; false; echo "inner: after (should not print)"; }
outer() { echo "outer: before"; inner; echo "outer: after (should not print)"; }
if ! outer; then echo "caught failure, script continues"; fi
echo "script did not abort"
```

Every line prints, including both "should not print" ones - `false` inside `inner()` does not stop `inner()`'s own next line, and `inner()`'s own failure does not stop `outer()`'s own next line either, because the entire call tree is running inside a tested conditional (`if ! outer`). This is the opposite of what "`-e` aborts on the first failing command" leads you to expect: once ANY command in a chain is being tested (an `if`, a `!`, an `&&`/`||` other than the last), `-e` stops mid-call as if it were never set, not just at the top level - it does not resume enforcing early-exit again once you're inside a function that a conditional is watching. Any function in `install.sh`/`uninstall.sh` meant to fail soft (return 1 and let the caller decide, rather than take the whole script down) has to check and return after every command that matters, by hand - `-e` will not do it for you inside that function, no matter how deeply nested.

**Uninstall** (`uninstall.sh`) reads `stack/.user` back, adds `stack/data` to the one existing data-deletion confirmation (`DELETE MY DATA` alongside `data/`, `backups/`, `received-backups/` - one all-or-nothing choice, not a second prompt), and either way calls `maipai-stack uninstall-service` as that user afterward - with `--remove-data` only when confirmed, matching `daemon.ts`'s own "Service removed, data kept" / "Service and data removed" contract exactly, so this script never separately `rm -rf`s `stack/data` itself.

**Upgrade** (`install.sh`'s existing `upgrading=yes` branch): the Stack's own service is stopped first (its binary lives inside `stack/`, which the upgrade's `rsync --delete` would otherwise touch) if a `.user` marker is found; `stack/` is added to that rsync's own exclude list alongside `data/`/`backups/`/`received-backups/` (real runtime state, never part of a release tarball - without the exclude, `--delete` would remove the existing `stack/` directory on every upgrade, since Home's own release tarball never contains one); `setup_stack()` then runs again unconditionally, rebuilding from whatever `STACK_TAG` this release pins and reinstalling the service - `engines.stack.url` gets rewritten to the same value when the port hasn't changed (a deliberate simplification against the design's own "not rewritten unless the port changed" - harmless, since `set-setting.ts` writing an unchanged value is a no-op in every way that matters, and avoiding it would need a read-then-compare this script has no other reason to do).

**`--dry-run`**: prints the Stack half's entire plan (fetch, build, the exact `install-service` command line with every env var, the healthz poll target, the settings-write command) against real values for the actual machine, with no root, no network call beyond nothing, no filesystem writes - and exits before touching Home's own pre-existing fetch/build/service-install flow, which never supported a dry run before this item and does not gain one here (a real, stated scope boundary, not an oversight: a script that claims to simulate its own existing half while still running it for real would be worse than not offering the flag). `render_stack_binary_name()` and `stack_install_service_command()` are the two pure, testable pieces the dry-run and the real path both call, so their tests hold the same assertion either way.

**A real bug found wiring this up, fixed in `getmaipai/stack`, not here**: `build-binary.sh`'s own `OUT_DIR` handling silently broke when given an absolute path (prefixing a stray `../`, which this installer always does - its own `OUT_DIR` is `${install_root}/stack`) - the binary compiled to a path that was never created. Fixed upstream (`getmaipai/stack@233bc4f`, `STACK_TAG` bumped to it), verified by rebuilding with both a relative and an absolute `OUT_DIR` before trusting either.

**Two review rounds found eight real bugs total, all fixed here, none in the live-verified run this section opens with** (that run happened before either round; the whole sequence was re-verified live again after every fix - see Verification):

**Round one:**

- **`main()` silently never ran under this script's own documented `curl -fsSL ... | bash` usage.** The sourced-vs-executed guard was `[[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]`, which looks right and is wrong for piped execution specifically: bash reading a script from a pipe sets `BASH_SOURCE[0]` empty and `$0` to `"bash"`, so the comparison is false and `main()` never runs - the installer would exit 0 having installed nothing, for the exact command this file tells a household to paste. Confirmed with `echo 'echo "[${BASH_SOURCE[0]}] [$0]"' | bash` printing `[] [bash]`. Fixed with the portable `(return 0 2>/dev/null)` "am I sourced" test instead, which does not depend on how the script was invoked - proven against direct execution, piped execution, and `bash install.sh` all three before trusting it.
- **`find_console_user()` on darwin accepted `root` as a valid console user.** `stat -f%Su /dev/console` answers `"root"` when nobody is logged into the console - a real state (a headless Mac reached only over SSH, or the gap between a logout and the next login), not a theoretical one - and the only guard downstream was "non-empty," which `"root"` satisfies. The Stack would have installed and run as root, exactly what this function exists to prevent. Fixed: `find_console_user()` itself now treats `root` as no answer.
- **`uninstall.sh` could silently leave `stack/data` on disk even after `DELETE MY DATA`.** The Stack-detection block conflated "found a Stack install" with "its binary is still executable," clearing `STACK_USER` to empty - and with it, `stack/data`'s own place in the one confirmation - the moment the binary check failed (a lost execute bit, a partial reinstall: real states). Fixed: found-ness (the `.user` marker) and binary-usability are now tracked separately; `stack/data` is still offered and still deleted (directly, since there is no usable binary to run `uninstall-service` through) even when the binary itself is gone, with a clear note that the service registration needs removing by hand in that case. The same fix folded in a DRY cleanup the review also flagged: `uninstall.sh` now sources `install.sh` for `detect_os`/`detect_arch`/`render_stack_binary_name` instead of a second, inline OS/arch mapping that could drift from the real one.
- **`engines.stack.url` was unconditionally overwritten on every install and upgrade.** A household that pointed it at a remote or hand-run Stack through the settings UI would have that choice silently clobbered back to this installer's own local port on the next upgrade. Fixed: `set-setting.ts` gained `--only-if-empty-or-prefix <prefix>`, and `install_stack_service()` passes `http://127.0.0.1:` - only ever touching a value this installer plausibly wrote itself.
- **A failed upgrade rebuild could leave `engines.stack.url` pointing at a Stack that no longer exists.** `main()`'s upgrade branch stops the running Stack before the rsync (it has to - the binary lives inside the tree being replaced); if `setup_stack()` then fails to rebuild or restart it, the setting still held the old value, so Home would see the Stack as merely offline rather than falling back cleanly to its own supervisors. Fixed: that failure path now clears the setting (best-effort, using the same `--only-if-empty-or-prefix` guard, so it only ever clears a value this installer itself would have set).
- **`ensure_service_user_linux()`'s own recursive `chown` would have clobbered the Stack's ownership on every Linux install.** Called after `setup_stack()` (which chowns `stack/` to the console user, on purpose - the whole point of that user is that it isn't the headless `${SERVICE_USER}` account), its `chown -R "${SERVICE_USER}:${SERVICE_USER}" "$INSTALL_ROOT_LINUX"` covered the entire install root with no exclusion, silently handing `stack/` back to `${SERVICE_USER}` moments after `setup_stack()` gave it away. Not flagged by the review (this session has no Linux box for it to run against); found re-reading the two functions' own ordering while fixing the review's other findings. Fixed: the chown now excludes `stack/` explicitly. Static, not live-verified - named again in Verification's own stated gap below.

**Round two, on the fix-hunks from round one:**

- **`--dry-run` made a real network call, contradicting its own documented "no network" guarantee.** `install_stack_service()` called `find_free_port()` unconditionally, before the dry-run branch's own early return - `port_in_use()`'s own `/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/<port>` probe is a real loopback socket connection, real activity in a network-sandboxed environment (a CI runner, a container with loopback namespaced) even though nothing was ever actually installed. Fixed: `find_free_port()` now runs only past the dry-run check; the dry-run output shows the base port (`STACK_PORT_BASE`) with a note that a real run may pick a higher one. Locked in with a test that stubs `find_free_port()` to fail loudly and asserts it is never called during `--dry-run` - a stronger guard than reading the source, since it would catch the call being reintroduced anywhere in the dry-run path, not just at today's call site.
- **The "shared" dry-run/real command was not actually shared.** `stack_install_service_command()`'s own comment claimed the dry-run log line and the real `sudo -u .../env ...` invocation ran "the identical command," but the real path hand-duplicated the same four env-var assignments a second time instead of building from that function - exactly the kind of thing that can silently drift (an env var added to one and not the other) while every existing test kept passing. Fixed: `stack_install_service_argv()` (new) is the one source of the argv, as newline-separated tokens; `stack_install_service_command()` (the dry-run's own readable line) and the real `sudo -u "$stack_user" env` call now both build from it, the latter via a `while read` loop into an array.

**A "while read into an array," not `mapfile`/`readarray`, and why it matters everywhere in this repo, not just here**: fixing the DRY duplication above first used `mapfile`, bash 4's built-in for exactly this. It worked in this session's own shell and failed the moment it was run under `/bin/bash` directly - macOS ships bash 3.2.57 as `/usr/bin/env bash`'s own system default (Apple has not shipped a newer one in years, for GPLv3 licensing reasons) and does not have `mapfile` at all. This script's own shebang, `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, resolves to exactly that 3.2 binary on an unmodified Mac - this installer's own primary target - unless a household happens to have a newer bash from Homebrew ahead of it on `PATH`, which cannot be assumed. Every function in `install.sh`/`uninstall.sh` (and, by the same reasoning, any future installer-adjacent script in this repo meant to run on a bare Mac) needs to stay bash-3.2-compatible: no `mapfile`/`readarray`, no associative arrays (`declare -A`), no `${var,,}`/`${var^^}` case conversion. Arrays themselves, `+=`, `[[ ]]`, and process substitution (`< <(...)`) are all fine - only the bash-4-and-later builtins are the trap. Found live, by literally running the fix under `/bin/bash --version` and watching it fail with `mapfile: command not found`, not by reading a compatibility table.

**Verification**: `bash -n` clean on both scripts, and the whole suite re-run under `/bin/bash` (the real system default, not whatever `bash` a dev shell's own `PATH` happens to prefer) after the bash-3.2 fix, not just under a newer one. `scripts/install.test.ts` (10 tests) and `backend/tests/setSetting.test.ts` (6 tests, `set-setting.ts` run as a real separate process against a scratch `MAIPAI_DATA_DIR` - round one's own finding that the only prior coverage was a dry-run string, never the write path itself): `render_stack_binary_name()` against `build-binary.sh`'s own naming, `stack_install_service_command()`'s exact env-var line, `find_console_user()` on darwin (a real console user, and root refused) and its Linux `logname`-fails-falls-through-to-`$SUDO_USER` path (forced deterministically with a same-named shell function, since `logname` itself succeeds even under a non-interactive `spawnSync` on this dev machine), `detect_os`/`detect_arch`, the full `--dry-run` output's own structure, `--dry-run` making no network call (round two's own fix, proven with a stubbed `find_free_port()` that fails loudly if called - confirmed to actually catch the regression by reintroducing the bug and watching the test fail before restoring the fix), `main()` actually running under piped execution (round one's own regression, reproduced by piping the real file into `bash` rather than invoking it as a file argument - the one way a test can actually catch this class of bug), `set-setting.ts`'s real write, its `--only-if-empty-or-prefix` skip and overwrite cases, and its exit codes on a bad key or missing arguments. `bash scripts/check.sh` green (`(cd scripts && bun test)` is part of that gate already; the new `backend/tests/setSetting.test.ts` runs with the rest of the backend suite, 3612/3612). Full real user-level run on this MacBook, never Home's own root-level service, done before round one and re-run twice more after - once post-round-one, once post-round-two, the second one calling `install_stack_service()` directly under `/bin/bash` (not `bash install.sh` from a dev shell) so the bash-3.2 fix was proven under the exact binary a household's Mac actually has: a compiled Stack binary built via `getmaipai/stack`'s own `build-binary.sh`, `install-service` with a scratch `STACK_DATA_DIR`/`PORT 8770`/`STACK_BUN_BIN`, `/healthz` answering, `status` showing every one of those env vars baked into the running LaunchAgent's own `environment` block, `engines.stack.url` written, then `uninstall-service --remove-data`, `launchctl list | grep maipai` empty, the data directory gone. Out of scope, a stated gap rather than an unproven claim: a real clean-account install (this session's own account, not a fresh one) and the entire Linux path (`systemd --user`, `loginctl enable-linger`, `find_console_user()`'s `logname` branch, and the `ensure_service_user_linux()` ordering fix above) - the render functions are unit-tested and `service/systemd.ts`'s own tests on the `getmaipai/stack` side cover the unit content, but nothing here has run on a real Linux box.

## The chat program: artifact data layer and the first structured parts (2026-09-21)

The design record is `docs/plans/shell-on-shadcndashboard-2026-09-21.md` (the org's 2026-09-21 "no hand-built UI" rule: Home's shell is `shadcndashboard`, the chat is assistant-ui Elements, both used exactly as shipped). This session's own row: the assistant-ui Elements' wiring contract (item 1), the artifact spec record and Home's half of it (item 2), and the first two generative-UI producers (item 4's weather/almanac half).

**The wire the Elements expect**: read every assistant-ui Element on this session's row (assistant-ui.com/elements) and set its exact part/prop shape against Home's turn stream today - fed, rename, or gap, table in the plan doc. Two real product decisions surfaced and were resolved by the coordinator rather than guessed: approval-card needs both a same-turn gate (the live tool call, `respondToApproval()`) AND Home's existing async decide-it-later queue (`approvals.ts`) for a cross-person decision, kept as two distinct kinds; guardrail-notice is a named gap for a later spec bump (title/explanation/policy/alternatives on `SafetyResult`, the message marked `incomplete`/`content-filter`), nothing built yet.

**The artifact record** (`spec-v0.1.7`, `spec/schemas/artifact.schema.json`): one immutable version of a generated markdown/code/html document - `id, conversation_id, turn_id, kind, title, body, version, parent_version, created_by, provenance, created_at, hlc`. Chains by `parent_version` naming the prior version's own `id` - conversation-turn's `parent_turn_id` convention, deliberately not `TurnArtifact`'s bare `revision` counter (COMP-01's unrelated evidence-grounded details document), because the wire needs a version's own id for the artifact-card/canvas-split tool call and the message metadata. `records/ts/validate.ts`/`records/py/validate.py` gained `validateArtifact`/`validate_artifact` (a self-chain guard and version/parent_version pairing - a medium review on the first cut found the self-chain gap unguarded, the same class of bug `validateEntity`'s own `parent_id` check already exists for) with matching `fixtures/validation/cross-field.json` cases proving both languages agree.

Home's half: `backend/src/db/schema.ts`'s `artifacts` table (migration `0053`) adds two Home-internal columns the spec record has no concept of - `artifactKey` (minted once at version 1, copied onto every later version, groups one chain) and `isCurrent` (a partial unique index keeps exactly one current row per `artifactKey`, flipped inside the same transaction `updateArtifact()` uses to insert the next version). `lib/artifacts.ts`: `createArtifact`/`updateArtifact` (refuses updating a superseded version, 409), `getArtifactRow`/`currentArtifactRow`, and `visibleArtifactRow()` - a child sees an artifact only from their own turn and only when that turn's `safetyAction !== "refuse"`, extending `canAccessPerson()`'s existing "own turns only" rule rather than a content-stripping projection (unlike `TurnArtifact`'s child projection, there is no field to strip here - the whole version is visible or it isn't). `routes/artifacts.ts`: `GET /api/artifacts/:id` and `GET /api/artifacts/:id/export` (a slugged-filename download, content type by `kind`) - read-only, since creating and updating happens through the turn-engine tool, never a route. `TurnValue.artifact?: {id, version}` added additively next to `document_available`, no writer yet (see the gap below). Forgot `artifacts` in `lib/hlc.ts`'s `HLC_BEARING_TABLES` on the first pass - the full suite's own `tests/hlc.test.ts` caught it immediately, fixed before landing.

**The turn-engine tool, a real gap named rather than shoehorned in**: every native tool call in `turnEngine.ts`'s `resolveToolCallsInOrder()` assumes a real catalog package (every check reads `rankedById.get(c.tool)!.manifest`), and a Tier 1 `handler.ts` has zero DB access (an isolated Deno subprocess). The sanctioned way a package writes a real structured record is a recipe primitive (`remember`'s own `"op": "remember"`, implemented identically in both interpreters against the shared `Host` interface) - giving the model a live artifact tool the sanctioned way needs an 18th recipe op spanning `commons/spec`'s TS and Python interpreters plus a real `packageHost.ts` implementation, not a same-item change. Filed as `docs/BACKLOG.md`'s **ARTIFACT-02**, next up for this session, high review (it spans three files' worth of behavioral parity).

**Weather and almanac-date as structured parts** (the generative-UI contract's first two producers - "no weather card, chart or component is created anywhere in Home or the kit"): `wire.ts`'s new `StructuredPart` type (`spec_sheet` kind today - `title`, `subtitle?`, `rows: {label, value, emphasis?}[]`, identical to assistant-ui's own spec-sheet prop shape on purpose, so the frontend passes it straight through) and `TurnValue.structured_part`. `composer.ts`'s `structuredPartForOutcomes()` maps weather's and almanac-date's own `result.data` (already typed facts, never model prose) onto it - first known producer wins among succeeded outcomes, the same precedent `buildDocument()` already sets for `TurnArtifact` sections. `almanac-date/handler.ts` gained a `data: {date, weekday}` field (Tier 1 handlers already pass `data` through per `denoHost.ts`'s `parseHandleResult()` - no plumbing change needed). Hooked into `turnEngine.ts`'s `logTurnSafely()` - the one choke point every `runTurn()`/`runTurnStream()` finalize site already routes through for `document_available`/`rung` - as one more unconditional line, no new dispatch, no risk to the tool-calling pipeline itself.

**Two more real gaps, checked before being built rather than rushed in, filed as their own `docs/BACKLOG.md` items** (**REASONING-01**: the reasoning Element's stream event is entangled with `wellFormed.ts`'s `<think>`-block reattachment deep in `turnEngine.ts`'s streaming buffer logic - understand why that reattachment exists before extracting it; **image generation**: no image-generation feature exists in Home yet at all - "image" is a role id in the Engines API's list and nothing else - so the image job's part sequence is `CHAT-MEDIA-01`'s own item, not a wiring task, with a one-line pointer added there to the `image-generation` Element's own contract and its missing numeric-progress prop).

**Verification**: `spec`'s own `bun test` (504/504) and `pytest` (240/240) after the artifact schema/validator/fixtures landed; `spec`'s full `bash scripts/check.sh` (core, ui, spec workspaces plus the standards core) green. Backend: `tests/artifacts.test.ts` (8, version chaining and the child-safety gate), `tests/artifactsRoutes.test.ts` (5, the two routes including a 404 for someone else's artifact), 9 new `composer.test.ts` cases for `structuredPartForOutcomes()`, `almanac-date/handler_test.ts`'s own 3 Deno tests (run directly, matching `smoke.ts`'s real `deno test --no-check --allow-read=<dir> --cached-only` invocation). Full backend suite green, 3625/3625, run three times to separate real signal from noise: run 1 caught this item's own `HLC_BEARING_TABLES` gap (fixed before landing); run 2 failed a different, unrelated test (`turnEngine.test.ts`'s own Cosmo 7 lookup case, passes clean in isolation - two full gates on the machine at once, per the coordinator) confirmed pre-existing flakiness by run 3's clean 3625/3625, not a regression from this diff.

## ARTIFACT-02, designed (2026-09-21)

The recipe-primitive design `docs/BACKLOG.md`'s ARTIFACT-02 item names was worked out in full before any code was written, then approved by the coordinator with one addition (provenance) - recorded here verbatim so a fresh session builds it cold rather than re-deriving it, per this repo's own "at a stop point, make the state durable" rule.

**Why a recipe primitive, not a native tool-call path**: traced `turnEngine.ts`'s `resolveToolCallsInOrder()` line by line - every check (`offeredIds.has`/`rankedById.has`, duplicate, cap, `validatePackageArgs`, `manifest.consequential`, `isActionPackage`) reads `rankedById.get(c.tool)!.manifest`, a real `PackageManifest` from a loaded, ranked catalog package. There is no branch anywhere in that function for a tool that isn't one. A Tier 1 `handler.ts` looked like an alternative until reading `packages/almanac-date/handler.ts`'s own header: "This file has NO import from anywhere outside its own directory" - it runs as an isolated Deno subprocess over MCP stdio, zero access to `db` or any `lib/` module, so it structurally cannot write an artifact version itself. The one place a package already writes a real structured record live is a recipe primitive: `remember`'s own `"op": "remember"` step, implemented identically in `interpreters/ts/recipe-interpreter.ts` and `interpreters/py/recipe_interpreter.py` (the file's own header: "must stay behaviorally identical... the conformance fixtures prove that"), calling a method on the shared `Host` interface that `packageHost.ts` implements for real. An 18th op, `artifact`, follows that exact precedent instead of forking the validation logic `resolveToolCallsInOrder()` already owns - "one definition, one place."

**The step and its one new pattern**: `{"op": "artifact", "as": "result", "title": "{title}", "kind": "{kind}", "body": "{body}", "id_from": "artifact_id"}`. `title`/`kind`/`body` interpolate normally. `id_from` is the one new idea, and it is small: it names a scope variable to read DIRECTLY (`scope[step.id_from]`, no `{}`), the same bare-name convention `pick`'s own `"from"` field already uses - not `interpolate()`'s templating path, because `interpolate()` leaves an unresolved `{name}` as the literal string `{name}` rather than `undefined`, which cannot tell "the model omitted `artifact_id`" apart from "the model's own answer happened to be that string." Whether `scope.artifact_id` is defined is exactly the create-vs-update discriminator the op needs, and the recipe language has no conditional to express that any other way. `title`/`kind`/`body` stay always-required in `write_document`'s own args (even on an update, where `kind` is ignored and the model just resends its own `title`) specifically to avoid needing the same optional-interpolation problem a second time for no real benefit.

**Host and host method**: `Host.artifact` (`host-emulator.ts`): `create({title, kind, body}): {id, version}`, `update({artifact_id, title, body}): {id, version}`, throwing `HostError` with an existing `errors/errors.json` code (`not_found`, `invalid_input`) rather than a new one. A deterministic in-memory version on both language emulators for the conformance fixtures. New permission `artifact:write` in `vocab/permissions.json`, one line matching every existing entry's own shape.

**Provenance (the coordinator's one addition to the original draft)**: `host.artifact.create`/`update`'s real implementation (`packageHost.ts`) sets `provenance` with the identical expression `remember()` already uses for `source` - `turnId ?? \`package:${manifest.id}\`` - so a document's provenance names the real turn (or the non-turn package invocation) that wrote it, not a bespoke string invented for this one op. `conversation_id` is resolved by looking up the bound `turnId`'s own row - real DB access, the thing a Tier 1 handler could never do, which is the entire reason this is a Host method and not a sandboxed handler.

**Wiring the result back**: the op binds two FLAT scope keys directly, `scope.artifact_id`/`scope.artifact_version` (never a nested `result.id` - `interpolate()` has no dot-path support, and every existing step's own `data` mapping already only reads flat top-level scope vars). The bundled `documents` package's recipe: the `artifact` step, then a `format` step whose `data` is `{"artifact_id": "{artifact_id}", "artifact_version": "{artifact_version}"}` - the exact shape `composer.ts`'s `structuredPartForOutcomes()` already reads weather's and almanac-date's own `result.data` from, so `TurnValue.artifact` (landed this session, additive, no writer until this item) gets its writer the identical way those two got their structured-part producer. Tool name `write_document`, matching what artifact-card's own frontend toolkit already binds to, so nothing extra needs registering on that side.

**Not started**: no code for any of this exists yet. The next session's brief is this section plus `docs/BACKLOG.md`'s ARTIFACT-02 item (same content, the pickup-ready checklist form) and `commons/docs/dev/session-b.md`'s own handoff note.

## ARTIFACT-02, landed (2026-09-21)

Built as designed above; `docs/BACKLOG.md`'s own item carries the naming and ownership-check notes verbatim. One thing found only by running the full suite, not by reading: `write_document`'s manifest first declared `routing.always_offer: true`, copying `websearch`'s own pattern on the assumption that a document-writing request is as open-ended as a web search. It isn't - `selectOfferedTools()` puts every `always_offer` package on literally every turn's Tier 2 candidate list regardless of embedding score, and adding a fourth always-offered tool (`recall`, `remember`, `websearch` were the only three before this) shifted enough ranking margins to fail 3-5 unrelated tests (`LOOKUP-01`, `hub-named-it`, an "engine: the read on both paths" case) that were tuned against the existing three-tool offered set. Removed: `write_document` earns its place through `routing.examples` and normal Tier 2 ranking like every other action package, the same as `list-add`/`remember`/`lock-doors`. If a future package genuinely needs `always_offer`, budget a full-suite run afterward specifically to catch this class of cross-package ranking shift - a package's own tests passing proves nothing about it.

Two more things a review found before this landed for real. First, `packageHost.ts`'s `artifact.create`/`update` throw `not_found` up front when `turnId` is unbound (the design's own `turnId ?? package:${manifest.id}` provenance expression, copied from `remember()`, would have been dead code here - `turn_id` is a required FK on the Artifact record, unlike `remember()`'s free-text `source`, so there is no fallback shape to fall back TO): provenance is simply `turnId`, guaranteed bound by that same throw, not the `??` expression the design doc above still shows verbatim as `remember()`'s own precedent. Second, and more load-bearing: the design's own wiring section describes `TurnValue.artifact` getting "its writer the identical way" `weather`/`almanac-date` got `structured_part`'s - that writer didn't exist until this pass added it. `lib/composer.ts`'s `artifactForOutcomes()` (a sibling to `structuredPartForOutcomes()`, not a case folded into it - `TurnValue.artifact` and `structured_part` are different wire fields) reads a succeeded `write_document` outcome's own `result.data.artifact_id`/`artifact_version`, and `turnEngine.ts`'s `logTurnSafely()` sets `value.artifact` from it right beside the `structured_part` line. Without this, the recipe and the host would have worked and every test would have stayed green while the acceptance criterion's own "`TurnValue.artifact` gets set from the real tool call" silently never happened - caught by a review reading `wire.ts`'s own field comment ("No writer yet... a separate integration"), not by any test, since the bundled package's own unit tests only ever checked the plugin's raw `result.data`, never the turn-level field the wire promises it.

## REASONING-01, the streaming buffer explained (2026-09-21, part 1 - read only, no code)

BACKLOG's own contract: `reasoning` (`assistant-ui.com/elements/reasoning`) binds to `TurnStreamEvent`'s own gap, named in `docs/plans/shell-on-shadcndashboard-2026-09-21.md`'s wire table - a new additive event `{ type: "reasoning"; text: string; sequence?: number }`, alongside `delta`. Read `turnEngine.ts`'s streaming path end to end (`composeBlocking`, `gateOutputSafety`/`gateGuards`, `holdOpening`, `holdForLookup`'s mid-stream `<think>` handling) and `wellFormed.ts`'s `visibleText()`/`thinkingPrefix()` before writing any of this - this section is that read, and the smallest-change proposal it points to.

### The one representation every function already agrees on

`wellFormed.ts` owns two regexes and nothing else: `THINK_BLOCK_RE` (`<think>...</think>`, closed) and `OPEN_THINK_RE` (an unclosed `<think>` running to end of string - a generation cut off mid-reasoning). `visibleText(text)` strips both; `thinkingPrefix(text)` extracts both (closed blocks joined, then any trailing open one) and calls the result a "prefix" by convention, not by enforcement - nothing here checks that a think block is actually first, it just always is in practice, because the chat template puts it there.

Every producer of a `TurnValue.reply.text` - `runTurn()`'s blocking path, `runTurnStream()`'s `finalize()`, the stored conversation-turn row, the row reloaded on a page refresh - treats that string as "the model's raw completion, think block included, if the model made one." Nothing strips it before storage. The ONE place it gets stripped is the frontend (`chatModelAdapter.ts`, #20), which parses the same tags back out for display. So the contract every function in this pipeline is already honoring, whether it says so or not, is: **`reply.text` (and every intermediate variable that will become it) may carry a leading think block; call `visibleText()`/`thinkingPrefix()` when you need to reason about just one half.** `repairReply()` is the cleanest example: it splits, repairs only the visible half, and reassembles `thinking + visible` - the block is never judged, never regenerated, never touched, just carried.

### Where a think block currently does and doesn't hold the wire

`openingReleases()` (the opening hold both paths share) treats a think block as free: it computes `visibleText(buffer)` and releases only once the VISIBLE portion clears its own threshold (two words, a sentence boundary, or 40 chars) - a think block on its own never satisfies that, so the block does not, by itself, trigger release. Its own safety valve is a RAW character bound (`OPENING_HOLD_MAX_RAW_CHARS`, 400): if the model is still inside an unusually long think block at 400 raw characters, the opening hold releases anyway, mid-block, with whatever it has (an open, unclosed `<think>` in the released chunk).

That safety valve is the fork in the road for everything downstream:

- **Short/ordinary think block** (closes before 400 raw chars, which is the common case): `holdOpening()`'s single released chunk already contains the WHOLE closed think block plus the first slice of visible text, glued together, because it was all sitting in `holdOpening()`'s own internal buffer when release fired. Nothing arrived at the wire "as it was generated" - it arrives all at once, retroactively, the moment the opening hold's visible-side condition is met.
- **Long think block** (still open past 400 raw chars): `holdOpening()` releases early with the still-open block, then stops buffering entirely and yields every subsequent delta as it arrives, live, one at a time (the `released` branch, `yield step.value`). From this point on, whatever comes next - the rest of the think block, then the visible reply - really does stream token by token to whatever's downstream.

`holdForLookup()` (the LOOKUP-01 hold, layered directly on top of `holdOpening()`'s output) is built for exactly this fork. Its own `inThink` flag exists for the SECOND case: when a chunk arrives live during an open think block (no `</think>` yet), it passes that chunk straight through unheld (`yield step.value`) and stays in `inThink` mode, watching subsequent live deltas for the close tag; once found, it slices the chunk at the boundary, forwards everything through the close, and resets its own `buffer` to just the tail after `</think>` - clean, pure visible text from that point on. In the FIRST case (the common one), the very first chunk `holdForLookup` ever sees already has both tags closed, so its `<think>-open-but-not-closed` check is simply false and it falls straight through to treating the chunk as ordinary buffer content - `buffer` at that point still has the closed think block sitting at its front, unstripped.

That's the whole explanation for the one reattachment this item was filed to understand: `holdForLookup`'s household-subject-promise-drop branch (`yield \`${thinkingPrefix(buffer)}${rest}\``) recovers whatever think content is STILL sitting in `buffer` (non-empty only in the common, first-chunk-had-both-tags case) and re-glues it to the front of the edited visible text, so dropping a promise sentence from the VISIBLE reply never silently deletes the model's reasoning too. In the live/incremental case, `buffer` is already pure visible text by the time this branch runs (the think content already streamed through and was reset out of `buffer` when `inThink` closed), so `thinkingPrefix(buffer)` correctly returns "" there - not dead code in either case, just two different states of the same variable depending on which fork fired.

The blocking path's own two reattachment sites (`composeBlocking`'s caller, `rawText = \`${thinkingPrefix(rawText)}${withoutSentences(...)}\``, twice) are the non-streaming twin of the identical problem: `withoutSentences()`/`withoutPromise()` only ever operate on `visibleReply` (never `rawText`), so re-gluing `thinkingPrefix(rawText)` back onto their result is what keeps the edit from silently discarding the model's own reasoning, the same as the streaming case.

### Guard and safety checks see the WHOLE thing, on purpose (as far as this read can tell)

`gateOutputSafety()` (the streaming per-sentence safety gate) and `guardSentence()`'s callers on both paths run on raw, unstripped text - `splitIntoSentences(rawText)` on the blocking path's guard precheck, and `gateOutputSafety`'s own sentence chunker on the streaming path - not on `visibleText()`'s output. Neither function has any `<think>` awareness at all. This means a model's own reasoning is currently classified for safety and judged by the guard system exactly like visible reply content - a `<think>` block that mentions something the safety classifier flags could refuse the WHOLE reply today, even if the visible text that would have followed was completely fine, and a guard rule (`banned_phrase`, register, repeat-reply) can fire on something the model only ever "thought," never said.

The ONE place that deliberately reads visible-only text instead is LOOKUP-01/02's own promise-read (`readLookupDraft(visibleReply, ...)` / `readLookupDraft(visibleHeld, ...)`), with its own comment explaining why: "The visible reply, never a think block's own 'let me check what I know'" - the model's internal self-talk about looking something up is not a promise made TO the household, so treating it as one would be wrong. This is a deliberate, narrow exception, not a general "guards only see visible text" rule.

**Decided (coordinator, 2026-09-21): safety/guard-checking the raw combined text is intentional and stays exactly as it is.** The reasoning Element shows this text to a person; it is content the household will read, not private scratch space, so it gets the identical safety and guard pass every other word of the reply gets - no resolver pass needed, no change to `gateOutputSafety()`/`gateGuards()` at all.

**Also decided: a child's turn never emits the `reasoning` event.** A child sees the answer, not the model's thinking - the reasoning content is dropped at the same wire boundary that splits it out, never sent to a child's own client at all (not redacted, not a placeholder - absent, the same way a package a child's manifest doesn't grant simply never appears). Safety scanning above is unaffected: the drop happens at the OUTPUT boundary, after the combined text has already gone through the identical, unchanged safety/guard pass every actor's turn gets.

### The retry-token machinery

Every regeneration - `composeBlocking`'s `shapeModelText()`, the blocking-path malformed-retry, `holdOpening()`'s own nested retry - forces `thinking: false` and caps the retry at `RETRY_TOKEN_CAP` (48 tokens). The reason is explicit in the code: under a 48-token cap, a real think block WOULD BE the entire budget, leaving nothing for a visible answer at all - and if thinking were left on and the tiny cap cut generation mid-block, `visibleText()`'s `OPEN_THINK_RE` would correctly report empty visible text, `assessReply()` would call that "empty," and the retry would have produced an unusable non-answer needing a THIRD generation this design explicitly refuses to allow ("its own repair stands, never a third try"). Forcing `thinking: false` sidesteps the whole failure mode by construction: a tiny-cap regeneration is guaranteed to spend its entire budget on a real, visible, gradeable attempt.

This machinery already proves the truncated-think-block case matters and is handled: `repairTail()`'s own comment ("nothing visible to repair (a think block alone)") and `isShortMalformed()`/`assessReply()` both key off `visibleText()`, so a generation that stops mid-block (this item's third required test case) is already, today, correctly treated as producing no visible text - REASONING-01 does not need to invent this handling, only avoid breaking it.

### The smallest change

Nothing above needs to change. Every function this section covers - `wellFormed.ts`'s primitives, `composeBlocking`, `gateOutputSafety`/`gateGuards`, `holdOpening`, `holdForLookup`, the retry machinery, `finalize()`, `logTurnSafely()` - keeps operating on the combined raw text exactly as it does today, in exactly the same order, with exactly the same reattachments. `fullText` (`routes/turn.ts`'s `streamTurnEvents()`) keeps accumulating the unmodified `current.value` chunks `result.tokens` yields, and `finalize(fullText.trim(), ...)` keeps building `TurnValue.reply.text` exactly as it does today, think block embedded - the STORED row and the blocking path's own reply shape are unaffected end to end.

The one new thing is a stateful pass added at the OUTERMOST boundary only - `streamTurnEvents()`, right where each `current.value` chunk currently becomes one unconditional `{ type: "delta", text: current.value }` (`routes/turn.ts:301`) - built as `wellFormed.ts`'s own new `feedThinkSplit()`/`flushThinkSplit()` functions, split each chunk into its think-tagged and visible spans as it emits wire events: a think span becomes `{ type: "reasoning", text }`, a visible span keeps becoming `{ type: "delta", text }`, both carrying their own `sequence`. `fullText` still accumulates from `current.value` (untouched, pre-split), so `finalize()` sees no difference at all.

**Correction (a review caught this): `feedThinkSplit()` mirrors `holdForLookup()`'s own `inThink` state machine (the identical two tag tests, the same close-boundary slicing) - it does not call or share code with it.** They are two independent implementations of the same idea, one more (fixing a bug in one does not fix the other), a real, named limitation rather than actual reuse - `wellFormed.ts` is the one shared home for the two tag regexes themselves (`THINK_BLOCK_RE`/`OPEN_THINK_RE`), but the two STATE MACHINES built on top of them are separate. A genuine third copy exists too: `commons`'s `chatCompleteStream()`/`home`'s `stackChatDeltas()` (see "the engine already separates it" below) run their own small `reasoningOpen` synthesis state machine, deliberately kept as a hand-copied "ported here verbatim" pair (the same precedent this file's own header already set before REASONING-01 touched it) rather than a shared export, since the two live in different repos with no existing shared-runtime-code path between them today. Consolidating any of this is a real simplification opportunity for a later pass, not something this item's own scope required.

## REASONING-01, landed (2026-09-21)

Part 1's design held; part 2 surfaced real gaps a high-effort review on each repo caught before this shipped, all fixed before landing. In order of how serious they were:

**`peekAndHandle()`'s tool-call disambiguation broke for a thinking-enabled turn that also offers tools.** `turnEngine.ts`'s own native-tool-calling peek (`resolveToolCalls`'s caller) used to call `.next()` ONCE and treat any non-`done` result as "the model answered in prose, not a tool call" - correct before this item, because a tool-offering completion's reasoning phase yielded NOTHING at all (content stayed empty the whole time, and nothing read `reasoning_content`). Once `llm.ts` started synthesizing real `<think>...` chunks from `reasoning_content`, the very first yielded chunk during a MODEL THAT THINKS BEFORE CALLING A TOOL is now reasoning text, not prose - `peekAndHandle()` would take the "real text" branch immediately, stream the reasoning as if it were the reply, and DROP the tool call entirely once it eventually arrived (logged as `"a streamed reply yielded real text before proposing tool_calls... dropped, never run"`). Fixed: `peekAndHandle()` now peeks PAST any purely-reasoning prefix (using the identical `feedThinkSplit()` state machine, buffering what it reads) before deciding whether the model answered in prose - real tool calls that follow reasoning now resolve correctly again.

**Correction, a second review pass caught this - the scope boundary above understated what actually happens.** When the peeked prefix resolves to a tool call (or to a genuinely empty reply), `buffered` is discarded outright, not merely "not surfaced as a wire event": `composeOrResolve()`'s own `TurnValue` for a plugin/tool-sourced reply is built entirely from the package's own phrased result, with no field that carries the model's pre-tool-call reasoning at all, so it never reaches `fullText`/`finalize()` either - genuine data loss from the stored row, not just from the wire, for this one turn shape. This is a REAL, pre-existing architectural gap, not one this item introduced: any template that leaks `<think>` tags directly into `content` (the fallback shape this file still supports) would have hit the identical peek-order bug before REASONING-01 too, and this fix leaves that turn shape net BETTER than before (the tool call resolves correctly now; before this fix it was dropped with an error log AND the reasoning was shown as if it were the reply, arguably a worse outcome). Fixing the data loss itself would mean deciding where a tool-sourced `TurnValue` stores reasoning that led to it - a real design question (a new field on the plugin outcome? on the turn row?) outside this item's own approved scope (streaming a MODEL reply's reasoning as its own wire event), not a technical ambiguity resolvable by rereading the design. Flagged to the coordinator as a follow-up item rather than silently left findable only by reading this note. `tests/tier2.test.ts` covers both `runTurn()` and `runTurnStream()` reasoning-then-tool-call cases (proving the tool call itself resolves correctly), and `spec/llm/ts/stubServer.ts`'s `scriptedToolCalls` gained a `scriptedReasoning` companion so a test can script the combination at all - neither test asserts on the discarded reasoning text, since asserting "it's gone" was judged not worth a fixture until the follow-up item picks a real destination for it.

**Two production output paths leaked raw reasoning with zero gating.** `routes/openai.ts` (the OpenAI-compatible API external clients like Home Assistant's Conversation integration speak) and `lib/wyomingServer.ts` (the voice-satellite protocol) both forwarded `reply.text`/`result.tokens` straight through - before this item, the live engine never put `<think>` tags in `content` at all, so this was accidentally correct; once `llm.ts` started synthesizing them, both would have started leaking raw `<think>...</think>` text (and, for a minor, actual reasoning content) to any client of either surface. Fixed: `openai.ts` splits and exposes reasoning through the SAME `reasoning_content` field a real llama.cpp reply already uses (this route claims that exact wire contract) for both streaming and non-streaming, minor-gated the identical way the chat route is; `wyomingServer.ts` has no reasoning concept at all, so it strips unconditionally via `visibleText()` - a voice satellite only ever hears the answer. `personaJudge.ts`'s own `JSON.parse(result.value.text)` got a defensive `visibleText()` wrap too: it never requests thinking today (so nothing changes in practice), but a future change flipping that would otherwise break judge parsing with a generic, misattributed error - a review named this exact failure mode.

**`dropReasoning` excluded teen.** The first draft read `actor.role === "child"` directly; every other minor-gated decision in this pipeline (`host.ts`'s chat-models gate, `turnEngine.ts`'s `withholdSensitive`/`mayDefer`, `composer.ts`'s child-only projection) treats child and teen alike via `ageBand.ts`'s shared, birthdate-aware band - the exact "an independent, less accurate signal than the birthdate-based band" bug class that file's own header says it was written to eliminate. Fixed: `dropReasoning: speakerAgeBand(actor, new Date()) !== "adult"`, both in `routes/turn.ts`'s `ResumeSession` construction and `routes/openai.ts`.

**A literal `</think>` inside the engine's own `reasoning_content` could prematurely close the synthesized block.** Reasoning text is never expected to contain real tag markup, but a model reasoning ABOUT markup (or an adversarial completion) could - if it did, `feedThinkSplit()`'s downstream re-parse would treat that as a real close, reclassifying the rest of the reasoning as ordinary `delta`, which is NOT gated by `dropReasoning` (that check only ever filters spans already tagged `reasoning`) - a minor would see the leaked remainder. Fixed: `llm.ts`'s new `neutralizeThinkTags()` breaks the tag SHAPE (not the meaning) inside `reasoning_content` specifically, before it ever reaches the synthesized wrapper - deliberately never applied to `content`, since an engine/template that legitimately leaks real tags into `content` (the fallback shape) must keep working unchanged.

**A whitespace-parity gap between the streamed split and the stored/final text.** `THINK_BLOCK_RE` (the regex `visibleText()`/the stored row use) consumes `\s*` right after a closing `</think>`; `feedThinkSplit()` didn't, so a reply shaped like `<think>...</think>\n\nAnswer` could show a stray leading blank line live-streamed that the final text never has. Fixed: `feedThinkSplit()`/`flushThinkSplit()` now discard that same trailing whitespace, holding it (never emitting it as its own visible span) until either real content or the stream's own end resolves it.

**Not fixed, by design**: the various regex/tag-literal duplications a review named (`THINK_BLOCK_RE`/`OPEN_THINK_RE` vs. `feedThinkSplit()`'s own tag tests vs. `holdForLookup()`'s vs. the two repos' `reasoningOpen` synthesis) are real but pre-existing in kind (this codebase already accepted `stackChatDeltas()` as a deliberate hand-copied port of `chatCompleteStream()` before this item touched either) - consolidating them is a genuine future simplification, not something REASONING-01's own scope required, and touching four call sites across two repos to chase a documentation smell was judged the wrong trade against the item's actual budget.

Tests: `wellFormed.test.ts` (+13: the splitter's own unit coverage, including the whitespace-parity and truncated-block cases), `turnEngine.test.ts` (+4: the four replay tests the work order named - unchanged visible text, the think block as its own event, no block, a truncated block - plus the child/minor-drop test), `tier2.test.ts` (+2: reasoning-then-tool-call on both the blocking and streaming path), `llm.test.ts` (+4: `complete()`/`startCompleteStream()` synthesis, the no-reasoning-engine passthrough, the tag-injection case), `openai.test.ts` (+2: the same synthesis through the external-facing route). Full suites green both repos: `commons` `spec` `bun test` 513/513 (was 509), `home` backend 3679/3679 (was 3667), frontend 506/506, `bash scripts/check.sh` clean in both.

## REASONING-02, landed (2026-09-21): the tool-call reasoning data loss, fixed

The follow-up the second review pass above named: a tool-resolved turn's own reasoning (the text that led the model to call a package) was discarded entirely, not merely hidden from the wire. Fixed by giving `TurnValue` an optional `reasoning` field (`wire.ts`), populated at the exact two places a tool call resolves:

- **Streaming**: `turnEngine.ts`'s `peekAndHandle()` - `buffered` (everything peeked before the tool call resolved, a genuinely open, unclosed think block, since a tool-calling reply never streams the visible span that would have closed it) is run through a new `wellFormed.ts` helper, `extractReasoningText()`, before `composeOrResolve()` runs. That helper is a one-shot `feedThinkSplit()` + `flushThinkSplit()` pass over a whole string - exactly the pipeline `streamTurnEvents()` already drives token-by-token for the live `reasoning` event, so the extracted text is provably "the same string the reasoning event carried," not a second, drifting implementation.
- **Blocking**: `runTurn()`'s own tool-call branch - `completion.value.text` (already carrying a synthesized `<think>` via `llm.ts`'s `withSynthesizedThink()`) gets the identical `extractReasoningText()` treatment before `composeBlocking()` runs.

Both attach via `{ ...resolved, reasoning }` before handing the value into `composeOrResolve()`/`composeBlocking()`, which was verified (not assumed) to survive to the stored/returned value: every transform in the chain (`composeOrResolve()`'s own early returns, `finalizeReply()`, `applyOutputBoundary()`, `enforceWellFormed()`) preserves unknown fields via object spread, with the one deliberate exception being a safety refusal (`applyOutputBoundary()`'s `refuse` branch builds a genuinely fresh `TurnValue` with no producer attribution at all, `reasoning` included - a refused reply dropping the pre-refusal reasoning is the same posture it already takes toward `plugin_id`/`routing`).

**Storage**: `conversationTurns` gained a `reasoning` text column (migration `0055_groovy_expediter.sql`, chained on `0054_chat09_embedding_identity.sql` - see the rebase note below), written by `conversationHistory.ts`'s `logTurn()` from `value.reasoning ?? null` - null for every prose reply, exactly as `stats`/`sources` already work.

**Wire drop for a minor**: the same `dropReasoning`/`speakerAgeBand()` gate the `reasoning` stream event already uses, applied at the two places a `TurnValue` actually crosses onto the wire whole: `routes/turn.ts`'s `streamTurnEvents()` strips it from the `done` event's value, and `POST /api/turn`'s own handler (which serializes the whole `TurnValue` via `c.json()`, unlike `/stream`'s hand-built events) strips it there directly, computing the same `speakerAgeBand(actor, new Date()) !== "adult"` check inline. The drop is presentation-only both times: the row keeps the real text regardless, the same posture the `reasoning` stream event itself already takes toward the stored combined text.

**Not touched**: `routes/openai.ts`'s own reasoning extraction (`thinkingPrefix(result.value.reply.text)`) never reads `TurnValue.reasoning` at all - it only ever recovers a prose reply's own embedded think block, which this item doesn't change. A tool-resolved turn through that route still has no `reasoning_content` in its response; nobody asked for one, and it's a separate follow-up if they do. The "immediate" kind of `POST /api/turn/stream` result (a safety refusal or a Tier 0 pattern-routed plugin, decided before the model is ever called) was left ungated: that shape provably never sets `.reasoning` (nothing in it ever calls the model at all before answering), so there's nothing to strip.

**A medium-effort review caught a real read-side gap the write-side fix above missed.** `conversationHistory.ts`'s `list()` and `listConversationTurns()` (`GET /api/conversations/turns` and `GET /api/conversations/:id/turns` - the chat history adapter's own real source, getmaipai/home#64) both spread the raw `conversation_turns` row straight into their return value, which now includes the new `reasoning` column with no gating at all: a child's own tool-call reasoning, hidden from the live `POST /api/turn` response and the streaming `done` event, reappeared unfiltered the moment that same turn loaded back as history. Fixed: both functions now drop `reasoning` when the READING actor's own band is not `adult` (`speakerAgeBand()`, the same check the write-side gate uses) - deliberately gated on the READER, not the turn's own recorded `minorSpeaker`, because `canAccessPerson()` only ever lets a non-adult see their OWN turns (this file's own access tests prove a teen can't see a child's, or vice versa), while an owner or admin reading a child's turns keeps seeing everything, matching this file's pre-existing "owner/admin see a child's turns in full" rule (`list()`'s own test of that name) - the point is withholding a minor's own reasoning from THEM, never from a parent's oversight. `ConversationTurnWithMemoryIds` (`wire.ts`) now Omits `reasoning` from the raw row type and redeclares it optional, the same treatment `stats` already has.

**Rebase note (2026-09-21, COORDINATOR)**: this item's own migration (`0054_violet_famine.sql`) was cut against a fork point that landed before CHAT-09's `0054_chat09_embedding_identity.sql` (8243873e), colliding on migration index 54 - CHAT-09 also never committed its own `meta/0054_snapshot.json` (an upstream gap, not something this rebase caused). Resolved on rebase: kept CHAT-09's real `0054_chat09_embedding_identity.sql` untouched, backfilled the missing `meta/0054_snapshot.json` by temporarily reverting `schema.ts` to the post-CHAT-09 state and re-running `drizzle-kit generate` (the generated SQL matched CHAT-09's own migration byte-for-byte modulo formatting, confirmed by diff before trusting the backfilled snapshot), then generated this item's own delta fresh as `0055_groovy_expediter.sql` on top of that real chain. `schema-version.ts`'s `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` bumped 40 -> 41 (CHAT-09 already claimed 40; this item's original commit had missed bumping it entirely, a genuine gap the rebase instructions caught) - `replyFeedback.test.ts`'s hardcoded assertion updated to match.

**Not fixed, a named boundary**: `conversationHistory.ts`'s `exportPerson()` (`GET /api/conversations/export`, memory.ts's own export route) returns the raw `ConversationTurnRow[]` completely unshaped - no field ever gets dropped from it, `reasoning` included, and a person may export their OWN data (`person` defaults to `actor.id`), so a child self-exporting sees their own raw reasoning right back. This is the identical, PRE-EXISTING gap `stats` (STATS-01, "adult-only telemetry") already has in this exact function - not something REASONING-02 introduced, and not fixed here: `exportPerson()`'s own stated purpose ("privileged, single-target," a full-archive dump, `memory.ts`'s `exportPerson()` precedent) is arguably meant to be complete and unredacted, unlike `list()`/`listConversationTurns()`'s browsing surfaces - whether a data-portability export should ever redact a field from the person it belongs to is a real design question this item's scope didn't ask, not a mechanical oversight. Filed as `docs/BACKLOG.md`'s **EXPORT-01** rather than silently fixed or silently left unfindable.

Tests: `tier2.test.ts` (+3: the existing blocking/streaming reasoning-then-tool-call tests extended to assert the field on both the returned value and the row; a new HTTP-level test proving `POST /api/turn` drops it for a child while the row keeps it; the pre-existing no-reasoning tool-call test extended to assert the field stays absent), `turnEngine.test.ts` (+2: the `done` event carries `TurnValue.reasoning` for an adult and drops it for a minor via `streamTurnEvents()` directly; the existing prose-reasoning replay test extended to assert the field is never populated for that shape), `conversationHistory.test.ts` (+2, from the review's own finding: `list()` and `listConversationTurns()` each proven to hide a child's own reasoning from the child while an owner/admin still sees it, and the row keeps it regardless). Backend suite green: see the check run below.

This satisfies the contract table's "streamed as it arrives" honestly rather than by construction: today's own fork (short block = bundled, long block = live) is inherited unchanged, since the new pass sits downstream of `holdOpening()`/`holdForLookup()` and just re-labels whatever granularity those already produce - a short block's `reasoning` event arrives bundled at opening-release time exactly as its `delta` counterpart would have today; a long block's `reasoning` events arrive live, one per delta, exactly as its bundled-in `<think>` text would have streamed today. No new latency is introduced or removed anywhere; the only change is which event type the client sees.

**Decided: "byte-identical to today" means the stored `TurnValue.reply.text`/`fullText` and the rendered, client-visible text** - both hold exactly, per above (neither is touched by this change). The `delta` WIRE EVENT's own granularity may change: in the common/short-think-block case, today's single glued `delta` chunk (think + opening visible text together) becomes two events tomorrow, a `reasoning` event and a smaller `delta` event. That's an accepted, expected difference, not a regression - the design above satisfies the visible-text reading, which is what the contract table and the assistant-ui reasoning Element actually need.

Non-streaming `runTurn()`/`POST /api/turn` is unaffected and out of scope: it has no live event stream to add a `reasoning` event to, and `TurnValue.reply.text` keeps the embedded-think-block shape it already has. A non-streaming reasoning surface, if ever wanted, is a separate, later gap.

### The engine already separates it - checked live, confirmed, wired in

`chat_template_kwargs: { enable_thinking }` (`llm.ts`) and `--reasoning off` (`engineAutotune.ts`, the server's own startup flag) both control whether the model's chat template emits a think block AT ALL - neither is llama.cpp's separate `--reasoning-format` setting (`none`/`deepseek`/`deepseek-legacy`, default `auto`), which controls whether the SERVER splits reasoning into its own `message.reasoning_content` field instead of leaving it inline in `content`. Nothing in `llm.ts` read or requested `reasoning_content` before this pass, and `engineAutotune.ts`'s own args array never sets `--reasoning-format` at all, leaving the server on its default `auto`.

Checked live against the pinned build actually running on this machine (`llama-server --help` on `/…/home/data/engines/llama-server-b10797-macos-arm64/llama-server`, then a real `curl` against the running chat engine on :8788 with the identical `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": true}` request `llm.ts` already sends): **`auto` resolves to clean separation for this model/template** - every streamed chunk's reasoning arrives ONLY in `delta.reasoning_content`, `content` stays empty until reasoning ends, and neither field ever carries a literal `<think>` tag. The non-streaming response shape matches (`message.reasoning_content` alongside `message.content`). So the tag-embedded shape the whole rest of this section explains is not what the live engine actually produces today - it was never exercised because nothing read the field that already carries it separately.

**Implemented as "prefer the engine's separation, tag-parsing as the fallback," per the coordinator's call**: `chatCompleteStream()`/`stackChatDeltas()` (`commons` `spec/llm/ts/client.ts`, `home` `backend/src/lib/llm.ts` - the Stack-routed path is a deliberate verbatim port of the direct client's own logic, kept in sync) synthesize `reasoning_content` into the IDENTICAL `<think>...</think>` shape the rest of the pipeline already expects, the moment it arrives; `complete()`/`completeViaStack()`'s own non-streaming twin (`withSynthesizedThink()`) does the same for a single blocking reply. This is the one and only place either engine behavior is normalized: an engine/template that never populates `reasoning_content` (tags already embedded in `content` instead) passes through completely unchanged, byte-identical to before this item. `wellFormed.ts`, `composeBlocking`, `gateOutputSafety`/`gateGuards`, `holdOpening`, `holdForLookup`, the retry machinery, and `finalize()` stay untouched, exactly as "the smallest change" promised: they only ever see the one uniform `<think>`-embeddable text shape, never `reasoning_content` itself. The wire-boundary split is genuinely engine-agnostic for the identical reason: it splits whatever `<think>` tags arrive, regardless of whether `llm.ts` synthesized them from a separated field or they arrived already embedded from a template that leaks them into `content`. **One real exception a review found** (below): `peekAndHandle()`'s own tool-call-vs-prose disambiguation genuinely needed a small, targeted fix, because reasoning now yields real string chunks where it used to yield nothing at all.

Pin since the vendored menu is Rename/Archive/Delete not Rename/Pin/
Delete), slice 3 (weather's and almanac-date's own structured result
renders through the shipped `SpecSheet` Element, keyed on the
producing package's real name, `display: "standalone"` so it isn't
tucked behind a collapsed "1 tool call" trigger), and slice 4
(artifacts: `TurnValue.artifact` becomes a real tool-call part
rendering the shipped `ArtifactCard`, opening `CanvasSplit` beside the
thread on desktop or a phone/tablet Sheet; a new `GET /api/artifacts/
{id}/current` route, resolved through the artifact's own Home-internal
key, is what makes this survive reload unlike #130's `structured_part`
and what makes a later turn's update replace the open pane on its own,
no id bookkeeping needed). Found live verifying slice 4, not fixed
there (getmaipai/home#131): `write_document` cannot actually create a
document on a real turn - `host.artifact.create()` needs the turn's
own `conversation_turns` row, but that row is written only after the
whole turn finishes, well after this tool call already ran, so the
insert always fails on the table's own foreign key. One layer of it
(the same method's `conversationId` was ALSO always empty, from an
equally always-missing DB lookup) is fixed alongside slice 4 -
`createHost()`/`runPlugin()` now take a bundled `{id, conversationId}`
straight from the caller's turn context - but the foreign-key ordering
problem itself is still open, both real fixes it needs (drop the hard
FK, or give a turn a real row before its own tool outcomes run) named
in the issue but not attempted, since both are bigger and riskier than
a `/next/chat` wiring slice's own scope. Open: the rest of SHELL-02's
own wiring table (suggestions and attachments, then read-aloud), then
the other SHELL rows.

## Memory outcomes as notifications (2026-09-21)

**Why**: `memory.updated` (`lib/notificationTypes.ts`) has been `configurable: true` and triggered from `memoryJudge.ts` since getmaipai/home#64, but never got a real settings key - a household could never actually opt it into Telegram, and there was no sibling notification for the judge's OTHER terminal outcome (the poison guard giving up after `MAX_JUDGE_ATTEMPTS` extraction failures, `judge_status: "failed"`), even though `chatMemoryChip.tsx` already renders a visible "failed" chip for exactly that state. The coordinator's own framing: get the notification side complete enough (both outcomes the chip currently shows) that a later item can consider retiring the chip's own 5s/10min polling lifecycle in favor of the notification center - not this item's own job to do that retirement, just to make it possible.

**Landed**:
- `lib/notificationTypes.ts` gains `memory.judge_failed` (passive, person audience, configurable, `in_app` default, `toast: false` - the same posture `memory.updated` already takes, since neither is urgent).
- `settings/notificationKeys.ts` gains BOTH missing toggle keys, following the `notifications.engines.*.telegram` four keys' own pattern exactly: `notifications.memory.updated.telegram` (the pre-existing gap) and `notifications.memory.judge_failed.telegram` (the new type's own toggle). Regenerated into `commons`'s `spec/settings/keys.json` (spec-v0.1.13) via `bun run gen:settings` - the diff against the previously-pinned spec-v0.1.12 keys.json contained exactly these two new entries and nothing else, confirmed before cutting the tag.
- `memoryJudge.ts`: `markAttempt()` now returns whether this attempt was the real, landed transition to `judge_status: "failed"` - not just whether the attempt COUNT crossed the threshold, since its own guarded UPDATE (`WHERE judge_status IS NULL`) can legitimately hit zero rows if a concurrent "forget that" already moved the row to `skipped` (this file's own long-documented race, the "#88"/"item 4b" comments throughout). `judgeTurn()`'s extraction-failure branch fires `trigger("memory.judge_failed", ...)` only when `markAttempt()` returns true, so the notification fires exactly once, at a REAL transition, never for a turn that was actually forgotten.

**A medium-effort review caught the exact race** `markAttempt()`'s own header comment already named: the first cut computed its returned boolean from `attempts >= MAX_JUDGE_ATTEMPTS` alone, so a "forget that" landing during the third, failing extraction call (marking the row `skipped` mid-flight, between `judgeTurn()`'s early `isSkippedTurn()` check and `markAttempt()`'s own write) would still fire the notification for a turn that was never actually marked failed. Fixed with the raw-sqlite `.run().changes` escape hatch `personLifecycle.ts` already established for the identical reason (Drizzle's bun-sqlite `.run()` types its result void): `markAttempt()` now returns `failed && changes > 0`. A new test in `memoryJudge.test.ts` reproduces the race with a scripted extraction callback that marks the row `skipped` on its third invocation (the same "direct DB write inside the scripted callback" technique the file's own pre-existing lease-race test uses to simulate concurrency deterministically), and proves the row stays `skipped` and no notification fires.

**Deliberately not fired**: the "judged, nothing worth remembering" outcome (`judge_status: "done"`, zero facts written - the overwhelming majority of turns) gets no notification, matching Jesse's own 2026-09-13 ruling already recorded in `chatMemoryChip.tsx`'s header comment ("a person should see this chip only when something actually happened - these are process, not an outcome"). Notifying on every non-event would be pure noise; this item extends coverage to the two outcomes that already ARE events (saved, failed), not to every possible resolution the judge can reach.

**Not done, filed as its own item**: retiring `chatMemoryState.ts`'s own polling lifecycle now that both its visible states have a real notification behind them - `docs/BACKLOG.md`'s new "Retire the chip's own poll in favor of notifications" item, which names the real remaining design question (the poll's `not_saved`/`pending` distinction has no notification counterpart and, per the ruling above, never should get one - a notification-only chip needs a different way to know "nothing happened, stop waiting").

Tests: `memoryJudge.test.ts` (+2: the existing poison-guard test extended to assert the notification fires, a new test proving the concurrent-forget race is closed). Backend suite green: 3684/3684.


## SHELL-01, the backend half: GET /api/dashboard (2026-09-21)

Why: the shadcndashboard template's modern-dashboard page (`/next`) needs one real aggregate to bind its KPI-card and chart widgets to - the vendored template ships them with hardcoded demo numbers ("714k weekly sales," an e-commerce "recent orders" table), so there is no existing prop shape to mirror; this item is the backend half only, built entirely from existing libs rather than a second read path for any of them - the page itself, the widget bindings and the screenshot pass are a separate, later item this doesn't close.

**Person-scoped, not admin-only** (the coordinator's own call): every signed-in person gets `people_count` (a household-wide fact everyone already knows), `updates_available` (the same reach `GET /api/updates` already has - reuses `lib/updates.ts`'s own `blockedBy` field, the semver-derived "a real update exists and nothing can apply it yet" signal, never a second, home-grown version comparison), `recent_activity` (a compact list - `turn_id`, `person_id`, `display_name`, `created_at`, `surface`, `source`, never the turn's own text) and `turns_per_day` (a gap-free 30-day daily count series for a chart). The latter two are scoped through `access.ts`'s own `canAccessPerson()` rule - an owner/admin's visible target set is themselves plus every child, never a teen's or another adult's own activity - reused exactly as `list()`/`listConversationTurns()` already enforce it, not a new or wider policy invented for a dashboard. `repairs_open` (`lib/issues.ts`'s `listIssues()`, after `syncStackHealthIssues()` folds in Stack health first, matching `repairs.ts`'s own GET) and `engines` (severity counts from a configured Stack's `health()`, `null` when no Stack is configured or the call fails) are additive fields present ONLY for owner/admin, matching `repairs.ts`'s and `engines.ts`'s own existing owner/admin-only gates for this exact data - absent from the wire entirely for anyone else, never a zeroed-out placeholder that could misread as "nothing wrong."

**A medium-effort review caught two real bugs before this landed.** (1) `updates_available` first computed itself as `app.latest !== app.installed`, a raw string comparison between GitHub's `vX.Y.Z` tag and an unprefixed installed version - the same class of bug `isNewerVersion()`'s own doc comment already warns against, which would read a fully up-to-date household as needing an update forever the moment the two strings merely differ in `v`-prefixing. Fixed by reusing `blockedBy` (see above) instead of re-deriving the boolean a second way; a regression test proves `latest: "v0.1.0"` against the default installed `"0.1.0"` reads `false`, not just a `"v9.9.9"` case the old buggy code would have also gotten right by coincidence. (2) `recentActivity()` first called `list()` once per visible target id - a real N+1, each its own full unindexed scan of `conversation_turns`. Fixed to one direct query (`WHERE person_id IN (...) ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?`, the same shape `turns_per_day`'s own grouped query already used), and a new `conversation_turns_person_id_idx` index (migration `0056_curved_adam_warlock.sql`) closes the underlying gap for good - `person_id` was filtered by several existing callers (`list()`, `listConversationTurns()`, `exportPerson()`) with no supporting index at all. No `schema-version.ts` bump: an index change alone, not a column/table add/remove/rename, matching this repo's own established rule (the PERF-4 precedent).

No spec tag: the response is a bespoke aggregate view, not a shared record.

Tests: `dashboard.test.ts` (new, 7 cases: auth required, the person/admin field split, `repairs_open`/`engines` against a real scripted Stack fixture, the child-visible/teen-and-adult-invisible activity scoping with no duplicates, and the two `updates_available` cases above). Backend suite green: 3690/3690.

**Why**: the backend half (above) built `GET /api/dashboard`; this is the page that reads it. Real blocker found before writing a line: none of the vendored modern-dashboard widgets (`@maipai/ui/src/dashboard/components/dashboards/modern/*` - `total-orders.tsx`, `total-sales.tsx`, `projects-orders.tsx`, and the rest) takes a prop or calls a data hook. Grepped the whole vendored `ui/src/dashboard` tree for `useSWR`/`global-fetcher`: zero matches, anywhere, for any view. `ui/docs/dashboard-upstream.md`'s own "Stripped" list names why - `chance` (the fake-data generator) and the MSW `api/mocks` tree were both removed at vendoring, and those were the real data layer even upstream. `Dashboard`/`DashboardActivityRow`/`DashboardTurnsPerDay`/`DashboardEngineCounts` moved from `lib/dashboard.ts` into `wire.ts` (the alias-free file `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` can actually import), the same "hand-copied here, re-exported there" shape every other cross-package wire type in this file already takes - `lib/dashboard.ts` re-exports them rather than redefining them, so backend callers keep importing from the same place.

**A lint rule caught before it shipped**: every new widget file first imported `lucide-react` icons directly, matching the vendored files' own style - but `docs/UI.md`'s "lucide only, by name" rule (enforced by `eslint.config.js`'s `no-restricted-imports`) requires `getIcon()` from the kit's own curated registry (`@maipai/ui/src/icons`) everywhere outside the one existing exception (`thread.aui.tsx`, the assistant-ui Elements file). Fixed: every icon now comes through `getIcon("name")`; one substitution was needed (`TrendingUp` isn't in the curated list - `history` is the closest available match for "a record over time").

**A medium-effort review found five more, all fixed before this landed.** (1) The page checked only `isLoading`, so a failed fetch (an expired session, a 500) left the loading skeleton showing forever with no error text or retry - fixed by routing the page through `AsyncState` (`@maipai/ui/src/primitives/AsyncState`), the kit's own shared loading/error/data triad every sibling page already uses, rather than a hand-rolled branch; a new test proves a failed fetch shows the real error message and a "Try again" button. (2) `Greeting.tsx` reimplemented time-of-day bucketing by hand (different hour boundaries, a stray "Good Night" bucket, its own capitalization) instead of calling `@/apps/home/greeting.ts`'s existing `greetingFor()`/`timeOfDay()` - already the shell header's own source for the identical text (`routeHeader.ts`) - so the old shell and `/next` would have shown a DIFFERENT greeting for the same person at the same moment. Fixed to call the real function directly. (3) The same file froze its computed greeting in `useState` from a mount-only effect, so it never updated across an hour boundary while the page stayed open (a real display-left-open case, not just a lint nit) - fixed by dropping the effect entirely and calling `greetingFor()` inline on every render, the shell header's own pattern. (4) `PeopleCountCard.tsx`/`UpdatesCard.tsx`/`RepairsCard.tsx`/`EnginesCard.tsx` were four hand-copied files repeating the identical `DashboardCard`/`CardContent`/icon-box JSX verbatim - exactly the "smallest composition of shipped parts" rule's own target, not a fourth parallel copy. (5) `EnginesCard.tsx` recomputed its issue count as `critical + error + warning` instead of reading the wire's own precomputed `total` - harmless today (the three severities are `HealthItem.severity`'s whole union) but a silent future footgun if a fourth severity is ever added without updating this card; fixed to read `engines.total` directly.

Tests: `NextDashboardPage.test.tsx` (7 cases: the greeting shows the signed-in person's own name and the household counts; repairs/engines cards render when the wire carries them; neither renders at all when the wire omits them, never a faked zero; recent activity shows real rows; recent activity's own empty state when there are none; the engines card's own "no Stack configured" empty state; a failed fetch shows a real error and a retry button, from the review's own finding).
