## Memory ingestion, one idempotent service (CHAT-06, 2026-09-21)

**Why**: before this, every write path that created a memory record (`memory.ts`'s `remember()`, `packageHost.ts`, `routes/memory.ts`, and the judge's own direct `db.insert(memoryRecords)` calls) did its own copy of the same checks - credential detection, scope authorization, person-exists, Zod spec validation, the vector store, and the pending-embedding queue - each in its own place, and none of them deduplicated. Repeating the same save twice produced two active facts with the same text; a correction superseded without keeping provenance cleanly, and a failed embed or failed model dedupe could leave work in a side file instead of the DB.

**Landed**: `backend/src/lib/memoryIngestion.ts` is the one service. It accepts actor, text, scope, category, tier, source, importance, validity bounds, and any precomputed embedding; validates through the existing spec and content policy; does a canonical duplicate comparison (NFC, trimmed, collapsed whitespace, case-folded) within identical scope/person; persists the record in a `sqlite.transaction()`; and fires-and-forgets the embed, queueing `pending_memory_work` (a new table, migration 0058, with `reason` "embed_failed" or "dedupe_failed") instead of a side file when the embed or the dedupe model call fails. `memory.ts`'s `remember()`, `packageHost.ts`, and `routes/memory.ts` now all route through `ingestMemory` - `grep -rn 'db.insert(memoryRecords)'` outside `memoryIngestion.ts` prints nothing. `supersedeMemory` and `drainPendingWork` handle corrections and the restart path: a repeated save yields one active fact, an interrupted normalization then restart yields one, a failed dedupe leaves work pending not an ADD, a correction yields one supersession with provenance kept, and same-turn retries neither duplicate nor re-supersede. All five are tests in `backend/tests/memory.test.ts` (the new "CHAT-06" describe block).

## CHAT-UI-01: five findings on /next/chat with the rail collapsed (2026-09-21)

**Why**: Jesse's own side-by-side with ChatGPT, rail collapsed on /next/chat - five real findings, none of them SHELL-02's own slice work, all about the shell composition around it.

**Landed**, one per finding: (1) collapsed section labels ("HOME"/"HOUSEHOLD"/"SYSTEM"/"MANAGE") rendered as a literal `"..."` and expanded to the full word on `group-hover` - root-caused to `nav-collapse/index.tsx`, the vendored template's own hand-rolled section-heading renderer (a hardcoded string, not `text-overflow`, confirmed reading the file directly), a different component from the primitive `SidebarGroupLabel` a few files over that already fades cleanly with no dots and no hover-reveal. The demo shows dots too - the template's own real default, not local breakage - and nothing about it is reachable from outside without either forking `nav-collapse` or a global rule broad enough to hit every other `group-hover:hidden` in the app. Named as a real deviation, not fixed. (2) the thread-list column sat roughly 75px into empty space once the rail freed more width than `FullLayout.tsx`'s own `.container` (`globals.css`'s `@utility container { max-w-[1367px] mx-auto }`, wrapping every /next page's `<Outlet/>`) actually used. Fixed with a scoped override in `frontend/src/shell/tokens.css` (Home's own Tailwind root, never the vendored file): `.container:has([data-slot="next-chat-shell"]) { max-width: none; margin-inline: 0 }`, reached through one marker `NextChatPage.tsx`'s own top-level element now carries. (3) the composer bounced scrolling to the bottom - two real, separate causes. `FullLayout.tsx`'s own wrapper around `<Outlet/>` is `min-h-*`, not `h-*`, so a growing composer or a streaming reply could push the whole page taller for a moment; fixed with `overflow-hidden` on `next-chat-shell`, a hard ceiling now, not a floor. The Footer sitting right below `<Outlet/>` always leaves the page a sliver of its own real scroll range, and the thread viewport's own scroll chained into it at the boundary and rubber-banded back - fixed with `overscroll-behavior-y: none`, scoped in tokens.css the same way as (2). (4) a ChatGPT-style collapse toggle for the thread-list column: the shipped `Sidebar` primitive (`threadlist-sidebar.aui.tsx`'s own composition) renders `position: fixed` against the true viewport edge - built to be a page's one top-level sidebar, not a second column nested beside one already there (it would render under or over the app rail, not after it) - so this reuses the identical plain-toggle pattern the file already had for the phone/tablet Sheet (`useState` plus a `Button`), not the primitive's own collapsible state machine. No hover-peek: the primitive has no such mode to reach for at all (`SidebarRail`'s own hover only tints its divider line), so per its own fallback that gap is named, not hand-built. (5) a centered date/time divider after a long gap between turns, like ChatGPT: the catalog has `day-separator.tsx`, but it owns an entire message list's own bubble rendering rather than being an injectable divider for Thread's own per-message flow - which this shell already relies on for reasoning, tool calls and artifacts, and would have to give up to use it. No composable divider atom exists for this composition today; named as a gap, not forked or hand-rolled (slice 5's own `message-timing` Element covers per-message time, not this).

`NextChatPage.test.tsx` gained one case for (4) (the toggle hides and restores the desktop column, the thread itself untouched). Verified live on 8787 for all five: the collapsed rail's own dots/hover-reveal match the vendored demo exactly, "New Thread" now sits flush after the rail with no dead gutter, a real weather turn still renders and the composer stays pinned with no visible jitter, the new toggle hides and restores the thread-list column cleanly leaving the thread and composer alone.

## SHELL-FLAG-01: `ui.shell.next` on means the whole app (2026-09-21)

**Why**: Jesse signed out and landed back on the old dashboard and sign-in form, then had to type `/next` by hand - with the flag on, the new shell should be the whole app, not just a route he has to remember.

**Landed**: `App.tsx`'s old `/*` route (`OldShellRoutes`, extracted but otherwise unchanged) now checks three pure functions in a new file, `frontend/src/shell/oldShellRedirect.ts` - `shouldRedirectRootToNext`, `isRootStillResolving`, `signOutDestination`, all keyed off `useShellNext()`'s existing `"loading" | "on" | "off"` state, no new state of its own. Kept out of `App.tsx` itself on purpose: that file imports `@/i18n`, which pulls in a `.po` file bun's test runtime has no loader for, so the decision logic needed its own file to be testable at all. A review caught a real bug in the first draft: it checked the redirect before checking `person === null`, so a signed-out visitor to `/` would wait on `useShellNext()`'s own auth-gated settings fetch (a guaranteed 401 for them) before the sign-in form ever rendered - a real added round trip that didn't exist before this item. Fixed by wrapping the whole block in `person !== null`, so a signed-out visit is byte-for-byte what it was before this item touched anything.

`oldShellRedirect.test.ts` (13 cases, both ways for all three redirects) plus one new integration test in `NextRoutes.test.tsx` proving an authenticated visit to `/next/sign-in` actually lands on the real dashboard, not just that the `Navigate` fires. `useShellNext()`'s own shape and its one existing consumer, `NextRoutes.tsx`, were left untouched on COORDINATOR's own instruction, to keep HOME-UI-04g's pending rebase small - the same three-state branch now exists in both places, a real, deliberate duplication worth a shared predicate once 04g lands, noted in `oldShellRedirect.ts`'s own comment rather than fixed here.

## CHAT-UI-02: the desktop rail toggle stops spending its own row, and gains hover-to-peek (2026-09-21)

**Why**: Jesse's own screenshot of CHAT-UI-01 finding 4's toggle - it sat above the thread-list column in a row of its own, and hover-to-peek was ruled a real requirement, not the gap CHAT-UI-01 named it as.

**Landed**: the toggle moved into the row it already has, rather than one of its own. Open, it's `NextThreadList`'s new `collapseToggle` prop, rendered beside `ThreadListNew` in the same flex row (`ThreadListNew` grows via `className="flex-1"`, the toggle stays icon-only). Collapsed, the identical-purpose control floats at the chat area's own top-left corner (`absolute top-2 left-2`), over the thread's top padding rather than a header row - so neither state spends one. The header row above the column is now `lg:hidden` outright: its only other content, the mobile Sheet trigger, was already invisible past `lg` (`className="lg:hidden"` on the button itself), so that row was dead space on desktop even before CHAT-UI-01 first put a second button in it - this just makes the row's own visibility match what was already true of everything inside it.

Hover-to-peek, first draft: hovering the collapsed toggle showed `NextThreadList` inside the shipped dashboard `Card`/`CardContent`, as an absolutely positioned overlay below the button, with a hand-rolled `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` pair on a wrapper div around both (`railPeeked`, one boolean, no timers) deciding when it showed. A medium review caught two real bugs in that: a dead zone in the gap between the button and the card - the wrapper's own hover box is only as tall as its in-flow content (the button), since an absolutely positioned child doesn't contribute to a parent's layout box, so the pointer crossing the `mt-1` gap between them read as leaving the wrapper entirely, flickering the overlay shut on the way to it; and no keyboard or focus path at all, so a keyboard user got no peek, only the fully-pinned state on activation.

**Landed for real**: the shipped `HoverCard` (`@maipai/ui/src/dashboard/components/ui/hover-card`, Base UI's `PreviewCard` underneath) replaces the hand-rolled pair outright - its hover interaction (floating-ui's own safe-polygon tracking) treats trigger and portalled content as one region with no dead zone, and it opens on focus as well as hover, for free. `open`/`onOpenChange` on `HoverCard` stay controlled (`railPeeked`, now just a mirror of Base UI's own computed state, not a second implementation of it) only so `aria-expanded` on the trigger can be accurate, matching the open-state toggle's own contract; a low re-review of that fix caught one more gap the swap had dropped rather than fixed - the collapsed trigger had no `aria-controls` at all - closed by giving `HoverCardContent` a fixed `id="next-chat-rail-peek"` and pointing the trigger's `aria-controls` at it, mounted or not. A click on the trigger still pins the column open (`setRailCollapsed(false)`), independent of the hover card's own state, and resets `railPeeked` in the same click so a later collapse never mounts already "open" from a stale peek.

Four cases in `NextChatPage.test.tsx`, one per state plus the leave-hides case: open (the toggle and New Thread share a parent row, no peek content anywhere in the DOM), collapsed (the floating toggle renders with `aria-controls="next-chat-rail-peek"` and `aria-expanded="false"`, the content itself not yet mounted), peeked (hovering mounts the overlay, its own New Thread button becomes reachable, `aria-expanded` flips to `"true"`, leaving unmounts it and flips it back), and pinning (a click while peeked collapses back to open and the floating toggle disappears). The rail's own `hidden`/`lg:block` class-list checks use a whole-token split, not `toContain` on the raw string - the dashboard `Card` family's base classes include `overflow-hidden`, which a plain substring check for `"hidden"` would false-positive on.

## CHAT-UI-02 follow-up: the peek looks like the column, not a card (2026-09-21)

**Why**: Jesse's own screenshot of the peek overlay - it read as "some odd popup" (a small rounded card floating below-left of the toggle), not the thread-list column sliding back in.

**Landed**: `HoverCardContent`'s own shipped card chrome (`rounded-lg`, `shadow-md`, `ring-1 ring-foreground/10`, `bg-popover`, `p-2.5`) is overridden via `className` (`tailwind-merge` resolves the conflicting utilities in favor of the later ones, the same mechanism `alert-dialog.tsx`'s own `render` composition already relies on) to `w-64 h-[calc(100vh-140px)] overflow-y-auto rounded-none border-r border-border bg-background pr-2 shadow-none ring-0` - the exact width, height, background and right border the real open column has, so a peek reads as the same column, not a floating panel. Positioned with `side="bottom" align="start" sideOffset={-40}` rather than the shipped default (`side="bottom"`, a positive offset, centered) - `align="start"` already left-aligns the popup with the trigger the same way the real column starts at the chat area's own left edge; the negative `sideOffset` pulls it up so its own top edge lines up with the trigger's top, instead of appearing below it with a gap. The toggle's own `z-20` is now `z-[60]`, above `HoverCardContent`'s shipped `z-50` - found live: without it, the portalled popup painted over the toggle during peek, hiding the one control that closes it (or pins it open). Verified live on 8787 (a real hover on 8787): the peek now spans the same height as the open column, right up to the footer, with the identical right border and background, closes cleanly on pointer-leave, and a click still pins it open into the ordinary layout.

## CHAT-UI-02, rebuilt: no floating placement, pixel-perfect by construction (2026-09-21)

**Why**: the HoverCard follow-up above never reached pixel parity. Jesse's live feedback, three rounds: (1) "shows better but it's not aligned to where it is when it's normally expanded" - measurable requirement, the peeked column's box must equal the open column's box to the pixel; (2) his zoomed screenshots after a first attempt at fixing that: "the toggle floats over the top-left of the column and overlaps the New Thread row in both the open and the peeked state"; (3) his zoom after the rebuild below landed the column's own alignment: "the toggle is a large floating button painted over the New Thread row and the search box" - the toggle itself, not the column, was still wrong.

**Round 1, why the HoverCard approach couldn't be patched into alignment**: side/align/offset math against the trigger's own rect measured live at `x:537` (with `container={chatAreaRef}`, kit `ui-v0.5.25`'s new `container` prop), then `x:304` (dropping `container`, overriding position directly) - both against the real column's own `x:272`, however the offset was tuned, because floating-ui's own placement is relative to the trigger's rect, not an unrelated sibling's. Overriding Base UI's own positioning node directly (`PreviewCardPrimitive.Positioner`, the popup's actual parent - the popup itself is `position: static`, confirmed by reading its live computed style) still failed silently: the override effect, keyed on `railPeeked` via `useEffect`, ran before Base UI had portaled `#next-chat-rail-peek` into the DOM at all, found by reading the live `positioner.style.cssText` and seeing Base UI's own untouched `position: absolute; transform: translate(...)`.

**Landed, replacing the floating placement entirely**: per Jesse's own literal spec (22:04), the column (`next-chat-rail`) is now one DOM node that always lives in the page's own layout at its own slot - open is normal flex flow, collapsed is `hidden`, peeked is the SAME node with `absolute inset-y-0 left-0` inside the row's own `relative` box (the row wrapping the rail and the chat area, not the chat area alone - so the peeked box starts at the row's own left edge, exactly where the open rail sits), at its normal open `w-64`, above the thread (`z-20`). No JS-measured rect, no portal, no effect: three Tailwind class strings keyed off two booleans, so the peeked box is pixel-identical to the open box by construction, not by measurement. Verified live on 8787: open rail, collapsed toggle, and peeked rail all measure `{x:272, y:81}`; the peeked rail's full box exactly matches the open rail's `{width:256, height:683}`; the app header's own bottom edge (`y:65`) stays above the peeked overlay's top edge (`y:81`) in every case, so the overlay can never paint over the header or search bar.

**The toggle went through two more rounds on top of that.** First: one floating button, a sibling of the column, fixed at the row's own top-left in every state (open, collapsed, peeked) via `position: absolute`. This fixed the column's own alignment but read as an oversized control painted on top of New Thread - Jesse's third round of feedback. Closing that peek used a `display: contents` wrapper around the toggle and the column so a shared `onPointerLeave` could see both without affecting the row's own flex sizing; found live, `display: contents` never received the pointerleave the real browser fired when the cursor left the toggle for the page below, because it removes the element from the rendered box tree Chromium's own hover-tracking hit-tests against - no box, no ancestor to fire on.

**Landed for real**: per Jesse's 22:22 correction, the toggle is now two mutually-exclusive `Button` instances sharing one set of handlers (`handleToggleEnter`/`handleToggleClick`, one `toggleLabel`/`toggleExpanded` pair). Open and peeked render `inlineToggle` - true flow, the first cell of `NextThreadList`'s own header row (its new `collapseToggle` prop, back to a plain `ReactNode` slot), the same icon-button size as the row's other controls, never absolutely positioned. Collapsed alone (no row left to be inline with, since the column is `hidden`) falls back to `collapsedToggle`, identically styled but `absolute top-0 left-0` at the row's own former top-left. Exactly one of the two is ever mounted. Closing the peek no longer needs the `display: contents` workaround at all: the inline toggle is now a genuine DESCENDANT of `next-chat-rail` when peeked, so a plain `onPointerLeave`/`onBlur` on the rail div itself, checking that `relatedTarget` isn't still inside it, gets the native ancestor-chain firing for free - no dead zone, confirmed live by real mouse movement from the toggle into the rest of the column (stays open) and out to the thread/composer area (closes).

`NextChatPage.test.tsx`'s four CHAT-UI-02 cases were rewritten for the new structure. happy-dom computes no real box layout, so "peeked equals open" is proven structurally rather than by a measured rect: the rail is asserted to be the SAME node reference across all three states (never remounted, never duplicated), and its peeked classes are asserted to include `absolute inset-y-0 left-0 w-64` - the same sizing class the open state uses, anchored to the same `relative` ancestor the open flow already starts at. The collapsed and peeked cases disambiguate the two toggle instances by DOM containment (`rail().contains(btn)`) since both can carry the same accessible name at once (the inline one, inert inside a `hidden` rail happy-dom doesn't actually hide, and the floating one) - a live-only distinction the unit tests can't see, which is exactly why the pixel probe against 8787 above is what proves the real behavior, not the test suite alone.

## ADMIN-COMPARE-01, backend: POST /api/turn/bare (2026-09-21)

**Why**: an owner/admin needs to tell whether a dumb reply is the model itself or the rest of the pipeline (routing, packages, persona, guards) - COORDINATOR's own two-part spec, (a) a one-off "Compare with the bare model" action per message and (b) a per-conversation switch to run a whole conversation both ways. This lands (a)'s backend only.

**Landed**: `backend/src/routes/turnBare.ts`, a new route mounted at `/api/turn/bare`, deliberately NOT reusing `routes/turn.ts`'s own machinery (resumable sessions, cancel routes, real turn logging) - none of that applies to a comparison that stores nothing. `requireAuth` plus an inline `isOwnerOrAdmin` check gates the whole route before anything else runs. History is `buildConversationWindow(conversation, { excludeTurnId, beforeCreatedAt: turnRow.createdAt })` (the new `beforeCreatedAt` option, below) plus the compared turn's own `userText` appended as the final user message; the completion is `startCompleteStream("chat", [system, ...history], { thinking: true })` with a bare one-line system prompt, no routing, no packages, no persona, no guards. The minor safety pass is the one deliberate exception - checked against docs/SAFETY.md before writing a line of this ("no admin setting... may disable or weaken" child-safety protections) - so `gateOutputSafety` runs unconditionally on every bare completion, age-banded off the ORIGINAL turn's own speaker (looked up by the turn row's own `personId`), never the admin actually calling the route; a refusal streams a `{type: "refused"}` event and nothing of the unsafe content. The response is a new, minimal NDJSON shape (`trace`/`reasoning`/`delta`/`refused`/`done`), not `TurnStreamEvent` - the first line is the "ours" trace, read straight off the compared turn's own row (`rung`, `rules`, `routing_tier`/`routing_score`, `guard_reason`, `source`, `plugin_id`/`command_id`, `stats`) plus a fresh `resolvePersona`/`composePersonaPrompt` call for "persona fragments in effect" (the household's current setting - persona isn't stored per-turn, so this can drift from what actually shaped the original reply if it's changed since).

A medium review on the first draft caught two real bugs: `gateOutputSafety` was called without the turn's own id, so `notifyOncePerTurn`'s per-sentence dedup never applied and a multi-sentence flagged reply could fire one parent notification per sentence instead of one for the whole comparison - fixed by passing the real `turnId` through, the same as every real turn's own call (it's only used for notification dedup, never written anywhere, so reusing the id a flagged sentence already fired on for the ORIGINAL turn is the correct behavior, not a leak). And `buildConversationWindow`'s own `excludeTurnId` only ever dropped the one named row by id, so comparing a turn that wasn't a conversation's newest fed the bare completion turns that hadn't happened yet when the compared turn actually ran - not "the same conversation history" this route's own header comment claims. Fixed with a new `beforeCreatedAt` option on `buildConversationWindow` itself (`conversationHistory.ts`), filtering rows before windowing rather than duplicating the function's own token-budget logic in the route; a permanent regression test (`turnBareRoutes.test.ts`) plants a later turn with a `FUTURE_MARKER` in its text and asserts it never reaches the bare completion's own request. A low re-review confirmed both fixes correct.

`TurnStats` gains a `thinking: boolean` field (`wire.ts`, `turnStats.ts`'s `buildTurnStats()`), threaded through the three `logTurnSafely()` call sites in `turnEngine.ts` that already produce stats (`meta.thinking: opts.thinking`) - no migration, since `stats` is already a JSON text column. This is for the trace's own "thinking on/off" line on the ORIGINAL turn, not the bare completion (which is always thinking-on by the route's own design).

Tests (`turnBareRoutes.test.ts`): the admin gate (403 for a signed-in adult household member who isn't owner/admin, checked before the body is even parsed), the no-store rule (a `conversation_turns` row count before and after, unchanged), the minor safety pass (an established output-refusal fixture - `safety01.test.ts`'s own "pipe bomb" phrase - refused on a child's own turn, and refused on the admin's OWN conversation too, since `harmful_request` is a universal refuse category: the real, checkable claim isn't "refused for a child but not an adult," it's that the pass never gates on bare mode at all), and the `beforeCreatedAt` regression case above. A stray dangling background stream (a test that checked only the response status without reading its NDJSON body kept generating after the stub server was torn down, surfacing as "could not reach" on whichever test ran next) was found and fixed by always consuming the body before a test's own stub teardown.

**Still open, not started**: feature (a)'s frontend half - the "Compare with the bare model" per-message action (a real kit-side gap: the vendored `AssistantActionBar`'s own "More" menu, `commons`'s `thread.aui.tsx`, is hardcoded to one item with no extension slot, so this needs a genuine kit API addition, not a Home-side composition) and the two-column canvas-split compare view. Feature (b) in full: the per-conversation `bare: true` switch on the real turn request, threaded into the live pipeline (not `routes/turn.ts`'s own `POST /`/`POST /stream`, which stay untouched by this item), a `bare` marker on the row so RVW-1's labels and the compare view can find it, and the conversation history's own "bare model" badge on the message (a shipped Elements badge, per COORDINATOR - nothing hand-drawn). COORDINATOR's own call on the memory judge: a bare-mode turn is diagnostic, not a real exchange, so it is never queued for extraction.

## Backups off the event loop (home#46, 2026-09-22)

**Why**: `runBackup()` in `lib/backup.ts` ran SQLite's `VACUUM INTO` and `backupCrypto.ts`'s whole-file AES-256-GCM encrypt/decrypt synchronously on the main thread, called from both a request handler and the scheduler. On a large database every other request stalled for the duration of the backup. The same was true of `restoreBackup()`, which ran the decrypt whole-file on the main thread.

**Landed**: two changes, both in `backend/src/lib/`. (1) `snapshotWorker.ts` (new): a `node:worker_threads` worker that opens its own `bun:sqlite` connection to the live database file and runs `VACUUM INTO ?`, returning the snapshot path to the parent. This avoids the live-DB double-open guard (two `bun:sqlite` connections to the same file in one process are not allowed) and moves the CPU-bound `VACUUM INTO` off the main thread entirely. (2) `backupCrypto.ts` rewritten from whole-file `crypto.createCipheriv()`/`createDecipheriv()` to streaming: `encryptFile` pipes a `fs.createReadStream` through a `crypto.createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", ...)` stream into a `fs.createWriteStream` (with a 28-byte header reserved and patched in after the stream ends), and `decryptFile` reads the 28-byte IV + auth tag header, then pipes the remainder through `createDecipheriv` into an output stream. The on-disk format is unchanged: `[12-byte IV][16-byte auth tag][ciphertext]`. `backup.ts`'s `runBackup()` now spawns the worker, awaits the snapshot, then calls the streaming `encryptFile` and moves the result into `backupDir`. `restoreBackup()` calls the streaming `decryptFile` into a staging file, then applies it.

**Measured**: a 300 MB database (315 MB after encryption) takes 656 ms on the worker thread while an unrelated `GET /api/people` completes in 2 ms on the main thread (the exit-check test in `backup.test.ts`, "a running backup does not block unrelated request handling on the event loop"). The request's 2 ms elapsed time is well under the 100 ms threshold the test asserts.

**Bun-specific gotchas encountered**: (1) `fs.promises as fs` aliasing makes `fs.createWriteStream` undefined - use the already-imported `createWriteStream` from `node:fs` directly. (2) `fs.promises.open()` returns a `FileHandle` object, not a numeric fd; `fs.promises.read(fd, ...)` expects a numeric fd and throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` when given a `FileHandle`. The working pattern is `fs.open(path, "r")` → `fd.read(buf, 0, len, offset)` → `fd.close()`. (3) `fs.promises.writeFile()` followed by `createWriteStream(outPath, { start: headerSize })` then `fs.open(outPath, "r+")` → `fd.write(header, 0, header.length, 0)` → `fd.close()` is the reliable way to patch the 28-byte header after the cipher stream has written the ciphertext. (4) `node:worker_threads` in Bun loads `.ts` worker files without needing a `"type": "module"` banner.

**HOME-UI-04g: no flash on refresh of /next** (S, found live 2026-09-21). Refreshing `/next` showed a navy body flash and the old shell's `RouteSkeleton` before React painted the kit. Root cause: `NextRoutes` rendered its loading branch (a vendored `RouteSkeleton`) until the settings query resolved, and the body's `.dark`/`.style-*` classes were only applied by React hooks after mount, so the first paint used the old shell's palette. Fix: a per-browser `localStorage` cache (`frontend/src/next/shellNextCache.ts`, key `maipai.shell.next`) written by `useNextLook` (look) and `useNextAppearance` (theme) and read by `main.tsx`'s `applyCachedNextPalette()` before React mounts, so the first paint already carries the correct look and theme. `useShellNext` seeds its initial state from the cache (`on`/`off`/`loading`) instead of always starting at "loading", so a cached refresh skips the skeleton entirely. `NextRoutes` now calls `useNextLook` unconditionally at the top (fixing a Rules-of-Hooks violation caught by `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks`) and the loading branch is wrapped in a `data-testid` for the test suite. `useNextAppearance` stays inside `NextRoutesInner` under the kit's `ThemeProvider`. Tests: `shellNextCache.test.ts` (5 cases: round-trip, empty, malformed JSON, wrong shape, storage blocked) and `NextRoutes.test.tsx` (9 cases including "loading with no cache renders RouteSkeleton"). Frontend suite: 528 pass. `bun tsc --noEmit` and `bun eslint .` clean (one pre-existing warning in `chatModelAdapter.test.ts`).

## Slice 5(a): sources, no inline markers yet - two shipped-component gaps named first (2026-09-22)

**Why**: COORDINATOR's own slice 5 order, item (a): "sources and citations into the sources/inline-citation/document-reference Elements from the citation data the turn carries." A `design-resolver` pass (platform principle 6, "no hand-built UI") read the three new kit Elements, spec.md's "Inside a turn" section, and the retired page's own precedent before any line was written, since the shipped Elements' own gaps needed naming first.

**Decision, `elements/sources.tsx` only, per the resolver's own reading**: `blocks/chat/SourcesCard` is the pre-2026-09-21 kit block the retired page used (the whole point of the shell rebuild is that these retire as each page moves) - `elements/sources.tsx`'s `Sources` is the shipped replacement, used exactly as it ships. `document-reference.tsx` is a different feature entirely (fed by the `document` ArtifactSection's page/quote anchors, not by `TurnValue.sources`) - out of scope here, its own item when the document-reading turn shape lands. `inline-citation.tsx` is a static two-sentence demo (its citation markers are hardcoded into its own JSX text, not a renderer for arbitrary body text) with no exported way to reuse its internal `Citation` popover - inline `[N]` markers in reply prose are **not built this pass**, named as a gap below rather than forked or hand-rolled.

**Two real gaps in the shipped `Sources` Element itself, named before landing on it**:
1. **No link out.** `Sources`' own rows are `<div>`s, not anchors - a household member sees a source's title and domain but can't open it. The retired `SourcesCard` had this (`rel="noopener noreferrer"` and `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`, the exact privacy promise `spec/schemas/source.schema.json`'s own `url` field describes). A real regression in reach, not a hand-built workaround for it: filed as `getmaipai/commons#7` (an optional `href` per row) rather than reaching around the Element to add a link ourselves.
2. **React key collision risk.** `Sources` keys each row by `source.domain` (`elements/sources.tsx:53`); the backend dedupes citations by `url`, not host, and two different pages on the same site (two Wikipedia articles in one reply) produce two rows with the identical key. Not fixed client-side (deduping by domain would silently drop a real citation and break the `[N]` numbering the inline-marker gap below depends on later) - filed alongside the link gap in `getmaipai/commons#7` (key by array index instead).

**Inline body citation markers: a named gap, not started.** spec.md's own "citations in the body are superscript numbers that scroll the card open and highlight the row" needs two things neither exists yet: a text/markdown slot on `ThreadComponents` (today `MarkdownText` renders with no `components`/`preprocess` hook reachable from `Thread`'s own composition, `elements/thread.aui.tsx`), and `inline-citation.tsx`'s own `Citation` popover exported so a caller can actually place one per marker. Filed as `getmaipai/commons#8`; the existing tracked item (`docs/BACKLOG.md`'s "Inline citation markers on sourced answers") gets a status note pointing here rather than a second parallel tracking entry. Until it lands, a `[N]` marker in a reply's prose renders as literal text - the honest, harmless state CHAT-16's own spec already describes.

**Landed**: the sources card rides the same synthetic-tool-call-part composition slices 3/4/5(e) already use for `structured_part`/`write_document` (no `ThreadComponents` slot exists for "something under the reply" either) - `chatModelAdapter.ts`'s `done` content array gains a `toolName: "sources"` part (fixed name, `${turn_id}-sources` id, **after** the text part per spec.md's own "a compact card under the reply" - the "tool parts before text" rule from 5(e) was about the structured reference card specifically, not every tool part), `chatHistoryAdapter.ts`'s reload path mirrors it (unlike `structured_part`'s own #130 gap, `sources` survives reload today - the column already exists). `NextChatPage.tsx` registers a `SourcesToolRender` mapping spec's `Source{site, title, ...}` onto the Element's own `{domain, title}` (`domain` reads `site` - `source.schema.json`'s own description of `site` is "the hostname a citation chip shows," exactly what `domain` means), `open` a plain `useState`, collapsed by default per spec.md. A fixed `toolName: "sources"`, never keyed on the producing package (`websearch`/`weather`/etc.) - `weather` is already taken by the SpecSheet registration, and WEATHER-GEN-01 will give the weather package its own structured `sources`-shaped output later, a real collision if this reused the package name.

**A review caught two more real issues, both fixed before landing.** (1) the shared adapters send this same part to the still-live legacy `/chat` route too (`ChatPage.tsx`, via `thread.aui.tsx`), where nothing was registered for it - Thread's own chain-of-thought grouping tucked it behind a new, extraneous "1 tool call" trigger under that page's own already-correct `SourcesCard` (fed separately from `metadata.custom.sources`), one click from `ToolFallback`'s raw-JSON dump. Fixed with a no-op `useAssistantToolUI({ toolName: "sources", render: () => null, display: "standalone" })` registration (`SuppressLegacySourcesFallback`) - `display: "standalone"` matters here specifically: without it the null-rendering component still sits inside a `ToolGroupRoot`/`ToolGroupContent` (a Radix `Collapsible`), so the "1 tool call" trigger itself would still show (and, found live writing the regression test, that grouping combination also hung `bun test` outright - `display: "standalone"` sidesteps the whole group-rendering path, fixing both). (2) the same tool-call-part object literal was hand-built five times across both adapter files (platform principle 1, "one definition, one place") - extracted into a shared `toolCallPart()` helper (`chatToolCallPart.ts`), used at all five call sites.

## /next/chat's own full height, not a guessed vh-calc (2026-09-22)

**Why**: Jesse's own ChatGPT comparison (23:55) - the thread-list column and the composer both stopped ~60px short of the window's real bottom edge (the column's list cut mid-item with a gap below; the composer floating with empty space under it), where ChatGPT's own thread and sidebar both reach the window's bottom edge exactly.

**Root cause**: `FullLayout.tsx`'s own chain from `SidebarInset` down to the Outlet (`<main>` → a `flex flex-1 flex-col gap-4 p-4` body div → a plain `.container` block div → a plain `min-h-[calc(100vh-140px)]` outlet wrapper div → `Outlet`) is a stack of plain block divs that each shrink-wrap to their own content's height rather than stretching to fill the flex row above them - only the body div carries `flex-1`, and even that does nothing useful since its own single child (the container div) isn't `flex-1` itself, so no real height ever propagates down. `NextChatPage.tsx`'s own `next-chat-shell` compensated with a hardcoded `h-[calc(100vh-140px)]` - a guess at the header height plus assorted chrome that never quite matched what the real chain actually consumed (the guess undercounted; a real gap was left over).

**Landed**: `tokens.css` (the same `:has([data-slot="next-chat-shell"])` marker the width-cap and `overscroll-behavior` rules above already key on, no vendored file touched) turns every intervening block div into a real flex conduit: `main` (`SidebarInset`) gets a real, fixed `height: calc(100svh - 1rem)` (the 1rem is `SidebarInset`'s own `m-2` margin - a review caught this needing no width gate, see below); its body div and the container div below it both become `flex-1 min-h-0` columns; the container's own last child (`FullLayout.tsx`'s `<Footer/>` wrapper - `Footer` itself renders `null`, but its wrapper's `pt-6` still claimed real space) is hidden outright, since a full-height chat interface has no room for a trailing slot. `next-chat-shell` then reads `h-full` off that real chain instead of its own guessed number.

**Verified live** on 8787, 1440-equivalent width (this session's own real viewport, 1600×823): the sidebar inset's own bottom, `next-chat-shell`'s bottom, and the thread-list column's bottom all measure identically, `{top:8, bottom:815}` for the inset, `{top:81, bottom:815}` for the shell and the rail - pixel-exact. The composer sits 24px above that (`pb-6`, its own intentional bottom padding, not a leftover gap). **A review caught this**: the first version gated the `1rem` subtraction behind `@media (min-width: 720px)`, on the premise that `SidebarInset`'s own `m-2` was `md:`-gated the same way the component's own default `className` is. Reading `FullLayout.tsx:19` directly found that's wrong: it passes a SECOND, plain `m-2` in its own `className` prop, and `cn()`'s `twMerge` only dedupes classes sharing the identical variant chain, so the unconditional `m-2` coexists with the component's own gated `md:peer-data-[variant=inset]:m-2` rather than replacing it - the margin is real at every width. Fixed: no media query, the `1rem` is always subtracted.

**Not verified live**: any narrower width - this session's own browser-automation tool reports a fixed virtual viewport (`innerWidth` stayed 1600 through a `resize_window` call that did change the real OS window's `outerWidth`/`outerHeight`), so a real narrow-viewport probe wasn't possible here. The fix now has no width-conditional CSS at all (the media query was the bug, now removed), so the same `-1rem` applies uniformly - a named gap in live verification, not a claim of proof.

## CHAT-UI-03: six ChatGPT-comparison fixes, plus the sources trigger moving into the action bar (2026-09-22)

**Why**: a batch of six items from Jesse's own side-by-side against ChatGPT, delivered in three passes, plus a follow-up on the sources card (landed above) moving its trigger from a standalone row under the reply into the message's own action bar.

**Landed, `NextChatPage.tsx` (items 1-6, home-a2 side)**:
1. The thread-list column and its collapse/peek transition now animate (`transition-[width] duration-200 ease-linear`, the app rail's own duration/curve, `motion-reduce:transition-none` honoured) instead of a `hidden`/`block` jump-cut. `border-r`/`pr-2` moved into the width-bearing states only (open, peeked) - a review caught the un-conditioned version leaving a persistent ~9px bordered strip in the collapsed state, since `box-sizing: border-box` can't shrink padding/border below 0 alongside an animated `w-0`.
2. `ThreadListNew` ("New Thread") drops the `flex-1` it had - Jesse's own comparison read it as stretched full width beside the toggle; it keeps its natural button width now.
3. The rail's own toggle uses `getIcon("message-square")` instead of sharing `panel-left` with the app rail's own `SidebarTrigger` - the two read as the same button in two places. Wrapped in `Tooltip`/`TooltipTrigger`/`TooltipContent` (composed directly, not the kit's `TooltipIconButton` - that wrapper is icon-only, and this toggle needed the same tooltip API the rest of this page already uses for icon buttons), tooltip text "Conversations."
4. Kit fix (`tokens.css`) - see below.
5. Kit fix (`thread.aui.tsx`) - see below.
6. Below `RAIL_AUTO_COLLAPSE_MAX_WIDTH` (1024px), the rail now starts collapsed (`window.matchMedia` read once, lazily, as `railCollapsed`'s initial state) so it never covers the chat pane at a narrow width; hover-to-peek and click-to-pin both still work from the collapsed state. Untested visually below 1024px in this session (see the verification gap below); covered instead by `NextChatPage.test.tsx`'s own `window.matchMedia` stub.

**Landed, kit (`commons`, `ui-v0.5.27`)**: (4) a second `[data-slot="sidebar"][data-collapsible="icon"] [data-slot="sidebar-footer"] > .hide-menu { display: flex; }` rule in `tokens.css`, beside the CHAT-UI-01/HOME-UI-04b rule it's modeled on - the vendored `SidebarFooter`'s own wrapper around `NavUser` applies `hide-menu` to the WHOLE block (icons included), where `NavUser`'s own per-item label correctly scopes its own nested `hide-menu` to just the label span - so Settings/Help were disappearing entirely in icon-collapsed mode instead of collapsing to icons like every other rail item. (5) `UserMessage`'s own action-bar wrapper in `thread.aui.tsx` gets the same `min-h-7.5 pt-1.5` reserved height `AssistantMessage`'s own footer already had (`ACTION_BAR_HEIGHT`) - `ActionBarPrimitive.Root`'s `autohide` genuinely unmounts (`return null`), not just CSS-hides, so hovering a previous user message no longer shifts the layout below it when the row unmounts.

**Sources trigger moves into the action bar (Jesse's own follow-up, after the compact-list shape landed)**: the trigger is the last item in the bar's own row, after "More" - ghost style, stacked favicon glyphs of the first three sources plus the word "Sources," no pill, no count badge, no chevron (the count lives in the tooltip, "N sources"). Expanding shows the same compact list, now rendered below the whole footer row rather than inline with the reply text. Two more upstream-bound kit patches (`ui-v0.5.27`, both documented in `commons/ui/docs/dashboard-upstream.md`'s "Patches pending upstream" table): `ThreadComponents` gains `AssistantActionBarExtra` (last item in the bar) and `AssistantMessageFooterExtra` (a block-level sibling after the whole footer row, since the bar's own single icon row has no room for a multi-line list); `Sources` gains `hideTrigger` so `NextChatPage.tsx`'s own trigger and the Element's own content can share one lifted `open` state without the Element's bundled trigger showing twice. `SourceGlyph` is now exported so the bar-row trigger reuses the exact glyph the list itself uses, not a second hand-rolled copy.

**Two real bugs, both found by this session's own test run (not by the review) and fixed before landing**:
1. `sourcesFromMessage`'s selector returned a fresh array on every call (`.map()`); `useAuiState` is a `useSyncExternalStore` selector, which needs referential stability to settle - a fresh array on every read looked like "changed on every render" and threw "Maximum update depth exceeded" the moment any assistant message rendered. Fixed with a `WeakMap` cache keyed by the tool-call part itself (stable across renders unless its own content changes).
2. The lifted open/close state's `close` callback was a fresh closure inside a `useMemo` keyed on the state Set itself, so every toggle gave the trigger's own unmount-cleanup effect (added for the finding below) a new `close` identity - which re-armed the effect and ran the OLD closure's cleanup immediately, closing the panel the same click had just opened. Fixed with `useCallback`-wrapped, dependency-free `toggle`/`close` functions using only the functional form of `setState`.

**A review caught one more real interaction gap, fixed before landing**: `AssistantActionBar` sits inside `ActionBarPrimitive.Root`'s `autohide="not-last"`, which unmounts the whole bar - trigger included - on any earlier message once the pointer/focus leaves it. `SourcesFooterContent` is a plain sibling outside that root, so it doesn't autohide - without a fix, the panel would stay open with its own trigger gone, no visible way left to close it. Fixed: `SourcesActionBarTrigger` closes its own message's panel in its unmount-cleanup effect, matching the rest of the bar (every other control in the row already disappears on the same condition).

**Verified live on 8787** (this session's real viewport, ~1525×784): the sources trigger renders in the bar as the last item after "...", tooltip reads "N sources," clicking expands the compact list below the whole footer row and collapses it back on a second click; the rail's collapsed-toggle glyph (message-square) is visually distinct from the app rail's own `panel-left`, and hovering it peeks the rail showing "New Thread" at its natural width; the app rail's icon-collapsed mode shows Settings and Help as icons (gear, lifebuoy), not blank; hovering a non-last user message reveals its action row without moving the reply text below it by even a pixel (measured: `{top}` of the reply text identical before and during hover).

**Not verified live**: item 6's actual narrow-viewport behavior (1024px/768px) - the same `resize_window`-doesn't-change-`innerWidth` gap named in the full-height entry above. Covered instead by `NextChatPage.test.tsx`'s `window.matchMedia` stub test, not a claim of visual proof.

**Full gate**: `bash scripts/check.sh` (home-a2) - backend 3720 pass, frontend 611 pass, lint/build/a11y/docs/gitleaks/PII/licence all green. Kit: `bun test` 383 pass, `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint src` clean (both before and after the review-fix round).

## SRC-ICON-01: sources open their page and show the site's icon (2026-09-22)

**Why**: the owner's own ask - a reply's sources could be opened (the `Sources` panel expanded) but not clicked, and every row showed a letter glyph instead of the site's real icon. `elements/sources.tsx`'s own `Sources` (slice 5(a) above) renders rows as `<div>`s with no `href`, and a domain-derived letter, never a favicon - both named as shipped-component gaps at the time (`getmaipai/commons#7`) rather than reached around.

**Commons half (`c-99e5a`, `ui-v0.5.33`)**: vendored assistant-ui's own citation chip, `sources.aui.tsx` (`packages/ui/src/components/react/assistant-ui/elements/sources.aui.tsx` at assistant-ui main `0dd6d46b0`) into `ui/src/elements/`, unchanged except its import paths (`cn`, the kit's own `./ui/badge`) - `Source` (a real `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`), `SourceIcon` (a favicon `<img>`, letter fallback on error, an injectable `faviconUrl` prop), `SourceTitle`. `NOTICE` gained its own attribution line (the file's own path and commit, since it comes from a different upstream path/commit than the existing `apps/registry` entry above it). **Tagged twice**: `ui-v0.5.32` (the vendoring commit itself, `d95c0d0`) was cut without bumping `ui/package.json`'s own `version` field - home's own `scripts/check.sh` checks a consumed tag's worktree version against the tag name and refused it live. Fixed forward, not by force-moving the pushed tag: a second commit (`4f5f8c9`) bumps the version field alone, tagged `ui-v0.5.33`; `ui-v0.5.32` is left in place as a dead, never-valid tag (deleted from origin) rather than reused.

**Two review passes (2026-09-22) on the same gap, both fixed before landing**: `fetchFaviconBytes()`'s first version collapsed "every candidate gave a real HTTP answer, none was an icon" and "every candidate timed out or hit a DNS/TLS failure" into the same plain `null`, and `getFavicon()` cached both alike - a transient network blip on the hub's own side (not a fact about the site) got cached as "no favicon" for the full 30-day unused-expiry window. First fix: a three-way `FaviconFetchOutcome` (`found` / `confirmed_absent` / `network_failure`); `getFavicon()` only writes the negative cache entry for `confirmed_absent`, returning `network_failure` straight through uncached. **The re-review of that fix (fix-hunks only, per the org's own review budget) found the marker itself still too broad**: it latched true the instant a candidate's headers arrived, before the outcome was actually definitive - a 5xx/429 status (the server in trouble, not a fact about the icon) took the same `!response.ok` path as a real 404 and got counted as confirmed; a connection dropped mid-body-read (a genuine network failure) also latched the marker before `readCapped` ever got the chance to fail. Fixed: the marker (renamed `sawDefiniteAnswer`) is now set only at the three actually-definitive points - a 404/410 specifically (`packageHost.ts`'s own identical not-found-vs-unreachable line, not any other non-ok status), a rejected content type (the full header set already arrived, no body-read risk), and `readCapped`'s own deliberate oversized-body `null` (a genuine mid-read drop throws instead, landing in the `catch` untouched). Four new tests total (`favicons.test.ts`): a 503 and a mid-read drop both `network_failure`, alongside the original "every candidate times out" and `getFavicon`'s own "a network failure... is never cached."

**Home half (`c-99e5b`)**: `sourcesFromMessage()` (`NextChatPage.tsx`) now keeps `url` alongside `domain`/`title` (dropped before); both `SourcesActionBarTrigger`'s stacked glyphs and `SourcesFooterContent`'s open list compose `Source`/`SourceIcon`/`SourceTitle` directly (no hand-built row - the kit's own `Collapsible`/`CollapsibleContent`, styled with the `collapsePanel` token the old `Sources` card's own panel used, replaces that card for this one caller), keyed by `url` (composer.ts's `sourceRows()` already dedupes by `url`, so it's stable - domain collides across two pages on the same site, index doesn't survive a reorder). `faviconUrl` points every `SourceIcon` at the hub's own `/api/favicon?domain=<host>` route, never the shipped default (`icons.duckduckgo.com`, a third-party call straight from the browser).

**The favicon route (`backend/src/routes/favicon.ts`, `lib/favicons.ts`)**: `GET /api/favicon?domain=<host>` (zod-openapi, `requireAuth`) validates `host` as a bare public hostname (no path, credentials, or port; not `localhost`; not a private/loopback/link-local address - reusing `@maipai/core/src/ssrfGuard`'s `assertNotPrivateHost`, the identical check `packageHost.ts`'s own outbound fetch already runs, not a second copy), then tries `https://<host>/favicon.ico` then `/apple-touch-icon.png` (10s timeout each, 64 KB cap, only an `image/*` content type accepted), falling back to a 204. The result - found or confirmed-absent - is cached under `<dataDir>/favicons/` (an `index.json` of `{ext, contentType, bytes, lastUsedAt}` per host, one file per found icon) so a site is asked at most once; a new daily core job, `favicons.sweep` (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `ensureCoreJob` in `index.ts`), deletes an entry unused for 30 days and evicts the oldest-unused entries first if the cache is still over its 20 MB ceiling.

**A pre-build check, per the work order**: does the vendored `SourceIcon`'s letter-fallback render sensibly on a 204? Read its own source first - `hasError` flips the moment the `<img>`'s `onerror` fires, and a 204 (no body) is exactly that: no decodable image, so the browser fires `onerror` the same as any other failed load, and the letter glyph renders. No special-casing needed on either side.

**Tests**: backend `tests/favicons.test.ts` (`validateFaviconHost` - accepts a bare hostname, rejects empty/path/credentials/localhost/a private or loopback IP; `fetchFaviconBytes` - first-candidate success, falls back to the second, rejects a non-image content type, rejects over the 64 KB cap, null when neither candidate answers; `getFavicon` - a miss caches and a repeat call makes no further fetch, a confirmed absence is cached too; `sweepFavicons` - an entry over 30 days unused is deleted and a fresh one stays, the oldest-unused entries are evicted first over the 20 MB cap) and `tests/faviconRoute.test.ts` (the route rejects not-signed-in/empty/path/localhost/a private IP with 401/400, a cache hit makes no second fetch, no icon is a 204) - `assertNotPrivateHost`'s own DNS step is stubbed (`__setFaviconDnsLookupForTests`) so the route-level host-validation tests stay deterministic and offline rather than depending on a fake `*.example.com` subdomain actually resolving. Frontend: `NextChatPage.test.tsx`'s sources test (renamed from the slice 5(a) version it replaces) now asserts the open row is a real link (`href` the source's own `url`, `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`) and that `SourceIcon` was handed the hub's own `/api/favicon?domain=...` URL - happy-dom has no real image decoder (the same gap `sttSocket.test.ts` already names for WebSocket), so every `<img>` it creates ends up in the letter-fallback state regardless of what the src actually was; proven instead by capturing the `src` value the component assigned (`HTMLImageElement.prototype.src` overridden for just this test, restored after) rather than reading it back off a real `<img>`.

**Screenshots**: not added to `scripts/screenshot.ts`'s own published matrix (no new route, just this one card's own content) - verified instead with a throwaway headless run against a real backend and a real production build on spare ports (`.demo-data`-style isolation, never 8787 or the real data dir), two real citations (`wikipedia.org`, a real `favicon.ico`; `example.com`, confirmed to have none), `/next/chat`'s sources panel opened, light and dark. Both images opened and judged: the Wikipedia row shows a real round favicon image fetched through `/api/favicon`; the Example Domain row shows the letter fallback (`E`), proving the 204 path renders sensibly with no special-casing needed; every row's `href`/`target`/`rel`/`referrerpolicy` and the favicon `<img>`'s own `src` were also read straight off the live DOM (not just eyeballed) and matched exactly.

**Full gate**: [to be filled after `scripts/check.sh` in `home-src-links`].

## Slice 5(b): the tool timeline, consumer before producer (2026-09-22)

**Why**: COORDINATOR's own slice 5 order, item (b) - the tool-timeline Element from the wiring table, "against the tool parts that exist." TOOL-EVENTS-01 (`docs/BACKLOG.md`) has its spec half tagged (`spec-v0.1.16`, `spec/schemas/turn-stream-event.schema.json` and its Zod mirror `spec/stack/ts/turn-stream-event.ts`) but its backend half (`backend/src/routes/turn.ts`, `turnEngine.ts` actually emitting `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`tool_error`) is a separate lane's own in-progress work, not landed here. A `design-resolver` pass read the kit's `ToolTimeline` Element, TOOL-EVENTS-01's own backlog line and dev.md handoff note, and the tagged wire shape before any code was written, since the item's own scope depends entirely on what's real on the wire today (nothing) versus what the spec already promises (a real, typed shape).

**Decision, the resolver's own recommendation**: build the frontend consumer end to end now, proven by scripted streams, the same "consumer before producer" order slice 5(a)'s sources card and slice 4's artifact card both landed in (sources rendered nothing live until CHAT-16 started emitting it; the artifact card was proven only against a scripted response because #131 blocked a real turn at the time). Not a bare registration stub, not a `done`-event fallback reconstructed from `plugin_id`/routing internals - `TurnValue` and the persisted `ToolExecutionOutcome[]` batch (`conversation_turns.outcomes`) carry no per-step start/timing data today, and deriving one from routing diagnostics would be exactly the Home-drawn narrative SHELL-02's own acceptance rules out first.

**Landed**: pin bump to `spec-v0.1.16` (`scripts/check.sh`, `backend/package.json`, `frontend/package.json` - both backend and frontend share one `SPEC_TAG`), `bun install --force` in both. `frontend/src/apps/chat/chatModelAdapter.ts` parses `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`tool_error` inside the same stream loop as `reasoning`/`delta` - these events are keyed by `t`, not `type` (a genuinely separate discriminant from backend/src/wire.ts's own `TurnStreamEvent` union, which `readTurnStream`'s return type is pinned to and has no such member yet), so they're intercepted via `ToolTurnStreamEvent.safeParse(event)` (the spec's own Zod schema) before the existing `event.type` chain runs, the same "cast/parse ahead of a not-yet-real wire member" shape Lane 11 item 1's `status` event used before it was real either. An insertion-ordered `Map<call_id, {packageId, state}>` becomes a `tool_timeline` tool-call part (`toolCallPart`, the same helper every other synthetic part already uses) whenever it's non-empty, placed BEFORE the text part (slice 5(e)'s rule: a trace of what ran while producing this answer reads above its own sentence, not under it like sources). `NextChatPage.tsx` registers `ToolTimelineTool` (`toolName: "tool_timeline"`, fixed, joining the reserved-name list `weather`/`almanac-date`/`sources` already keep) rendering the kit's `ToolTimeline` Element - `steps` from the map (`verb` a 3-state copy table: "Running"/"Ran"/"Failed", `chip` the package id, `wrench` icon), `stats: []` (no per-file diff-stat producer anywhere in Home; the kit's own upstream use is a coding-agent timeline, a real, named gap here, not invented data), collapsed by default.

**The one seam left alone, per the resolver's own reading of "leave it for the start event"**: a `tool_call` with no matching `tool_result`/`tool_error` yet is the ONLY thing that creates a step in the running "streaming" state - this pass consumes that event rather than synthesizing one from anywhere else. An orphan `tool_result`/`tool_error` (a `call_id` this stream never saw a `tool_call` for) is silently ignored rather than inventing a step with no start, tested explicitly (`chatModelAdapter.test.ts`).

**Real today, but not yet real in the app**: nothing in the running product emits `tool_call`/`tool_result`/`tool_error` - TOOL-EVENTS-01's backend half hasn't landed - so this renders nothing on 8787 today; not live-verified for that reason, proven instead by `chatModelAdapter.test.ts` (a tool_call+tool_result pair, a tool_call left running, a tool_error, two interleaved calls, an orphan result - 5 new cases) and one `NextChatPage.test.tsx` render case (collapsed by default, the package id visible on expand). ## Slice 5(c): the thinking indicator - a real wire event, not scaffolding (2026-09-22)

**Why**: COORDINATOR's own slice 5 order, item (c) - the `thinking-indicator` Element from the wiring table's "Thinking before the reply" row. **Landed**: the legacy `/chat` route (`frontend/src/apps/chat/thread.aui.tsx`) already had this exact behavior - its own "indicator" case reads `useTurnActivity()` (the `status`/`spoken_cue` text) plus a 45s "still working" timer, rendered as hand-drawn prose (`<span>● {text}</span>`). `/next/chat` never got the port.
