The kit itself needed one more upstream-bound patch (`ui-v0.5.29`): `elements/thread.aui.tsx`'s `ThreadComponents` gained an `Indicator?: ComponentType` slot, and its own unset default now renders `ThinkingIndicator` too (label "Thinking…") instead of the hand-drawn `<span>●</span>` it had before - a real Element in place of hand-built UI, independent of Home, so every OTHER caller of the vendored Element benefits too. `NextChatPage.tsx` passes `Indicator: ChatThinkingIndicator` to override it with the real activity text.

**Cleanup, found doing this**: `chatTurnActivity.ts` had an unused `TurnStatusEvent` type (a forward-compatible stub from before `status` was real, never imported anywhere) - deleted outright rather than left as dead code. Its own header comment and one in `chatModelAdapter.ts` both still claimed `status` "isn't a real TurnStreamEvent member yet" - fixed to say what's actually true now.

**Verified live** on 8787: asked a question that forces a websearch lookup - the activity line ("Checking that for you." and similar package-authored text) shows through the real `ThinkingIndicator` Element while the lookup runs, then clears the moment the reply's text starts streaming. Also proven by a genuinely staggered-stream test (`NextChatPage.test.tsx`, `staggeredNdjsonStream` - not a fully-synchronous stream, since the whole point is observing a state that exists only mid-turn): a `status` event's text shows, then clears once the reply arrives. Frontend suite: 619 pass (618 + 1 new). Full `check.sh` green.

## Two real chat-column bugs, both from Jesse's own eyes on the live column (2026-09-22)

**Why**: two defects Jesse found using the column after CHAT-UI-03/the sources work landed, flagged as priority over the PR-2 queue: the hover peek was reflowing the chat pane (it should be a pure overlay), and the collapse-click's own phantom-peek suppression had regressed.

**Bug 1: the peek reflowed the chat pane.** Root cause: the row spaced the rail off the pane with a shared `gap-4`, but `gap` only counts a FLOW sibling. `next-chat-rail` is flow (a real `w-0` flex participant) when collapsed-not-peeked, but `position: absolute` when peeked (removed from flow to become a pure overlay, by design) - that flow/absolute swap fired on every hover, not just a click, changing whether `gap-4` applied before the pane and bumping its left edge in and out on every peek. Fixed by decoupling the pane's own spacing from the rail's flow status entirely: the row's `gap-4` is gone, and the chat pane (now marked `data-slot="next-chat-pane"`) carries its own `ms-4`/`ms-0` margin keyed on `railCollapsed` alone, animated in step with the rail's own `transition-[width]` so a real click (the only thing that changes `railCollapsed`) still slides smoothly - `railPeeked` never enters into it. The artifact and bare-compare canvas panels, the row's other two flow siblings, pick up the `ms-4` `gap-4` used to give them directly, since they're always-flow and never touched by this specific bug.

**Bug 2: the collapse-click's own peek suppression had regressed.** `suppressHoverPeekRef` (landed earlier, suppressing the click-triggered DOM swap's own phantom `pointerenter` on the freshly-mounted collapsed toggle) was cleared by `handleToggleLeave` on ANY pointerleave of either toggle instance - including one the OUTGOING (inline) toggle itself fires, incidentally, as part of the very same hit-test recomputation that fires the phantom enter on the incoming one a moment later (the same stationary pointer, no real transition). That incidental leave raced ahead of the phantom enter and cleared the flag before it was ever checked, exactly undoing the original fix. Tried `relatedTarget` first (the same signal `closeRailPeek` already uses to tell a real departure from an incidental one) and found it untestable: happy-dom never reports an unspecified `relatedTarget` as falsy the way a real browser does (it defaults to `window`), so a test can't represent "no real destination" with it at all. Fixed with real pointer movement instead: `suppressPointerOriginRef` records the click's own `clientX`/`clientY`, and `handleToggleLeave` only clears the flag when a later leave reports DIFFERENT coordinates - the incidental leave/enter pair a DOM swap fires under a stationary pointer report the exact same ones the click did (the OS cursor hasn't moved), so it's ignored; any leave following a genuine hand movement reports different ones and clears it correctly.

**A permanent regression test for each**, both added before the fix (confirmed red, then green after): the pane-spacing test asserts the pane's own className is byte-identical between collapsed-not-peeked and peeked (and differs only after a real click), and the suppression test fires the exact missing event (`fireEvent.pointerLeave` on the outgoing toggle, with no real movement) the original bug's own test never exercised - it reproduced the regression precisely before the fix. Four existing tests representing a genuine re-hover now pass explicit, different `clientX`/`clientY` alongside their existing `relatedTarget: document.body`, since the coordinate check needed them to actually look different rather than share the click's own default `(0, 0)`. `NextChatPage.test.tsx`: 24 pass (22 + 2 new).

**Not verified live, named honestly rather than faked**: both bugs (and the desktop rail itself) only apply at or above the kit's own `lg` breakpoint (960px, `tokens.css`) - this session's real browser viewport is fixed at 500px wide with no override available (the same `resize_window`-doesn't-change-`innerWidth` gap this file has named several times before), so neither a real hover-peek nor a real open-column click could be exercised in an actual rendered layout this session. The `fireEvent`-based tests above are the rigorous substitute: they drive the exact same event handlers a real browser would, with precise control over event sequencing a live probe couldn't give anyway (the whole point was reproducing a specific event-ordering race). A session with a genuinely wide real viewport should still confirm both fixes visually before calling this closed.

**A review caught a real gap in the coordinate-based fix itself**: a keyboard-synthesized click (Enter/Space on the focused toggle, `detail: 0` per spec) always reports `clientX`/`clientY` (0, 0), unrelated to wherever the real mouse actually is - comparing a later leave's own real coordinates against that meaningless origin would never match, permanently blocking a legitimate mouse hover from ever reopening the peek after a keyboard-driven collapse. Fixed: `handleToggleClick` records `null` (no origin) instead of `(0, 0)` when `e.detail === 0`, and `handleToggleLeave` treats a `null` origin as "clear unconditionally on the first leave," the same behavior this mechanism had before the coordinate check existed - correct for a keyboard interaction, where there's no real mouse position to protect against in the first place. Surfaced a second, quieter environment quirk while writing this test: `fireEvent.click()` in this suite's own happy-dom setup also defaults `detail` to `0` (not the `1` a genuine mouse click carries in a real browser) - every existing toggle-click call in this describe block now passes `{ detail: 1 }` explicitly to keep representing a real mouse click under the new check, the dedicated keyboard test the one exception with `{ detail: 0 }`. A new regression test proves the keyboard case doesn't get stuck. `NextChatPage.test.tsx`: 25 pass (24 + 1 new). Frontend suite: 622 pass.

**Two more review findings, judged and left alone, not silently dropped**: (1) the toggle is two separately-mounted `Button` instances the browser hit-test-recomputes on every swap, which is the actual root cause behind both this regression and the original phantom-enter bug it was built to fix - the reviewer's own suggestion (one stable node repositioned via CSS, the same pattern `next-chat-rail` itself already uses) would remove this whole class of bug at the source instead of patching each newly-discovered symptom. Not done this pass: a real redesign of an already-heavily-iterated toggle mechanism, on top of two urgent bug fixes Jesse wanted "before anything else," is a bigger, riskier change than this item's own scope - filed as a real simplification opportunity for a later pass, not a defect in what shipped. (2) the artifact and compare canvas panels each hardcode their own literal `ms-4` instead of sharing one declaration with the pane's own conditional margin - accepted as consistent with this codebase's own Tailwind convention (a utility class is the literal, not a JS constant referenced from several places), and the three spots are visually and behaviorally adjacent enough in the same file that a future spacing change is unlikely to miss one silently.

## Slice 5(d): Details, the stats reveal - two Elements ship, three real gaps named (2026-09-22)

**Why**: COORDINATOR's own slice 5 order, item (d) - the "..." menu's Details entry (`CompareWithBareModelMenuItem`'s own comment named it as a placeholder back in slice 5(e)). The wiring table names five Elements (`cost-meter`, `context-breakdown`, `context-display`, `trace-waterfall`, `message-timing`), source "turn stats from the backend." Checked `TurnStats` (`backend/src/wire.ts`) against each Element's own prop shape before writing anything, since "turn stats from the backend" undersold how differently-shaped the five actually are - this was reported to COORDINATOR as bigger than an hour before starting, per the standing instruction, and the reply is the scope below.

**Landed**: `message-timing` and `context-display` ship in Details. `MessageDetailsMenuItem` (the "..." menu's own second entry, `AssistantMoreItems`) has no admin gate of its own - `TurnStats` (timing, token counts) isn't sensitive the way "compare against the bare model" is, and every household member already sees the reply itself; it renders only when the message actually carries `stats` (a reload'd or tool-sourced turn without them shows no Details entry at all, not an empty one). Clicking it toggles a lifted-by-`turnId` open state (`DetailsOpenContext`, the identical shape `SourcesOpenContext` already has, simpler here since the trigger lives inside the "More" menu itself, never exposed to the bar's own autohide unmount risk `SourcesActionBarTrigger` has to guard against). The reveal itself joins `SourcesFooterContent` in the SAME `AssistantMessageFooterExtra` slot (one wrapper, `MessageFooterExtra`, composing both - each keyed by its own open state, no shared logic between them): `MessageTiming` renders a flat `{label, value}[]` built straight from `time_to_first_token_ms`/`total_time_ms`/`tokens_per_second`/`engine` (`buildTimingStats`), and `ContextDisplay.Bar` (admin-only, since it needs `api.engines()`, an owner/admin-gated route) renders when the currently-loaded chat role's own `measuredContextLength` (the Stack roles API, the wiring table's "Model choice" row's own source) is available, mapping `usage.totalTokens`/`inputTokens`/`outputTokens`/`cachedInputTokens` from `context_tokens`/`prompt_tokens`/`predicted_tokens`/`cache_reuse_tokens`.

**`cost-meter` does not apply, by COORDINATOR's own explicit call**: local inference has no per-turn price, and a self-hosted product inventing a "compute cost" would be a number nobody can act on. Dropped from Details entirely, not redefined into a compute meter - recorded in the wiring table as not applicable.

**`context-breakdown` is the one that survives long-term, not `context-display`**: `context-breakdown` wants per-category segments (system/history/current) against a limit - what an admin actually reads - but `TurnStats` has no segment data today, only one aggregate `context_tokens`. `context-display` (its coarser, total-only cousin) ships in its place for now because it maps to real fields; [CTX-SEG-01](https://github.com/getmaipai/home/issues/133) (S, backend) tracks the segment data, and `context-breakdown` retires `context-display` from Details the day it lands - the wiring table carries this note so a future session doesn't build both.

**`trace-waterfall` needs real per-phase spans `TurnStats` doesn't have** - routing, a lookup, a tool call, generation, each with a start and duration. Not built this pass rather than faked with invented spans; [TRACE-SPANS-01](https://github.com/getmaipai/home/issues/134) (M, backend) tracks it, wanted by ADMIN-PERF-01 and the bare-model compare tool's own trace column too, so it's not orphan work.

**A real backend gap found scoping this, not previously named**: `context_used_percent` (`TurnStats`) is a permanent, hardcoded `null` in `backend/src/lib/turnStats.ts` - never computed, not a transient bug. COORDINATOR's own first-pass instruction was to derive `modelContextWindow` from `context_tokens / context_used_percent` if the Engines API came up empty; found this wasn't viable (dividing by a field that's always `null`) before implementing it, so the fallback is "leave the context bar out" instead - a message with no measured chat role, or no Stack configured at all (`roles: []`, the common case today per `routes/engines.ts`'s own header comment), shows `MessageTiming` alone, correctly, rather than a bar built on a fabricated window.

**Verified live** on 8787 against a real turn: Details shows in the "..." menu only for a message with real stats, reveals "First token 5.1s · Total 5.4s · Speed 39 tok/s · Engine local qwen3-8b-instruct-q4-k-m" on click (real numbers, not fixture data), and the context bar correctly does not appear on this dev machine (no Stack configured here) - toggling Details closed again removes the reveal. 4 new tests (`NextChatPage.test.tsx`): the menu entry hides with no stats, timing reveals on click, the context bar shows once the Stack reports a measured role, the context bar stays out when it doesn't. Frontend suite: 626 pass (622 + 4 new).

**A review caught two real bugs in the context bar's own data mapping, both fixed before landing**: (1) `totalTokens` was set to `context_tokens` alone, which `turnStats.ts` defines as a bare alias for `prompt_tokens` - a turn's own `predicted_tokens` (what it actually generated) never counted toward the percent-full reading at all. Fixed: `totalTokens` is now `prompt_tokens + predicted_tokens`, the real post-turn context size. (2) `cachedInputTokens` was mapped from `cache_reuse_tokens`, but that field is ADDITIVE to `prompt_tokens` in this backend's own math (`turnStats.ts`'s own `cacheDenominator = cacheTokens + promptTokens`), not a SUBSET of it the way `ContextDisplay`'s own contract assumes a provider's cached-token count is - on a turn with heavy cache reuse, the tooltip could show a "Cached input" segment reading larger than "Input" itself, self-contradictory for the admin using this to judge context pressure. Fixed: `cachedInputTokens` is left out of the mapping entirely rather than mapped to a field with the wrong shape. Also caught: the query used its own `["engines-overview"]` cache key instead of `["engines"]`, the key `NextEnginesPage.tsx` already uses for the identical `api.engines()` call - an admin with Engines already loaded got a second, independently-stale network round trip here instead of reusing react-query's own cache entry. Fixed to share the key.

## The rail's third pane-jitter report: only a click may ever ease the width (2026-09-22)

Jesse's third report of the same bug, this time with the exact repro: "when it's collapsed and I mouse out, the right pane animates when it should just stay still." `transition-[width]` sat on the rail's own base className unconditionally (`NextChatPage.tsx`), so *any* width change animated, not only a click-driven one - closing the peek flips the node from `absolute w-64` (out of flow, harmless) to `static w-0` (in flow, so the chat pane got squeezed by the shrinking box for the transition's own 200ms). A new `railWidthAnimating` flag now gates the transition classes, `cn()` dropping the whole entry when it's false so the property is genuinely absent, not merely overridden - only `handleToggleClick` ever sets it true; no hover handler (`handleToggleEnter`, `handleToggleLeave`, `closeRailPeek`) calls `startRailWidthAnimation` at all, a source-level guarantee a hover interaction can never animate the width. Cleared on the rail's own `onTransitionEnd` (`e.target === e.currentTarget && e.propertyName === "width"`, so a bubbled child transition can't trip it) - the normal path for a real click-driven width change. Landed `288ab082`.

**A fallback exists because not every click-driven state change is a real width VALUE change**: clicking the peeked toggle to open fully goes `absolute w-64` -> `static w-64` - the identical width, so no "width" `transitionend` ever fires to clear the flag. `motion-reduce` is the other case (the transition never runs at all). First cut: a plain `setTimeout(200)` scheduled synchronously inside the click handler. **A review caught this racing ahead of the real transition**: a CSS transition's own clock starts at the next paint, not the instant this class flips in JS, so the JS timer fired a few ms before the genuine `transitionend` and truncated the animation early on *every* click, not just the no-value-change case the fallback exists for. Fixed by deferring the timer's own scheduling one `requestAnimationFrame` (the same "wait for the committed frame" pattern this file's own toggle-focus effect already used), so its clock starts close to when the real one does.

**Live verification on 8787 found a second, real gap neither review pass caught**: this session's own automation tab is genuinely backgrounded (`document.visibilityState === "hidden"`, `document.hasFocus() === false`), and `requestAnimationFrame` confirmed not firing within 1000ms there - the browser's own spec'd throttle for a tab that isn't actively painting. The rAF-deferred fallback above would never run in that state, leaving `railWidthAnimating` stuck `true` (quietly reintroducing the original bug for hover, on that tab, until the next real click's own `transitionend` happened to clear it). Fixed with a second, hard backstop: a plain `setTimeout(600)`, scheduled synchronously alongside the rAF (not chained after it, so it can't reintroduce the early-truncation race above), padded well past the real ~200ms so it never wins the normal foregrounded case. Landed `f10340a1`.

**What was and wasn't actually watched live, honestly**: the click path was directly exercised on 8787 by dispatching real events against the running production build (not just tests) and reading the rail's own live `className` at measured intervals - this is what caught the backstop gap, proving the fix's actual browser behavior, not just its happy-dom behavior. The hover/peek path itself (the literal "watch the pane hold still" ask) could not be watched visually: this session's real Chrome viewport is fixed at 500px wide (`resize_window` doesn't change the real `window.innerWidth` - a previously-documented constraint, reconfirmed here), under the kit's own `--breakpoint-lg: 960px`, so the desktop rail never renders at this viewport at all (`hidden ... lg:block`) and dispatching synthetic `PointerEvent`s at the underlying React handlers directly did not reliably reproduce the same peek-opening behavior `fireEvent.pointerEnter`/`pointerLeave` triggers in the test suite (a real-Chrome/React-19 event-delegation gap from the test harness's own event simulation, not chased further). The hover path's correctness rests on two things instead: the source-level guarantee above (no hover handler can reach `startRailWidthAnimation`), and two tests exercising it directly (`NextChatPage.test.tsx`, the "hovering the peek open or closed never animates" and "the fallback timeout clears the animating flag..." cases). Frontend suite: 629 pass.

## RESP-04 (f): the composer's thinking control, and why it isn't Popover (2026-09-22)

COORDINATOR's ruling (2026-09-22, after the scope report below) shrank slice (f) to one control: build the thinking-effort toggle, not the model picker. Three reasons, all confirmed against the code before the ruling landed: no `model` field exists anywhere in the request path (`api.streamTurn`'s options, `backend/src/routes/turn.ts`'s own body type - `thinking?: boolean` only, both copies); the Engines API's `roles` list is "commonly empty" today per its own route comment, so a picker would usually have nothing to pick from; and `reasoning-effort.tsx`'s `spent`/`budget` assume a reasoning-token-budget `TurnStats` has no field for. RESP-04's own text already named the fallback for exactly this: fold Instant/Thinking into one menu. The model picker becomes its own item, MODEL-SEL-01 (`docs/BACKLOG.md`), backend-first and gated on the Stack actually serving two or more chat models - not this session's.

**The kit patch**: `ThreadComponents` (`commons-a/ui/src/elements/thread.aui.tsx`) gains an optional `ComposerExtra?: ComponentType` slot, rendered in `ComposerAction` beside the attach button - the same append-point shape `AssistantMoreItems`/`AssistantActionBarExtra`/`AssistantMessageFooterExtra`/`Indicator` already established for the message side, just on the composer's own row. Default unset, no existing caller's render changes. Landed `ui-v0.5.31` (`commons` `b8b7cc4`); `home-a2` pinned to it in the same landing, which also finally pinned the still-outstanding `ui-v0.5.30` (the sources truncation fix, cut days earlier and never pinned in - a loose end from PR 7962's own landing, closed here rather than left for a session to hit cold).

**The control itself**: `ComposerThinkingControl` (`NextChatPage.tsx`) composes `composer.tsx`'s own `ComposerModelTrigger`/`ComposerMenu`/`ComposerModelItem` - used exactly as they ship, despite the "Model" naming, since their actual shape (a trigger showing the current label, a menu of `{name, meta}` entries with a selected checkmark) is generic. `ThinkingModeContext` threads the mode down (the same lifted-context shape `SourcesOpenContext`/`DetailsOpenContext` already use, since `ComposerExtra` is a bare `ComponentType` slot with no props). Wired to `useNextChatRuntime`'s `consumeThinking()` - a real implementation now, not the `() => true` stub slice 5(d) left behind - via the identical one-shot `thinkingRef` read-and-reset pattern `ChatPage.tsx`'s own "Think longer" toggle already uses: per-turn only, reset to Instant the moment a send consumes it, never remembered across turns. That's deliberate, not a shortcut: `conversation.schema.json` (`spec-v0.1.17`) is `additionalProperties: false` with no settings field at all, so "remembered per person with the conversation" (RESP-04's own text) is a real spec change - COORDINATOR filed `PERSIST-CONV-01` for that chain, and it isn't built here. A `localStorage` cache was considered and ruled out for the same reason `shellNextCache.ts` doesn't fit: it's device-local, and the same conversation opened on a different device would silently show a different mode.

**Two real defects, both caught by review, neither shipped**:

1. `ComposerMenu`'s own `open` only ever toggles opacity/scale (CSS) - it never unmounts its children, so a closed menu's two buttons stayed in tab order and in the accessibility tree, reachable by keyboard before Send even when visually gone. Fixed with `inert={!open}` on the menu, the same fix already used on the rail above (`NextChatPage.tsx`'s `inert={railCollapsed && !railPeeked}`) - a real HTML mechanism, not a bespoke `tabIndex`/`aria-hidden` pair on every item. Worth naming: `@testing-library`'s role queries in this suite's own happy-dom environment don't actually enforce `inert`'s exclusion from the accessibility tree (`menuItems()` still finds the buttons via `getByRole` regardless) - the regression test checks the `inert` attribute directly rather than trusting a query the test environment doesn't model faithfully.

2. The first cut dismissed the menu with a hand-rolled `useEffect`: a `document.addEventListener("pointerdown"/"keydown")` pair, attached only while open, closing on an outside click or Escape. A review caught this as a "no hand-built UI" defect (platform principle 6: "a maintained library for a solved problem beats hand-rolled logic doing the identical job") - the review's own citation was the *identical* call already made in this program five days earlier, the rail's hover-to-peek first draft (a hand-rolled `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` pair), replaced by the shipped `HoverCard` after a review found it had no keyboard/focus path. The review's suggested fix, though, was `Popover` - the primitive `ChatPage.tsx`'s own "Think longer" toggle already uses for this exact per-turn concept - and that turned out to be wrong: a `design-resolver` pass found `Popover.Content` renders through `@radix-ui/react-popper`'s `useFloating`, which sets its own inline `transform`/position style on the floating element even without a `Portal` - it would have overridden `ComposerMenu`'s own `absolute bottom-full` composer-anchored positioning, the actual shipped Element's actual shipped look. The real fix is one layer lower: `DismissableLayer.Root` (`radix-ui/internal`, already a dependency - the same package `Popover` itself composes) has no positioning opinion at all, so wrapping the control's whole root in it (trigger and menu both, not the menu alone - wrapping only the menu reintroduces a dismiss-then-reopen bug on the trigger's own click, which is why `Popover`'s own non-modal content does an explicit `targetIsTrigger` check) removes the hand-rolled listeners entirely while leaving `ComposerMenu` pixel-identical to how it ships. Net two lines in place of fifteen, plus real behavior the hand-rolled version didn't have: Escape only dismisses the topmost mounted layer (`isHighestLayer`), not whichever menu happens to be open underneath a dialog.

**A gap named for the next consumer, per principle 6 ("when nothing shipped does the job, the gap is named before a line is written")**: `ComposerMenu` ships with no dismiss behavior of its own, and `Popover` cannot be used to add it without fighting the Element's own positioning - `DismissableLayer` is Home's own composition around it, not a kit patch, since `ComposerMenu` has no other consumer anywhere in `commons-a` or `home-a2` yet ("one definition, one place" applies at the second consumer, not the first). If `MODEL-SEL-01` needs the same wiring for a second composer menu, promote it into the kit as `ComposerMenu` gaining an optional `onDismiss`, through the "Patches pending upstream" mechanism, rather than copying this file's own version.

**Also found, not this item's to fix**: the kit vendored `elements-model-selector` (`commons-a/ui/src/elements/model-selector.tsx`) months before this slice - a full `Popover` + `cmdk` model picker whose own `ModelSelectorEffort` row renders exactly a "Thinking" label with low/med/high radios. It is not the right part for this control (its effort row is a sub-component of a model list, and RESP-04's own text already gives the Instant/Thinking fallback its own shape), but it is very likely the shipped answer once `MODEL-SEL-01` lands - and it would put a second, `Popover`-styled menu convention in the same composer beside `ComposerMenu`'s own composer-anchored one. Named here so `MODEL-SEL-01` decides that deliberately rather than discovering it mid-build. Separately: `commons-a/ui/docs/dashboard-upstream.md`'s "Patches pending upstream" table has four rows (five now, with `ComposerExtra`) sitting at "pending - PR not yet opened" - the doc's own text calls a row left there across a session the defect the note exists to catch. Flagged to COORDINATOR, not fixed here.

**Verified**: `bash scripts/check.sh` in `commons-a/ui` (383 pass) and `home-a2` (frontend suite, 634 pass, `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` both clean). 5 new tests (`NextChatPage.test.tsx`): the trigger's default label and the menu's two entries, opening the menu and picking Thinking, outside-click dismissal, Escape dismissal, and a real turn send resetting the mode back to Instant. **Live on 8787, unlike the rail entry above**: the composer isn't `lg:`-gated, so this session's own fixed 500px viewport didn't block it. The trigger reads "Instant" beside the attach button; clicking it opens `ComposerMenu` anchored directly above the trigger (composer-anchored, not floating elsewhere - the actual reason `Popover` was ruled out, confirmed by eye); picking "Thinking" updates the trigger and closes the menu; sending a real turn reset the trigger back to "Instant" the moment Send was clicked, before the reply even arrived - the one-shot consume, watched, not just asserted in a test.

## ADMIN-COMPARE-01 (b): the compare switch, and the seam that kept the safety floor unskippable (2026-09-22)

COORDINATOR's ruling on the three open questions from the scope report: (1) take the extraction - one shared bypass function both bare-mode features call, never a branch inside `turnEngine.ts`'s own routing; (2) the switch lives beside feature (a) in the "..." menu, same concept family, no new surface; (3) the switch is ephemeral, session-local React state, never persisted - a mode that changes what the assistant IS must not be able to outlive the investigation that turned it on, and while it's on, it has to be obvious (a persistent banner, not a toast).

**The hard constraint, made structural rather than documented**: bare mode removes persona, routing, packages, and the quality guards (`guardReply()`'s honesty/repeat-detection fixes - MaiPai's own coat on the model). It never removes the safety floor (`gateOutputSafety()` - child protections, content ceilings, `docs/SAFETY.md`'s "architecture, not settings"). `backend/src/lib/bareCompletion.ts`'s `startBareCompletion()` calls `gateOutputSafety()` internally, unconditionally, and its return type is the already-gated stream - there is no exported function anywhere in this diff that hands a caller bare mode's raw, ungated tokens. Both bare-mode callers (`routes/turnBare.ts`'s existing feature (a), refactored into a thin wrapper over this function; and the new `turnBareStream.ts`'s `runBareTurnStream()` for feature (b)) go through it the same way.

**The seam** (found by a fork dispatched specifically to map `runTurnStream()`'s own shape without touching `turnEngine.ts`'s routing logic to find it): `TurnStreamResult`'s `kind: "stream"` variant is a generic contract `routes/turn.ts`'s own resume/NDJSON-streaming code already consumes without caring what produced it. `runBareTurnStream()` is a sibling function, never a branch, built entirely from pieces `turnEngine.ts` and `conversationHistory.ts` already exported or were extended to export (`validateTurnInput`, `deriveCrisisResources`, `resolveOrCreateConversation`, `buildConversationWindow`, `acquireTurnLease`, `fallbackSignal`) - `routes/turn.ts`'s `/stream` handler is the one place that decides, before calling in, whether a turn goes through `runTurnStream()` or `runBareTurnStream()`.

**Three gates on who can ever construct a bare turn**: owner/admin only, and never a minor "whoever flips the switch" - checked at the route (a clean 403), checked again inside `runBareTurnStream()` itself (a structural backstop, `BareModeForbidden`, since `TurnFailure`'s own status union has no 403 slot by design), and implicit in `resolveOrCreateConversation()`'s own ownership rule (a turn can only post into a conversation the actor owns, so the turn's speaker is always the actor - there is no cross-person bare turn). The minor check blocks both minor bands (`speakerAgeBand() !== "adult"`), not "child" read narrowly, matching the codebase's own existing minor-detection convention.

**The durable marker vs. the ephemeral switch**: `conversation_turns.bare` (migration 0060) is confirmed hub-internal (schema.ts's own comment: "not part of the synced conversation record"), so this is a clean, additive column with no spec change - unlike a real, persisted per-conversation setting would have needed (`conversations` IS spec-shaped, `additionalProperties: false`, no settings field - the same wall RESP-04's own persistence question hit, named `PERSIST-CONV-01`). The switch itself never touches this column or any storage; it's `useNextChatRuntime`'s own `bareMode` React state, reset on conversation switch, gone on reload. The memory judge excludes a bare turn twice: `judgeStatus: "skipped"` written at insert (the same "ineligible ones skipped at insert" pattern `judgeStatusAtInsert()` already uses), and `memoryJudge.ts`'s own eligibility predicate additionally excludes `eq(bare, false)` directly, so it stays correct even if some future write path forgets the first.

**Two review passes, four real defects, all fixed before landing** (one pass explicitly high-effort, focused on the safety floor - it found the floor itself unskippable everywhere it checked, and instead found the real defects in resource lifecycle and safety-adjacent bookkeeping around the new hand-built stream pipeline):
1. The lease leaked on an engine-unavailable failure. `runBareTurnStream()`'s own `if (!started.ok) return {...}` is a plain return, not a throw - the original `try { ... } catch (err) { if (!handedOff) lease.release(); throw err; }` only released on the throw path, so this exact case leaked the lease forever (`turnActivity.ts`'s own comment: leases are "never a decrement" outside an explicit release), permanently blocking `turnActiveWithin()`'s own gate on the memory judge's batch runs and the conversation summary refresh. Fixed with `finally`, matching `runTurnStream()`'s own documented reasoning for using one ("everything up to the handoff runs under one finally... so a future throw anywhere... cannot leak") - a return leaks exactly the same way a forgotten throw does, and `finally` is the one construct that runs on both.
2. `Cancel` didn't actually stop a bare-mode generation. `runBareTurnStream()` took no `AbortSignal` at all, so `routes/turn.ts`'s own `abortController.signal` (threaded through every other turn kind, the route's own COR-7 comment names why) never reached `startCompleteStream()`'s real fetch - an admin hitting Cancel on a bare reply got a "cancelled" client experience while the engine kept generating server-side. Fixed by threading `signal` through `runBareTurnStream()` -> `startBareCompletion()` -> `startCompleteStream()`'s own 4th argument.
3. `crisis_signal` was never written. `finalize()` built the `TurnValue`'s own `safety` field correctly but never passed `crisisSignal` to `logTurn()`, so the persisted row's column landed `false` regardless of what the bare reply actually said - `conversationInCrisis()` reads this column back across a conversation's last 10 turns to decide whether the household stays in the crisis-overlay state, so a silently-`false` bare turn would have broken that continuity for the ordinary turns around it. Fixed: `carriesCrisisSignal(value.safety)`, computed and passed the same way `logTurnSafely()` already does for a real turn.
4. The persistence write had no `try/catch`. Unlike `logTurnSafely()` (which wraps its own `logTurn()` call specifically so a transient DB failure never crashes an otherwise-successful turn), `finalize()`'s call was bare - a lock-contention failure would have surfaced as a mid-stream error to the admin even though the bare reply had already generated and streamed. Fixed to match `logTurnSafely()`'s own pattern exactly (a `console.error`, not a rethrow).

A fifth, frontend-only bug found the same way: `chatModelAdapter.ts` called `deps.consumeThinking()` unconditionally on every send, including a bare one - `consumeThinking()` isn't a pure read, it resets the composer's own Instant/Thinking selection, and bare mode's own completion ignores `thinking` entirely (`bareCompletion.ts` hardcodes it on). Sending a bare message with "Thinking" selected used to visibly flip the composer back to "Instant" for a value the request never looked at. Fixed by skipping the consume for a bare send, leaving the composer's own selection untouched for whatever the next (possibly non-bare) send actually is. Caught by the same re-review, testing this fix: `bare: deps.isBareMode?.() ?? false` sent a literal `bare: false` on every request from every surface, including the old `ChatPage.tsx`, which has no bare-mode concept at all - `JSON.stringify` only drops `undefined`, not `false`, and an existing exact-body-match test (`ChatPage.test.tsx`) caught it immediately. Fixed to `bare: bare || undefined`.

**Why `ChatPage.test.tsx`'s exact-body-match assertion stays exact (COORDINATOR, 2026-09-22)**: this is the second time in one day a strict `toEqual` on a full request body caught a real cross-surface leak the FIRST time it happened, not the second (RESP-04's own `thinking`/`isBareMode` work is the sibling case). A looser assertion - `toMatchObject`, or checking only the fields the test itself cares about - would have let `chatModelAdapter.ts`'s shared `run()` silently grow a new field on every surface's request, forever, with nothing failing until whatever eventually reads that field on the backend did something surprising with an unexpected `bare: false`. The strictness is doing real work specifically because `chatModelAdapter.ts` is shared: a change scoped to one surface's own new feature (`NextChatPage.tsx`'s bare mode) has no natural reason to touch `ChatPage.tsx`'s own request shape at all, and this test is the one thing that proves it didn't. Worth knowing before loosening it for convenience later.

**A test-coverage gap, also review-caught**: the "never a minor" test originally only posted through `POST /api/turn/stream`, where `routes/turn.ts`'s own route-level check fires first and returns 403 before `runBareTurnStream()` is ever called - proving the route's check works, not the function's own structural backstop, the whole point of checking it twice. Fixed by adding a test that calls `runBareTurnStream()` directly, with no route in the way.

**A real environment finding while writing the lease-leak's own regression test**: a URL-configured chat backend (`llmSupervisor.ts`'s `startChatBackend()`) returns a client REGARDLESS of its own health check - an unreachable URL doesn't fail synchronously at all, only lazily, the first time something actually iterates the token generator (a different code path, already correctly handled by the existing `holdLease()` try/finally). The genuinely synchronous "unavailable, no throw" case `!started.ok` exists for is the engine being manually stopped (`stopChatBackend()`, Household -> AI models) - used instead once this was found live, rather than the turnEngine.test.ts's own stub-server-then-stop() technique, which doesn't reach the same code path here.

**Verified**: `bash scripts/check.sh` in `home-a2` (backend suite, 3731 pass; frontend suite, 637 pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean on both; `eslint` clean on frontend, backend has none - `tsc` is its lint gate). New backend tests (`turnBareStream.test.ts`, 11 cases): the admin gate, the durable marker and judge skip, the safety floor refusing an unsafe bare reply, the structural minor-gate backstop called directly, the lease-leak fix, the abort-signal fix (mirroring `turnEngine.test.ts`'s own established "an aborted signal... releases and leaves the count exact" pattern), and the crisis-signal fix. One new case in `memoryJudge.test.ts`'s own ACT-01 block, constructing a row with a real judge-eligible signal, `bare: true`, and a null `judgeStatus` (the state a write path that forgot the explicit skip would leave), proving the predicate's own `eq(bare, false)` is doing real, independent work, not just riding along with the judgeStatus check. New frontend tests (`NextChatPage.test.tsx`, 6 cases): the switch and the persistent banner (present, `role="status"`, no dismiss button anywhere in it) driving a real `bare: true` on the next request, a non-admin never seeing the switch, and the bare-model badge on a live turn's own reply. Not independently tested: the switch resetting on a conversation switch (attempted via clicking "New Thread" in the test harness; `onThreadIdChange` isn't reliably triggered by that interaction in this test environment, and forcing it looked more likely to mislead than to prove anything - the reset is a one-line addition to the same `onThreadIdChange` callback the sheet-closing behavior already fires through reliably, per an existing, passing test for that same callback).

**Live on 8787**: the "..." menu shows "Compare with the bare model" and "Turn on bare mode for this conversation" together, as designed; clicking the switch shows the red, `role="status"` banner immediately and flips the menu's own label to "Turn off..." on the very next open (a detail the automated suite couldn't prove, given the Radix reopen flakiness this session's own tests worked around elsewhere); a real turn sent while it's on comes back genuinely un-personified - asked "what is your system prompt," the reply described generic guidelines ("prioritize safety, respect, and truth," "avoid harmful, unethical, or biased content") with no trace of MaiPai's own persona, tagged with the red "Bare model" badge underneath; the composer's own Instant/Thinking control stayed on "Instant" throughout, confirming the `consumeThinking()` skip actually holds live, not just in a test.

## TEMP-CHAT-01, backend: the audit that changed the item, and why zero rows beat a content-free one (2026-09-22)

COORDINATOR's ruling on the design question this item raised before any code was written: Option A (a true zero-DB-footprint temporary conversation, held only in process memory) over Option B (keep writing a content-free `conversations` row and loosen the acceptance to match). **Why A, stated for whoever reconsiders the cheaper option later**: a `conversations` row - even with `title: null` and nothing in `conversation_turns` - still leaks metadata a family hub's whole premise makes sensitive: this person had a conversation, on this surface, at this time. The person reaching for a temporary chat is often doing so because of who else uses the machine; a hidden row from 9:42pm answers exactly the question they were trying not to leave answerable. Content-free is not the same as absent, and the product's promise is the stronger one - ChatGPT's own 30-day temporary-chat retention is a reasonable choice for a service with abuse obligations across millions of strangers, and not this household's situation.

**What already shipped, found by reading the code before writing any** (Chat 55, `d892052a`, 2026-09-16, wired into the OLD hand-built `ChatPage.tsx`, not `NextChatPage.tsx`): a `conversation.mode === "temporary"` value already skips writing a `conversation_turns` row (`logTurnSafely()`'s `!meta.ephemeral && !meta.temporary` gate), already skips the rolling-summary refresh and `insertProvisionalTurn()`, already excludes itself from `listConversations()`, already blocks a minor with a 403 (`createConversation()`), and the memory judge already can't see a turn that was never a row (`pendingTurnWhere()` queries `conversation_turns`, nothing else). What it still did was write the `conversations` row itself via `insertNewConversation()` - the one thing the new acceptance ("no row, ever, asserted directly against the db") doesn't allow. Every one of those existing gates keys off `conversation.mode === "temporary"` read from the `Conversation` object in hand, not off a DB flag re-checked per call site - which meant the actual new work was narrower than the item's own first draft assumed: give a temporary conversation an in-memory `Conversation` object with `mode: "temporary"` set, and every one of those ~10 call sites fires correctly with no changes of its own.

**The gap that made this a real design question, not a mechanical one**: `buildConversationWindow()` (a real turn's multi-turn context) queries `conversation_turns` by `conversation.id` directly. A conversation that writes nothing there is amnesiac turn to turn - not a privacy feature, a broken chat, and the reason this needed asking rather than guessing. Closed by extending the one in-process pattern already doing this job (`routes/turn.ts`'s `resumeSessions`/`inFlightTurns`, for stream resumption) rather than inventing a second kind of store: `conversationHistory.ts`'s own `temporarySessions` map, keyed by the conversation's own id, holding the growing `ConversationTurnRow[]` a real turn's DB write would have produced (same shape, built through the identical `buildTurnRow()` - extracted out of `logTurn()` for exactly this reuse, not duplicated), capped at `WINDOW_ROW_FETCH_LIMIT` (200, the same bound a real conversation's own window query already uses - far more than the token budget could ever draw from, so it never changes which turns are visible, only stops one runaway session from growing without limit) and idle-expired at two hours (long enough a parent stepping away for coffee doesn't lose the chat, short enough a forgotten tab doesn't hold memory for a day - the same order-of-magnitude reasoning `RESUME_TTL_MS`'s 60 seconds uses for a much shorter question). Gone on a server restart, by construction, since nothing here is durable storage.

**One implementation, not two**: `createConversation()`'s own `mode === "temporary"` branch (the OLD chat's entry point, `POST /api/conversations`) now calls the same `createTemporaryConversation()` the new turn-level `temporary: true` flag uses, instead of `insertNewConversation()`. `ChatPage.tsx`'s existing toggle needed no frontend change at all: it already just POSTs to that same endpoint and later re-posts whatever conversation id comes back, and `resolveOrCreateConversation()` recognizes a given id against the in-memory session map before ever trying the database, regardless of whether the caller also passes `temporary: true` on the follow-up turns. Checked with home-37 before touching anything under `frontend/` (none was needed) so as not to collide with their upcoming `ROUTE-FIND-03`.

**Safety, unchanged by construction, not by care taken**: nothing above touches `prepareTurn()`'s own routing or `gateOutputSafety()`'s output pass - a temporary conversation runs the identical persona/routing/packages/quality-guard/safety pipeline a real one does, on an in-memory `Conversation` object instead of a DB-backed one, the same way `ephemeral` already does for a widget query. The one age/role gate (owner/admin/adult only, matching Chat 55's own existing rule) is checked twice: the route's clean 403 (`routes/turn.ts`, mirroring `ADMIN-COMPARE-01 (b)`'s own bare-mode pattern) and `resolveOrCreateConversation()`'s own structural backstop, proven with no route-level check involved at all (`temporaryChat.test.ts`).

**A durable-write audit, run before any of this was built, per the coordinator's explicit condition** ("do not build before this is reported"): every table with a `conversation_id`/`turn_id` column was read, not assumed. Two real, pre-existing gaps found:
1. `setReplyConstraint()` (`prepareTurn()`, CONS-01) had no `ephemeral`/`temporary` gate at all, unlike every other durable write in that function - a pre-existing leak (also true for `ephemeral` widget queries today, not introduced by this change) into `reply_constraints`, a table with no DB-level foreign key, so it never crashed, it just silently outlived the conversation it belonged to. Gated with the same `!ephemeral && conversation.mode !== "temporary"` condition `insertProvisionalTurn()` already uses; `fired()`'s own operational trace line stays unconditional, matching every other trace point in this file.
2. `host.artifact.create()` (`packageHost.ts`, ARTIFACT-02) needs a real `conversation_turns` row to satisfy `artifacts`' own foreign key - `insertProvisionalTurn()` is deliberately never called for an ephemeral or temporary turn, so that row never exists, and the existing missing-turn guard (`!turn?.id || !turn.conversationId`) never catches this case because both fields ARE populated for a temporary turn. Before this fix: an uncaught FK violation, not a clean refusal - dormant today (`ephemeral` is a narrow widget-query flag almost nothing hits), but this item turns temporary conversations into a feature people actually use, which promotes a dormant crash into a routine one. Fixed with the identical `HostError` shape the missing-turn case already throws (`permission_denied`, "Documents aren't available in a temporary chat because nothing is saved."), so it travels the same normal declined-tool-outcome path a real turn's pipeline already handles, never an unhandled exception mid-stream.

**Two findings that on inspection needed no fix, corrected against my own first audit rather than built around**: `replyFeedback` (thumbs up/down) and `attachments` (file upload) both have real FK columns too, and my first pass flagged both as reachable crash risks the same way `artifacts` was. Wrong: both already have a genuine existence check in front of the write (`routes/conversations.ts`'s `visibleTurn()` 404s before the feedback insert; `attachments.ts`'s `createAttachment()` requires a matching `conversationTurns`+`conversations` join before touching the filesystem or the DB), so neither can reach the FK at all for a synthetic temporary id - both correctly 404 instead. Caught only once I went to implement the fix I'd already told the coordinator I would make; reported as a correction rather than shipped as unnecessary code. A third finding from an independent review, `queueOpenQuestion` (`resolvePendingAsk()`'s "who"/"relay" continuation), turned out the same way: unreachable, because `getPendingAsk()`/`setPendingAsk()` already close the path for a temporary conversation (the pre-existing `mode === "temporary"` check for a real row; a synthetic id's DB query simply matches nothing either way) - proven by a direct test rather than assumed, since "I read the code and it looks safe" is not the same bar the other two findings that WERE real got held to.

**Verified**: `bash scripts/check.sh` - backend suite green (`tsc --noEmit` clean), two unrelated tests flaky under the full 185-file run (`turnEngine.test.ts`'s wildcard-capture routing test, `tier2.test.ts`'s invention pre-check), each passing 3/3 in isolation, reported as an environment finding per the org's own gate-flake policy, not fixed forward. New tests: `backend/tests/temporaryChat.test.ts` (13 cases) - the role gate at the route and as a structural backstop with no route involved, no row in `conversations`/`conversation_turns` after a real streamed turn, the thread list excluding it, the memory judge never invoked (a real `spyOn` of `complete()` from `@/lib/llm`, set up AFTER the turn's own reply already streamed so the spy can only ever see a judge call, plus `runJudgeBatch()` processing zero), the safety floor still refusing an unsafe reply, a second turn in the same temporary conversation actually carrying the first turn's content into the model's own window (the amnesia gap, proven fixed, not just described), the reply-constraints leak fixed, and the open-questions path proven unreachable. `backend/tests/packageHostArtifact.test.ts` (+2 cases): the artifact-creation refusal is the clean `HostError` shape, not a crash - and neither is its sibling. Code review: medium, one pass, one real finding: `host.artifact.update()` didn't get the same `isTemporaryConversation` guard `create()` did, so the identical FK-crash gap survived on the sibling method (an artifact made earlier in a real conversation, edited from a temporary one). Fixed with the same `HostError` shape and message as `create()`'s own fix, and a test mirroring `create()`'s own (start real, create there, switch to a temporary turn, attempt `update()`, expect the clean refusal). Re-review of the fix hunk (9 lines, an exact structural mirror of the already-reviewed `create()` guard): self-verified rather than a second full subagent pass, per the org's own budget guidance - the fix changes nothing about the pattern a first pass already approved, only where else it's applied.

## LAT-03: f16 KV cache against q8_0 on the hub's chat engine (2026-09-22)

**The question.** The hub's chat engine runs `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` with flash attention on Metal, and its effective prefill rate on 2026-09-22 was 183 tok/s (llama-server `/metrics`: 2,892 prompt tokens in 15.79 s) against 279 to 369 tok/s on two direct probes of the same engine earlier that day. Is the quantized KV cache the drag?

**Method.** A side instance of the hub's own binary and model, one slot, `-c 8192`, otherwise the hub's flags (`-fa on -ngl all --reasoning off -ub 1024 --jinja --cache-reuse 256`), started twice on a spare port, once per KV type; the hub's own engine on 8788 was never touched. Eight chat completions per run: four at about 285 prompt tokens and four at about 911, each a distinct prompt so nothing beyond the 16-token shared system line was cached (`cache_n` 16), `max_tokens` 4, temperature 0. The first request of each size is the warm-up and is not counted. No run started while a `check.sh` gate was on the machine, and a repeat that overlapped a gate starting mid-run was discarded (one q8_0 repeat at 911 tokens; its number matched the other three). Engine build b10797, model file `qwen3-8b-instruct-q4-k-m.gguf`, Apple M4 Pro, 20-core GPU, 24 GB. Decode was not measured (four tokens per request); this item is about prefill.

| KV cache | about 285 prompt tokens, prompt tok/s (3 repeats) | about 911 prompt tokens, prompt tok/s (3 repeats) |
|---|---|---|
| q8_0 (today's flags) | 411, 408, 411 | 405, 404, 406 |
| f16 | 390, 394, 396 | 387, 385, 385 |

**Verdict.** f16 is not faster. q8_0 is 4 to 5 percent faster on both sizes and holds the KV cache in half the memory, so the flags stay and `llmSupervisor` is untouched. LAT-03 closes with no change.

**What the run does say.** A fresh one-slot instance prefills at about 405 tok/s where the live hub engine measured 279 cold and 183 effective on the same box the same day. The KV type is not that difference. What is left: the live engine's four slots at `-c 32768`, and, more likely, contention on the machine while the hub's turns ran (the CPU-only 4B judge on 8789 with four threads, other sessions' gates and builds; the 17:55 "hi" also decoded at 27 tok/s against the usual 33 to 40). The fixes that matter for "hi" are the two the latency diagnosis named and PERF-ALERT-01's record carries: the think-exhausted first generation that the opening hold regenerates, and the offered tools block breaking the prefix cache at 567 tokens. An engine-side check, only if the hub's rate stays low after those two land, is a one-slot A/B of `--parallel 4 -c 32768` against `--parallel 1 -c 8192` with this same probe.

## U0a: the owner's replay set, the OLD-path baseline (2026-09-22)

`backend/scripts/bench/datasets/owner-replay.json` (the plan's point 4,
verbatim: six failed conversations the owner actually had today plus
thirteen controls, including the tool-call corpus's five negatives) and
`backend/scripts/bench/replay.ts`, mirroring `conversation.ts`'s own
runner shape (a pure fixture loader, a dual offline/`--live` entry
point, the same import-order rule) but driving
`conversationRunner.ts`/`conversationScore.ts` - one definition, not a
second harness - three repeats per row, reported as two blocks (failed
rows must pass, control rows must not regress) instead of one table.

**The live run did not happen today.** `pgrep -fl llama-server` showed
a side instance already up on port 8798 (another session's own
benchmark) beside the household's own engines on 8788 (chat) and 8794
(embed); the org rule is explicit that another session's live bench
takes priority and 8788's slots are never a bench's. Per the
coordinator's own fallback, this ran scripted instead: an in-process
stub (`@maipai/spec`'s `stubServer.ts`, the same double
`tests/conversationBench.test.ts`'s `withStubBench` already uses)
answers both the chat and embed endpoints, so the run needs no engine
at all. The stub never calls a tool on its own - it only echoes - so
this measures the pipeline's own DETERMINISTIC decisions (the pre-model
lookup ladder, routing, guards) for real, never a live model's own tool
choice. That is the real limit of a scripted run; it is not a
substitute for `--live`, only what is honest to report when no engine
can be spared. The harness itself is proven correct offline too
(`backend/tests/ownerReplay.test.ts`, 5 cases: the fixture loads and
validates, no row names a household member, the JSON-to-runner plumbing
runs both a control and a multi-turn failed row end to end, and the
repeat-summary arithmetic is unit-tested directly).

**Scripted baseline, 2026-09-22, 75 turns executed (25 rows x 3
repeats):**

- **Failed rows (must pass once U2 lands): 0 of 6 clean on every
  repeat.** Exactly the expected shape - these are today's known bugs.
  `president-of-france-repeat`: the stuck line still fires on the
  second "who is the president of France" (`guard.repeat_reply` in the
  turn log). `apple-announce-this-week`, `president-of-chile-when-born`:
  no lookup at all under the stub (no tool call, the model's own
  discretion, which this mode cannot exercise - genuinely untested
  today, not passing or failing on the merits). `search-mariners-game`:
  the literal "search" command DOES run websearch (2 of 3 repeats
  clean), one repeat came back with no sources - see the flake note
  below. `primetime-trailer-correction`: the "Here's a video, the
  link's below" line still fires on the correction turn, exactly the
  D5 bug. `chatgpt-6-luna`: 2 of 3 clean, one repeat's sourced-search
  turn again hit the flake below.
- **Control rows (must not regress): 11 of 13 clean on every repeat.**
  Two known scripted-mode limitations, not regressions: `control-
  twelve-plus-thirty` needs live arithmetic reasoning the stub's echo
  can never produce; `control-search-mariners-explicit` hit the same
  intermittent "no sources on the delivered turn" flake as two failed
  rows above (1 of 3 repeats clean) - the literal-pattern websearch
  call itself ran every time, but the fake SearXNG's canned rows did
  not always reach the reply under repeated back-to-back turns in one
  process; not chased further today (a scripted-environment artifact,
  named rather than root-caused, per the fallback's own scope). One
  real fixture bug found and fixed by this same run:
  `control-remember-pizza-night` was authored with `toolRan: null`;
  the remember package genuinely runs on "remember that X" (correct
  behavior), so the row's own expectation was wrong, not the pipeline -
  fixed to `toolRan: "remember"`, now clean 3/3.

**Next:** the genuine live OLD-path baseline (every row's real
tool-calling behavior, not just the deterministic half) is `bun run
backend/scripts/bench/replay.ts --live` against a spare-port side
engine, once one is free; U6's own acceptance needs it regardless. The
scripted numbers above stand as today's record, not a final baseline.

## ARCH-BUILD-01: the buy-or-build verdict (2026-09-22)

The spike's data is Session A's, in `data-scratch/arch-build-01-measurements.md` (numbers only, never judged there) and `data-scratch/skeleton-results.md`; this section is the verdict. Method as the row asked: each candidate ran the same representative turn (safety, model, websearch, model, output guard) on its own primitives in a throwaway worktree, never merged; the model and tool steps used the real `complete()` and `runPlugin("websearch")`. Two things the data cannot say, and this verdict does not use: speed between frameworks (47 of 48 timed rows ran beside a `check.sh` gate on the same machine, and the one clean row is a single sample), and correctness between frameworks (one sample of the same model and prompt per row; the Chile row went wrong under one framework and right under two, which is sampling, not orchestration). What the data does say is install size, cold start, what each candidate replaces or merely wraps, its exit cost, and how each fits the accepted design's two hard shapes: the typed action plan for side effects, and the per-node trace with deadlines (the plan's section 11).

| Candidate | What it would replace | Install, cold start | Lines replaced / wrapped | Exit cost | Fit to the accepted design | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LangGraph JS (embedded, never its server) | The loop and its state, retries, interrupts, checkpoints | +19 MB, 48 packages (a LangSmith client stub among them); 0.71 s median cold start | ~150 to 250 lines of hand-rolled control flow; wraps all of `resolveToolCallsInOrder` and everything upstream | Low to moderate; the checkpointer is the real lock-in | Its tool primitives call the tool directly, so the design's "side effects only through a typed action plan and a deterministic executor" would be hand-built beside it; a phone-home surface arrives with the dependency and the spike could only snapshot connections with `lsof`, never enforce a block | **Reject** for orchestration. It fails the row's own bar: it does not delete a large amount of our orchestration, and the one node that matters most it cannot own |
| XState v5 | The sequencing layer only: states, transitions, guards, actors with abort, inspection | +3 MB, 10 packages, no telemetry; cold start within noise of the baseline (676 vs 654 ms) | Formalizes `composer.ts`'s hand-rolled `TurnMachine` (a wash on lines today); wraps, never replaces, the policy in `resolveToolCallsInOrder`, `guards.ts`, `lookupDecision` | Low: one glue file, a day or two to leave | The machine definition is ours (TurnState, Node, Transition, ToolRequest, ActionProposal, PolicyDecision); XState runs it, and its inspection events are the per-node trace section 11 requires, its actors carry the per-node deadline and abort signal, and a node implementation is swapped by registering another actor under the same event, which is section 11's swap rule; typechecked clean on the first attempt against the repo's real types; runs on Bun on the Pi at 3 MB | **Adopt**, as the sequencing runtime of U2, scoped to the machine and its actors; nothing of our semantics lives in XState's primitives |
| In-house TurnGraph | The same sequencing layer, written by us | 0 bytes; 0.65 s median cold start | 51 lines of runtime today; replaces almost nothing of `turnEngine.ts` (A's honest finding: `prepareTurn` and the tool resolver are domain code, untouched by any orchestration choice) | Near zero today | Every part the real turn needs and the demo lacks (retries with backoff, an interrupt, a checkpoint a paused turn resumes from, the trace, deadlines) is new code we would write and maintain, and it is the identical job XState ships | **Reject**. Principle 6: a maintained library for a solved problem beats hand-rolled logic doing the identical job, and 51 lines is the demo's cost, not the turn's |
| Cedar (WASM, evaluator only) | `meetsMinRole()` and the consequential-package check: 4 lines at 4 call sites | +13 MB; 23 ms cold, 0.18 ms per evaluation | ~10 to 15 lines; nothing else in household authorization (exclusions parsed from speech, live consent, content ceilings) is Cedar's to evaluate | Low: one translation function, policies are data | The spec declares, Cedar evaluates, which is the acceptable shape; but today there is no declared household policy record for it to evaluate, only a 4-line role ladder | **Adopt partially, deferred**: Cedar becomes the evaluator of ARCH-POLICY-01's household policy record (permissions and role floors) when that record exists; not before, because 13 MB for 4 lines fails the bar today |
| Home Assistant | Device execution | Already the runtime (`home.call_service` recipes) | n/a | n/a | Unchanged | **Adopted** (already the case) |
| Letta's memory-block and archival concepts | The shape of ARCH-MEM-01's record | Not run; read | n/a | n/a | Concepts only, never its runtime | **Read into ARCH-MEM-01's record**, no dependency |

**Why XState and not our own.** The accepted design added two requirements after the row was written: a per-node trace on every turn (node, implementation and version, start and end, outcome, the model's generations under the model node) and a per-node deadline with an abort that reaches the engine, so that a layer can be watched and swapped. A statechart library ships both as its ordinary features (inspection events, actor cancellation), and A's spike showed the machine typechecks against the repo's own types without a fight. The in-house shape would grow those features by hand, and LangGraph would ship them at the price of owning the tool-call semantics the design keeps deterministic. The exit is cheap either way; the maintenance is not, and that is the difference.

**What the skeleton and the framework runs taught about the interim rule.** Across A's runs the rule ("a question about the world is searched") fired once in 20 model turns, on the second ask of the France question, where the model had already answered correctly from the conversation; the forced search cost about 2.6 s and changed nothing. The Chile failure (a question the model answers from memory instead of searching) did not reproduce on any of the three re-runs, so it is probabilistic, and B's measurement is the number that matters: the 8B calls a fitting search 19 times in 50 (38 percent) with 0 false calls in 50. So the rule stays on for the 8B, and U2's state record answers one question before the rule ships: its form gains "unless this conversation already holds the answer", and the model decides that inside the same structured call rather than in prose. The proposed shape: the forced call offers two choices, the search tool and an `answer_from_this_conversation` tool whose one argument is the quoted line of the window it answers from; the engine verifies the quote is in the window (a set check, not a judgment) and otherwise runs the search. Tonight's quiet-window run, ten repeats with the rule on and off, gives the cost and the miss rate that settle it.

**RSS and robot fit (A's last two rows, 2026-09-22).** Stubbed-turn resident memory, idle and peak: LangGraph 367 and 387 MB, XState 359 and 378 MB, the in-house TurnGraph 316 and 336 MB; a spread of about 51 MB, inside the Pi's budget, so it changes nothing. Robot fit: the robot's household runtime is the hub's own package setup (bot RUNTIME-01), so the spike worktrees are that install; XState installs and boots on arm64. Two gaps recorded, neither changing the verdict: no Bun version is pinned anywhere in the org (every run was on 1.3.14; filed by the coordinator), and nothing ran on an actual Pi because no documented access to one exists, so the robot row is proven on arm64 and the Pi's memory budget on paper until the robot bench exists.

**Caveats on the record.** The network-block measurement was `lsof` snapshots, not an enforced block, because the shared machine's networking could not be cut under other sessions; the adopted candidate has no network code path, and the rejected one is not adopted, so no decision rests on it. The Cedar table row is A's final fold; if its numbers move, the deferral does not.

Engine for the framework runs: the hub's own chat engine on 8788 (b10797, qwen3-8b-instruct-q4-k-m); the spikes' side runs on a spare port with the same build; Apple M4 Pro, 20-core GPU, 24 GB.

Owner's spec (relayed via the coordinator): the "+" button opens a
grouped menu - Add (photos and files, a phone's camera, Create image,
Web search) and Apps (the installed packages, choosing one scopes the
turn) - plus two voice controls at the composer's right (a dictation
mic, a waveform+chevron for a live voice conversation).

hardcoded a bare `<ComposerAddAttachment />` immediately left of the
`ComposerExtra` slot - putting a grouped menu there too would have put

assistant-ui's own Elements catalog (`packages/ui/src/components/
react/assistant-ui/elements/`, via `gh api`) found no shipped
add-menu Element to adopt instead. So: commons gained a sixth
`ThreadComponents` append point, `ComposerAddAttachmentOverride?:
ComponentType`, the same shape `ComposerExtra`/`Indicator`/
`AssistantActionBarExtra`/`AssistantMessageFooterExtra` already
established (commons commit d438eac, tag `ui-v0.5.34`, pins bumped in
`scripts/check.sh` and `frontend/package.json`) - when set, it replaces

`ui/docs/dashboard-upstream.md`'s pending-patches table and
`ui/CHANGELOG.md`; handed to home-37 (already mid-PR on
assistant-ui/assistant-ui#8003, "Thread: five append points for
product-specific controls") to add as the PR's sixth.

**The menu (`frontend/src/apps/chat/composerAddMenu.tsx`, new):**
composed entirely from shipped pieces - `elements/composer.tsx`'s
`ComposerAttachButton`/`ComposerMenu`/`ComposerMenuItem` (the exact

- **Apps**: `GET /api/plugins`, filtered to `status: "enabled"`.

**Behind a new module-level flag (default off), built and unit-tested

**PDF and office documents** stay out of the Add menu entirely, not

**A real regression caught before landing:** every pre-existing
