## Track 3: the local decider verdict (2026-09-22)

The question phase 0's track 3 asked: can a small local typed-decision model replace the word rules and the interim rule as the decider for "does this turn need a web lookup", on this hub and on the robot's Pi. Session's data: `data-scratch/jev-bakeoff/results.md` (the rerun section), 17 rows (the ROUTE-FIND-03 and REPLY-FIND-02 rows with their null pins, the three Chile turns with prior turns as context, the Luna and "search the web" turns), CPU and Metal on the M4 Pro, 24 GB.

| Candidate | Size, licence | Positives right | False positives on the five ambiguous negatives | Latency (CPU p50) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| open-jev-deberta-v3-large, zero-shot from the schema text | 400M, Apache-2.0 | 12 of 12, all three Chile turns included | 5 of 5, websearch at 0.51 to 0.62 against a flat spread | 65 ms (Metal no faster at batch one) | **The path, after fine-tuning; not in shadow mode as it stands** |
| jeff (GLiFormer, 576M) | MIT | 5 of 12, no prediction at all on 8 of 17 rows | 1 of 5 | 117 ms | **Dropped** as the decider; a GLiNER-lineage span extractor does not reason over schema text, and its README's single-word label shape was not tried |
| openjev (DiffusionGemma 26B) | Apache-2.0 | not run | not run | 18 GB of weights | **Dropped** on hardware: an NVIDIA 24 GB GPU or 16 GB free on Apple silicon, and never a Pi |

**Why not shadow mode yet.** RULES-AND-LEARNED-COMPONENTS.md lets a learned check run beside the deterministic path in shadow mode and adopts it when its measured false-positive rate beats the rule's. Zero-shot, DeBERTa makes exactly the interim rule's decision (a question about the world is searched) with the rule's exact failure (every ambiguous negative admitted), and costs 65 ms and a resident process to do it. A shadow run of a decider that reproduces the rule logs no comparison signal, only cost, and 17 rows cannot measure a false-positive rate anyway. Its published numbers say where the gain is: 0.854 accuracy and ECE 0.022 in its training domains against 0.690 out of domain, so the household's own labels are the lever, not a bigger sample of the zero-shot behaviour.

**What LOOKUP-HEAD-01 needs first, in order.** (1) A labelled set: the label is "needs a lookup, and which tool", not "which package"; the sources are U0a's replay set (the owner's real turns, the only labelled history that exists), the routing corpus's question and null rows relabelled for lookup need (with the caveat that the corpus is the ladder's own calibration set), and the owner's own labelled turns; never a frontier model over household transcripts, which is egress (owner's ruling, 2026-09-22; a frontier model may label roster-based synthetic data only); the negatives must include the ambiguous class (an organization name that is also a word, a news verb with no time window), because that is the class both the rule and the zero-shot head admit. `corrected_next_turn` is NULL on all 278 rows today, so the harvest (`scripts/bench/labels.ts`, RVW-1b) has to start writing it before the hub's own history can label anything. (2) The shadow seat, which U2 now provides: the head runs inside the model node before the call, its choice and probability are written to `stats.nodes[]` under the model node beside the interim rule's decision and the model's actual tool call, and the decision is unchanged; the weekly report compares the three. (3) The fine-tune: DeBERTa on the labelled set (a few hundred rows is enough for an NLI-style encoder; SetFit-style), calibrated by temperature scaling on a held-out slice, thresholds chosen on precision, shipped as a fetched artifact under the model-capabilities spec, run on CPU (65 ms is inside the budget; Metal buys nothing at batch one). (4) The bench: the tuned head against the interim rule and against the 8B's own tool call (measured today: 19 fitting searches called in 50, 0 false calls in 50) on held-out rows and the replay set; adopted per model budget when its false-positive rate on the ambiguous negatives beats the rule's and it loses no positives, with the 2026-09-16 review's margin (five macro-F1 points) on the corpus's question rows. The robot: 400M at f32 is about 1.6 GB and int8 about a quarter of that, so it fits the Pi on paper; measured when a Pi is reachable, and until then the robot's budget keeps `model_transitions` off and the head is a hub decision.

**Astra's amendments (outside review, 2026-09-22).** DeBERTa is a pilot, not the winner; the ModernBERT-class head is unmeasured and runs in the same bench; shadow mode is permitted earlier than step 2 implies, with bounded overhead and disagreement logging, once a labelled set exists; the labelled set is 500 to 1,000 locally labelled examples split by conversation, never by row; the metrics at the operating threshold are precision, missed lookups, Brier score and reliability; GLiFormer's result is inconclusive (a label-format mismatch), not a verdict on the architecture. Frontier-model labelling of household transcripts is egress and is ruled out (owner, 2026-09-22); a frontier model may label roster-based synthetic data only.

**Is DeBERTa tuned on labelled rows the path?** Yes, provisionally: it is the one candidate that reasons over the schema text, it is Apache-2.0 and offline, it runs in 65 ms on CPU, and its calibration is documented in domain. The ModernBERT-class head ROUTER-RLCD-01 names is the same class of model and the same recipe; the bench in step 4 picks between them, and nothing in this verdict pre-empts that. What the verdict rules out is a bigger zero-shot sample or a second prompt-engineering pass on labels: the gain is in the household's labels, not in the schema wording.

Two gaps in the track's own report, recorded here: the 8B baseline was not obtained by that session (it is above, from ARCH-MEASURE-01), and the interim-rule on/off measurement it was asked for was blocked because the skeleton spike's worktree was removed; that measurement now belongs to U2d on the real machine, where it was already scheduled.

## LINT-UI-01: `@shadcn/lint` on Home's new UI (2026-09-22)

`@shadcn/lint` (`frontend/eslint.config.js`, scoped to `src/next/**/*.{ts,tsx}` only - the old shell retires with SHELL-09 and the vendored kit trees are never linted) makes the org's no-hand-built-UI rule mechanical: its six rules (`no-restyle`, `no-raw-colors`, `no-arbitrary-values`, `no-inline-styles`, `no-unknown-classes`, `require-static-classes`) catch a restyled component, a raw Tailwind color, an off-token pixel value, an inline `style` prop, an unrecognized class, and a runtime-computed className string - the same defects a design-system review would otherwise have to catch by eye. Three findings survived a real fix and stayed inline-disabled: `Sheet`'s caller side needs `max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]`/`max-h-[85vh]` because the vendored `SheetContent` (`ui/src/ui/sheet.tsx`) has no size or max-dimension prop of its own to reach for instead - a real upstream gap, recorded as a draft note in `commons/ui/docs/dashboard-upstream.md` (not filed, per Jesse's standing call). Everything else the linter found in `src/next` was fixed with the component's own variant, size, or a real scale token - never by disabling a rule.

## ADMIN-PERF-01: the admin performance dashboard, design note (2026-09-22)

Objective per `docs/BACKLOG.md:5709`. A survey of what already exists came first (every field below is a real file/line, not an assumption) since the item's own rule is "no new collection, only aggregation of what exists."

**DASH-CARDS-01 dependency.** No card registry exists yet (`frontend/src/next/pages/dashboard/cards.ts` is not a file today). Per the coordinator's ruling, this ships as a plain page now, `/next/performance`, composed the same way `NextDashboardPage.tsx` is (one page, several panel components, one query hook) rather than as registry cards. Each panel below is still built as its own component under a new `frontend/src/next/pages/performance/` folder (not `dashboard/`, to keep it separate from the home dashboard's own cards) specifically so registering each one as a card is a follow-up wiring change, not a rewrite, once DASH-CARDS-01 lands.

**Backend: `GET /api/performance`** (`backend/src/routes/performance.ts`, mounted at `/api/performance` in `app.ts`, admin-only via `requireRole("owner","admin")` - the exact pattern `engines.ts` and `repairs.ts` already use, zod-openapi `createRoute`). Query param `days` (default 30, max 90, matching the retention window below). Response, one object per panel:

| Panel | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `turns.by_day`, `turns.by_engine` | `conversation_turns.stats` (nullable JSON text, `backend/src/wire.ts`'s `TurnStats`/`TurnGeneration`) | Median/p95 of `time_to_first_token_ms`, `total_time_ms`, tokens/sec, computed in JS after parsing each row's JSON - SQLite has no percentile function, and there's no existing aggregation helper for this column (the closest precedent, `dashboard.ts`'s `turnsPerDay()`, is a plain gap-filled COUNT by day; same day-bucketing shape, different math). No column carries a parsed-out model id, so `by_engine` groups by the turn's stored `stats.engine` string (host/build/model joined) instead - the closest real thing to "per model" that exists. |
| `turns.by_route` | `conversation_turns.source` | A turn's own `source` column (model/plugin/command/safety_refuse/...) IS the route it took - no field invented, no `nodes[]` parsing needed. |
| `layers` (the coordinator's 2026-09-22 addition) | `conversation_turns.stats.nodes[]` (U2's per-node trace, only on rows made with `turn.pipeline.next` on) | Median/p95 duration per node (`endMs - startMs`) across every traced turn in the window, plus the count of turns that carried a trace at all. `turns_with_trace: 0` and an empty `nodes` list on any hub where the new pipeline hasn't produced a row yet - the frontend's `LayersCard` renders that as an honest empty state, not a table with nothing in it. |
| `engines` | `GET /api/engines`'s existing overview/budget/health, passthrough | No restart-history table exists anywhere; "health history" for this panel is Repairs' own `issues` table filtered to engine-sourced entries (`createdAt`/`resolvedAt`), not a new store. |
| `queues` | `judgeQueueStats()` (`memoryJudge.ts`), `pendingEmbeddings`/`pendingMemoryWork` tables (`schema.ts`) | Point-in-time counts only, same as today - no new "per day" history table. |
| `labels` | `conversation_turns.rung`/`.rules`/`.correctedNextTurn` (`schema.ts:434-443`) | `backend/scripts/bench/labels.ts` already exports its pure report-builder functions (only `main()` touches the DB) - the route calls those directly against turns read from the DB for the current window, rather than reading `data/labels/*.jsonl` off disk, so the panel has real numbers even if the weekly script hasn't been run recently. |
| `hardware`, `disk` | `GET /api/engines/hardware` (Stack passthrough), `storageSummary()` (`lib/storage.ts`) | Both already exist as-is; this panel is a read, not new plumbing. |
| `stack` | `isStackConfigured()` + `GET /api/engines/` roster | **Scoped down from the backlog's "job feed" language.** The Stack has no bulk job-list endpoint - only per-id lookup (`stack/client.ts`'s `job(id)`) and an SSE bridge (`stack/events.ts`) that nothing subscribes to yet. Building a live job feed here would mean wiring that bridge into a route for the first time, which is its own item. This panel instead mirrors `NextEnginesPage.tsx`'s existing "not configured" empty state and shows the engine roster when a Stack is configured; the job feed itself is a named gap, not a stub. |
| retention | stated constant, `90` | Not new code: `conversation.retention` (`conversationHistory.ts`'s `runRetention()`) already hard-deletes whole turns - stats included - past `household.conversation_retention_days` (default 90) once a day. The acceptance criterion's "stated retention" is documenting that existing default, not building a second purge path for the `stats` column alone. |

**Frontend.** `frontend/src/next/pages/NextPerformancePage.tsx`, one `useQuery(["performance"], () => api.performance())` feeding every panel, wrapped in `AsyncState` (loading/error/empty), the same shape `NextDashboardPage.tsx` and `NextEnginesPage.tsx` already use. Composition only from what's vendored: `Card`/`CardHeader`/`CardContent` (never `DashboardCard`, per the DASH-LOOK-01 ruling every sibling file already follows), the `ChartContainer`/`recharts` pairing `TurnsPerDayChart.tsx` already demonstrates for the by-day chart, and `DataTable` (`NextEnginesPage.tsx`'s import) for the by-engine, routes, layers, labels and engine-issues tables. No hand-built chart or table.

**Built, 2026-09-22.** Eight panel components under `frontend/src/next/pages/performance/`: `TurnsChart` (median first-token/total-time lines), `TurnsByEngineTable`, `RoutesCard`, `LayersCard` (the coordinator's addition), `QueuesCard`, `LabelsCard` (guard/rule/rung hits in one table, retire-eligible rules listed underneath), `EnginesHealthCard` (recent engine-sourced Repairs issues, links to `/next/engines` for the live roster rather than duplicating it), `DiskHardwareCard`. Backend logic lives in `backend/src/lib/performance.ts`, thin route in `backend/src/routes/performance.ts`; the label-harvest panel is the one reverse import in this codebase (`backend/src/lib/performance.ts` importing `backend/scripts/bench/labels.ts`'s exported pure functions) - reusing the one report builder rather than a second copy of the guard/rule-hit counting logic. `conversationHistory.ts`'s `DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS` was exported (one word) so `retention_days` states the real constant instead of a second literal `90`. `GET /api/storage` has no `/next` page of its own yet, so the disk panel names no link rather than pointing at one that doesn't show it. Typecheck, eslint and both test files (`backend/tests/performance.test.ts`, 5 tests; `frontend/src/next/pages/NextPerformancePage.test.tsx`, 4 tests) pass; full gate green, captures at 1440/390 light/dark taken and opened (`captureNextPerformanceReview()` in `scripts/screenshot.ts`, `--next-performance-review`).

## ARCH-MEASURE-01: the per-model budget verdict (2026-09-22)

Written at 22:45 from exactly what was measured; the results file's quiet-window header read "STATUS: FINAL" at that moment; the amendment at 22:55 carries the final numbers. Sources: `data-scratch/arch-measure/results.md` (the tool-calling bench at ten repeats per row on the fixed pipeline, the inverse-miss rows included; the query-rewrite bench; the routing corpus), `data-scratch/skeleton-results.md` (the bare skeleton on the live 8B), the track-3 verdict above, and U2d's live replay run relayed by the coordinator. Engine build b10797, models `qwen3-8b-instruct-q4-k-m.gguf`, `qwen3-4b-q4-k-m.gguf`, `qwen3-1.7b-q8-0.gguf`, side instances on a spare port with the hub's flags and one slot, Apple M4 Pro, 20-core GPU, 24 GB. The 27B is dropped (a coding fine-tune at 3.4 bits on another build, and its routed rows never replied). Latency was not measured tonight for any model; the 8B's numbers stand from LAT-00 to LAT-03 (183 tok/s effective prefill live, 405 on a fresh one-slot instance, 36 tok/s decode) and the skeleton (2.5 s median, 3.9 s p90 to first visible token).

**Measured.**

| Model | False calls, bare prompt (50 negatives) | False calls, production prompt, outside always-offer (50) | Fitting searches called (50, the inverse miss) | Query rewrite (15 rows, 10 repeats) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8B | 0 (0%) | 0 (0%) | 19 (38%) | not usable: 4 of 15 rows attempted under a running gate, one row lost to contention entirely |
| 4B | 0 (0%) at 10 repeats, 0 of 25 at 5 | 5 (10%) at 10 repeats, 1 of 25 (4%) at 5 | 19 (38%) at 10 repeats and 7 of 25 (28%) in a fresh 5-repeat run; confirmed against its own log, the match with the 8B's figure is coincidence | 1 of 8 rows at the bar (5 repeats); rows 9 to 15 not attempted |
| 1.7B | 0 (0%) | 0 (0%) | 0 (0%), two independent runs agree | 2 of 15 rows at the bar (13%) at 5 repeats, all 15 rows clean |

**Derivation rules, fixed before the numbers, plus one field the numbers forced.** The query-rewrite results (1.7B 2 of 15 rows at the bar, 4B 1 of 8, the 8B pending) mean "the model writes the query" cannot be the only path below the 8B, so the budget record gains `query_writer: "model" | "builder"`: with `builder`, the engine's own query builder (the fallback the state record already keeps) writes every search, and with `model` the model's argument is the query and the builder takes over only when that argument fails the term-level grounding check. The 1.7B and the 4B are on the builder until measured otherwise; the 8B is on the model pending its quiet run. `always_search` is on when a model calls a fitting search in fewer than 95 percent of repeats (an inverse miss over one in twenty). `model_transitions` is on when the model's false-call rate on the production prompt is at or under 2 percent (Fix E's bar) and its query rewrite passes 90 percent of rows at 9 of 10; an unmeasured rewrite takes the conservative value and the cell is marked. `rounds` is 1 when `model_transitions` is on, else 0; 2 only when a replay or corpus row needs it, and none does. `thinking_for_minors` is false everywhere (the reasoning ruling). `context_tokens` is the prompt budget the engine assembles today (about 4,000 characters of system prompt plus the window); deadlines are the state record's starting values.

**The budget records, starting values.**

| Field | 8B (`qwen3-8b-instruct-q4-k-m`) | 4B (`qwen3-4b-q4-k-m`) | 1.7B (`qwen3-1.7b-q8-0`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `always_search` | on (19 of 50) | on (19 of 50 and 7 of 25, confirmed) | on (0 of 50) |
| `model_transitions` | on, provisional: false calls 0 percent, rewrite pending a quiet run | off: false calls 10 percent at 10 repeats (4 percent at 5) on the production prompt, over the 2 percent bar; rewrite 1 of 8 rows at the bar | off: rewrite 2 of 15 rows at the bar, and 0 fitting searches means the model never chooses a tool on its own |
| `query_writer` | model (builder on a grounding failure), pending the quiet run | builder | builder |
| `rounds` | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `tools_offered` | the ordinary set (recall, remember, websearch) plus the installed packages' fixed sorted set per U1 | the same set, unused while `model_transitions` is off | the same, unused |
| `answer_from_context_tool` | on | off (no model-driven transitions) | off |
| `thinking_for_minors` | false | false | false |
| `context_tokens` | 4,000 | 4,000 | 2,048 (an 8K context engine) |
| deadlines (model, tool, total) | 20 s, 10 s, 45 s | 20 s, 10 s, 45 s | 20 s, 10 s, 45 s |
| measured on | 2026-09-22, b10797 | 2026-09-22, b10797, confirmed twice | 2026-09-22, b10797 |

What "off" means for the 4B and the 1.7B: the machine runs identically, the model node runs with `tool_choice: "none"`, the interim rule's forced search is still the engine's (always-search on means the search runs with the model writing nothing), so a world question still gets a sourced answer from the engine-built fallback query, and the model phrases. That is the robot-class shape, and the 1.7B is the first model measured into it.

**Which catalog records the U2 session fills.** The catalog holds one chat record today, the 8B (`modelCatalog.ts`, id `qwen3-8b-instruct-q4-k-m`); it gets the 8B column as `turn_budget` (spec first, U2a). The 4B and the 1.7B are files on disk (the 4B serves the judge role, the 1.7B is unassigned), not catalog chat records; they get records only if they are offered as chat models, and until then a model without a record runs with `model_transitions` off, which their numbers say is right anyway. The 4B column above is the record to write if it is offered.

**The query-rewrite acceptance** (U2's own number for "the model writes the query") is pending a quiet 8B run of all 15 rows; the four attempted rows scored 3 of 4, 4 of 4, contended, 9 of 9 among the repeats that replied, which is consistent with passing and proves nothing at this sample. The 1.7B's 2 of 15 rows and the 4B's 1 of 8 say those classes do not write queries reliably, which their `query_writer: builder` reflects.

**U6, the flip: not yet.** U2d's live replay tonight: the old path passed 2 of 6 failed rows and 12 of 13 controls (solid); the new path passed 0 of 7 failed rows and 8 of 13 controls, under a grounding check built as a literal substring match that the state record never meant (it refused rephrased queries and control rows alike; the record now states the term-level contract, 2a28e4e8). The recommendation is to rerun U2d after that fix and decide on the rerun; tonight's numbers are recorded as they are and do not count against the design. The flip's bar is unchanged: every failed row passes on the new path, no control row regresses, and "hi" is under the skeleton's 2.5 s median.

**Astra's amendments (outside review, 2026-09-22).** "0 of 50 false calls" is overstated: it is 0 of 50 outside always-offer, with 10 of 50 lookup calls on the negatives ungraded, over five questions at ten repeats; the one-sided 95 percent upper bound on 0 of 50 is about 5.8 percent, so the 2 percent bar is not established by this sample, and `model_transitions` on for the 8B is provisional on that ground too. Every capability number is versioned against the model artifact (file and hash), the engine build, the prompt and the tool set it ran under, and is invalid when any of the four changes. The `answer_from_context_tool` column reads false for every model until the escape returns (state record). MEASURE-02's centrepiece is end-to-end search success on fresh held-out multi-turn conversations through the shipping configuration, with timeouts counted as failures, compared against the builder fallback.

**Still owed, as MEASURE-02:** the 8B query-rewrite on all 15 rows in a gate-free window;  the 4B rewrite rows 9 to 15; latency per model with the LAT-03 probe; the Studio's model on arrival. None of these blocks U2's build; the 8B rewrite blocks U2d's acceptance and the 4B confirmation blocks its record.

## U4: the answer register by surface, landed on the new path (2026-09-23, `f17dcc1b`)

RESP-01's budget half (ARCH-AMEND-01's accepted design): length lives in the plan and nowhere else. `surfaceClassOf(surface, spoken?)` declares the three classes once (chat/tv written, robot/pod/phone spoken, overlay glance, `spoken: true` forces spoken for a dictated chat turn); `register.ts`'s `planFor` reads an optional `surfaceClass`, defaulting to "spoken" so the frozen path's four call sites keep today's exact numbers untouched. `turnNext.ts` computes the class once, per the state record's "decided once, never recomputed" rule, and passes it into its one `planFor` call - still the plan's only length authority (`maxTokensFor` in `nodes/model.ts` was already reading `plan.max_words`, so it needed no change).

**The written budget, by act (no evidence bump unless noted):**

| Act | Spoken (unchanged) | Written |
|---|---|---|
| greeting | 15 words / 1 sentence | 15 / 1 (same reaction shape - "hi" still gets "hey") |
| closing | 8 / 1 | 8 / 1 |
| backchannel | 20 / n/a | 25 / 2 |
| inform | 30 / 2 | 90 / 6 |
| commissive | 20 / n/a | 40 / 3 |
| directive | 25 / n/a | 160 / 10 |
| question | 60 / 2 (1 on robot) | 220 / 14, **360 / 24** with a source, a deliverable, or two choices |

The child band's 40-word cap holds on every class; `brevity: true` on the written class uses the spoken row for that turn (not a second written table). A known, named gap: `turnNext.ts`'s one `planFor` call still hardcodes `evidence: { choices: 0, sources: 0, deliverable: false }` before any tool round runs, so the 360/24 evidence-boosted row is unreachable on the new path today - the plan is computed once, upfront, never re-derived after real evidence exists. Closing that (re-planning after a tool outcome, or moving the plan computation later in the machine) is its own unit, out of U4's own scope.

`replyConstraints.ts`'s `constraintsFor` gained an optional `currentTurnId`: a `length`/`shape` row now expires after its setting turn's own next three done turns (a banned phrase, or a row with no setting turn, never expires); the frozen path's one call site (no second argument) is unaffected.

**Benches.** `written-set.ts` (new): twenty typed questions (fact/how-to/comparison/list/small-talk) on the new path, each row `humanVerdict`-judged (conversationScore.ts's own convention for a completeness call no regex should make) rather than deterministically scored. Run scripted here (this session's environment has no live engine to spare) - 20/20 mechanically clean, meaning the harness and the path both work; the actual "complete for a typed reader, against the ChatGPT bar" judgment still needs a live run with a reader reading the replies, not yet done. The existing offline guards bench (`conversation.ts`, no engine needed) reran clean at its own documented 22/29 baseline (the two failures, `chest-pain-urges-help` and `no-oh-nice-opener`, predate this change) - no regression, since `guards.ts` was untouched.

**Narrowed from RESP-01's own scope (coordinator's ruling, 2026-09-22):** the persona-prompt half - `WRITTEN_POLICY` beside `NATURALNESS_POLICY`, `composePersonaPrompt(persona, surfaceClass)` - stayed out. `turnMachine/messages.ts` builds the new path's system message from `ContextItem`s alone; it never calls `composePersonaPrompt` today, on either register, a pre-existing gap this item found rather than caused. Wiring the written policy in without first giving the new path ANY persona prompt would be a half-finished change, so it is named instead: BACKLOG.md's U4b.

A code review before landing caught two real, low-severity gaps, both closed: `surfaceClassOf`'s own branches (the `spoken` override, the `overlay` mapping) had no direct test - `surfaceClass.test.ts` now covers every branch; and `stillWithinWindow`'s decay query has no upper bound at `currentTurnId`'s own position, so a caller evaluating an out-of-order turn would over-count the window - unreachable today (nothing calls it out of order), now stated as an explicit caller contract in a comment rather than guarded against speculatively.

## An infinite render loop in the shell header's own data bridge, caught building CHAT-HEADER-01 (2026-09-22)

`chatHeaderData.tsx`'s `useSetChatHeaderData(data)` depended on `data` itself in its `useEffect` - `data` is a fresh object literal on every render of the caller (`ChatHeaderDataBridge`, `NextChatPage.tsx`), so the effect re-ran and called the context's own `setData` on every single render. `setData` changes `ChatHeaderDataProvider`'s state, which re-renders every consumer of that context INCLUDING THE CALLER ITSELF, producing another fresh object and re-triggering the effect again, with nothing to ever settle it - a genuine unconditional loop, not a hypothetical one. It never showed up building or testing the feature because every test up to that point rendered `NextChatPage` with no real `ChatHeaderDataProvider` in its ancestry (the context's own default value has a no-op `setData`), so the loop's one trigger condition - a REAL provider actually in the tree, which is always true in production (`NextRoutesInner` wraps every `/next` page in one) - was never exercised until a regression test for a different bug (the temporary-chat race) finally wrapped the page in a real provider for the first time. Fixed by depending on the primitive fields that actually distinguish one call from the next (`title`, `temporaryAllowed`, `shareAllowed`, whether `data` is null) instead of the object's own identity, with a ref holding the latest full value (including its closures) for the one effect run that actually happens. The lesson for any future header-data-shaped bridge: a hook that calls a context setter from an effect must never depend on an object rebuilt every render if that same context can also trigger the caller's own re-render - the two facts together are the loop, and neither one alone shows it.
## DICT-01: dictation did nothing in any browser - a wire-shape mismatch, not a Firefox bug (2026-09-23)

Jesse's own report: "I don't think dictation works in the browser yet" (Firefox, `/next/chat` on 8787, the mic button `createSttDictationAdapter` wires to `WS /api/stt/stream`). Diagnosed with a headless-Chromium repro first (a throwaway backend, its own temp data dir with the real dev hub's `voice/stt/` assets symlinked in - no ~240 MB copy needed - Playwright launched with `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream` and `--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture` playing a real WAV from the vendored Moonshine model's own `test_wavs/0.wav`, known transcript). Chromium reproduced the exact symptom Jesse saw: the socket opened, the server's `ready` arrived, and nothing else ever happened - zero audio frames left the browser, no error, no crash. Not Firefox-specific at all, so no Firefox-only fix was needed (Playwright Firefox still doesn't launch headless on this machine - "Firefox not verified," 2026-09-22 - so this could not have been checked there directly, but the root cause reproduces identically in a fully supported browser).

**Root cause.** `frontend/src/lib/voice/sttContract.ts` hand-declared its own guessed shape for the server's messages (`{type, text}`) before the real route existed - "the frozen C-to-E contract," dated 2026-09-06. Once the backend shipped, it correctly implemented the real spec (`@maipai/spec/voice/ts/sttTypes.ts`'s `SttWireEvent`: short keys, `{t, v}`), but nobody reconciled the frontend's guess against it. `sttDictationAdapter.ts`'s `switch (message.type)` therefore never matched a single real server message, ever, including `ready` itself - `startMicCapture()` was never called, the whole feature was dead code that looked wired. Fixed by re-exporting the real `SttWireEvent` from the spec (one definition, not a second hand-copy) and switching the adapter on `message.t`/`message.v`; a client-side `hello` message the spec never declared (and the server never read) is gone too. A structured server-side `error` message (`{t:"error", v:string}`) the old contract never declared either now ends the session cleanly instead of falling through the switch unhandled - a second instance of the same silent-no-op shape, caught while fixing the first.

**A second, real bug found fixing the acceptance test.** `NextChatPage.tsx`'s composer-adapters `useMemo` had an empty dependency array with a comment claiming it was harmless because every adapter was "already stably memoized" - true of the attachments adapter, no longer true once the dictation adapter started reacting to `sttStatusQuery.data` (below): with `[]`, the runtime keeps the FIRST `dictationAdapter` forever, built before the STT-status query had answered, so any "installed" check built into it would freeze at whatever it read on that first render. Fixed by adding `attachmentsAdapter`/`dictationAdapter` to the outer memo's own deps (an eslint-disable on the exhaustive-deps warning: the rule can't see that `dictationAdapter`'s own deps genuinely change across renders, and would have reintroduced this exact bug if followed).

**Also built (the coordinator's acceptance line): the not-installed state.** The socket route (`routes/stt.ts`) never checked asset installation before opening a session, so a household without the STT download would have hit the identical silent-nothing shape the wire-mismatch bug had, just for a different reason. `createSttDictationAdapter` now takes `sttInstalled`/`onNotInstalled` deps (mirrors `localImageAttachmentAdapter.ts`'s own vision-capability check): when assets aren't installed, `listen()` never opens a socket or prompts for the mic at all, ends the session immediately, and calls `onNotInstalled()` - `NextChatPage.tsx` wires that to a `sonner` toast and a new `GET /api/voice/stt/status` read (`api.sttStatus()`), permissive (assumed installed) while that query is still loading so the message never flashes false before a real answer exists.

**Verified:** `frontend/src/lib/voice/sttDictationAdapter.test.ts` (17 tests: the wire-shape fix, the new `error` case, the not-installed short-circuit - no socket, no mic prompt), `sttSocket.test.ts` (7, the real shape end to end, no hello sent), `NextChatPage.test.tsx`'s new DICT-01 describe (not-installed: click never opens a session, typing and Send still work - the frozen-memo bug reproduced and was fixed by this exact test). Full frontend suite green (671 tests). The "fake 2-second utterance produces a transcript" half is proven by the Chromium repro itself, not a jsdom mock - jsdom has no AudioWorklet to run a real worklet thread in, so a mocked version of that assertion would only prove the mock. The repro's own real transcript, from a fresh throwaway backend with no code changes needed to run it: "After early nightfall, the yellow lamps would light up here and there, the squalid quarter of the brothels" (0.wav's own real content, matching `test_wavs/trans.txt`).

`GET /api/voice/stt/status` had no frontend consumer anywhere before this - added to `api.ts` from the real spec type, no hand-copy.

**A review caught the same not-installed gap on the old shell.** `ChatPage.tsx` (`/chat`, still live-routed, not retired behind `ui.shell.next`) wires the identical `createSttDictationAdapter` and had the identical exposure - missing assets there would have hit the same silent-nothing symptom this whole item exists to fix, just via the install check instead of the wire shape. Same `sttInstalled`/`onNotInstalled` wiring added there too; no frozen-memo risk to fix alongside it, since that page's own `useLocalRuntime` adapters object is inline, rebuilt fresh every render already. A second finding, the same pass: `onNotInstalled`'s toast had no stable id, so repeated mic clicks while still uninstalled stacked duplicate toasts instead of replacing the one already showing - fixed with `{ id: "stt-not-installed" }` on both pages.

## VOICE-LIVE-03: real voice selection, a real microphone picker (2026-09-23)

`VoiceChevron` (already mounted by VOICE-LIVE-01, previously a static placeholder list) now reads and writes the person's real `tts.voice_id` setting: `GET /api/voice/catalog` for the entries, `GET /api/settings?scope=person:<id>` (`api.settingsValues()`) to show which one is already chosen on mount (mirroring `VoiceCatalogSection.tsx`'s own `expand()` - no second read pattern invented), `POST /api/voice/catalog/select` (`api.selectVoiceFromCatalog()`, the same route Settings already calls) on selection, with an optimistic local update and a query-cache invalidation so a failed write self-corrects on the next menu open instead of a toast.

New `MicrophoneGroup`, appended below the voice list in the same chevron menu: `useAudioInputDevices()` calls `navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices()` (no permission prompt to call it, only to get real labels back - `MediaDeviceInfo.label` is empty until the household has granted mic permission at least once, the honest `Microphone N` fallback for that case) and refreshes on `devicechange`. RESP-04 (f)'s ruling applied directly: fewer than two audio-input devices and the group renders nothing, not a disabled trigger - the common one-laptop household never sees a picker with nothing to pick between. The choice writes `frontend/src/lib/voice/micDevicePreference.ts` (new, the same plain module-level `localStorage` read/write pair as `shellNextCache.ts`, the one existing precedent for a per-browser preference), key `maipai.chat.mic-device-id`. `mic-capture.ts` gained a `deviceId?: string` option, spread as `{ deviceId: { exact: deviceId } }` into the `getUserMedia` constraints when set - `exact`, not `ideal`: a stale id (the device was unplugged since the preference was written) fails loudly as a real permission error, never silently opens a different microphone than the one chosen. `sttDictationAdapter.ts` reads the preference at the start of every session (`readMicDevicePreference() ?? undefined`) - the CURRENT session's already-live stream is never re-opened mid-flight, only the next one.

**The wake-word shortcut clause is deferred, not dropped.** The original item's third clause ("only when a wakeword package is installed, offers the shortcut to that device's declared wake-word setting") has nothing to point at yet: HANDSFREE-01 (c) (below) is the item that defines the settings key a device's wake word lives under, and no "wakeword package installed" concept exists on Home's side either - only a Stack engine role of that name, a different thing entirely. Building the shortcut now would mean inventing both the key and the install concept inside this file, exactly the kind of second copy the platform's "one definition, one place" principle forbids. `composerVoiceControls.tsx` implements the honest absent case today (nothing rendered); the present case is HANDSFREE-01 (c)'s own scope once that key exists.

**Verified:** `composerVoiceControls.test.tsx` gained a fourth test (VOICE-LIVE-03) - two fake input devices, both listed in the open chevron menu, choosing the second writes `maipai.chat.mic-device-id` via `readMicDevicePreference()`. The existing three tests needed two real fixes, not cosmetic ones: the mocked fetch's generic `{}` fallback broke `VoiceChevron`'s new `currentQuery.data?.find()` once it started reading real settings (added an explicit `/api/settings` -> `[]` case); and `MicrophoneGroup`'s `enumerateDevices()`/`devicechange` calls need a `navigator.mediaDevices` fake in bun's test environment (the same `Object.defineProperty` pattern `useWakeWord.test.ts` and `sttDictationAdapter.test.ts` already use) - unmounting before restoring it needs an extra microtask tick, since the effect cleanup that calls `removeEventListener` runs as a passive effect a tick after `unmount()` returns, not synchronously within it. The first test's own name and comment were stale after VOICE-LIVE-01b (2026-09-23): "no Stack configured" no longer means an empty roles list, so it's reworded to what it actually tests now (the overview reporting no roles at all, e.g. before the query resolves). `NextChatPage.test.tsx`'s own VOICE-LIVE-01 "both ready" test needed the identical two fixes (it mounts the real `ComposerVoiceControls` too) once VOICE-LIVE-03 started calling real settings/mediaDevices from inside it.

## ENGINE-CONTRACT-01: the first recorded failure, `tool_choice: "required"` on a warm KV cache (2026-09-23)

Filed upstream 2026-09-23 as ggml-org/llama.cpp issue 29295 (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29295), the four sets, the log lines and the open question on grammar enforcement.

The pinned chat engine (llama-server b10797, macOS arm64, the hub's own
`qwen3-8b-instruct-q4-k-m.gguf`, the hub's flags: one slot, 32K
context, `-fa on`, `--reasoning off`, `--jinja`, `--cache-reuse 256`,
q8_0 KV) does not honour `tool_choice: "required"` once the slot's KV
cache holds the request's prefix. Found by the oMLX versus llama-server
tier 1 bench (`data-scratch/omlx-vs-llama/results.md`, "Re-checks
(2026-09-23)", raw reps in its `logs/`), on a side instance on port
8798, the hub untouched. The request in every set: user "who is the
president of chile", `tools: [websearch]` (the hub's own manifest as an
OpenAI function tool), `tool_choice: "required"`, `chat_template_kwargs:
{enable_thinking: false}`, `max_tokens` 64, temperature 0.

| Set | Shape | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | the identical prompt five times, `cache_prompt: false` | 5/5 tool calls, `cached_tokens` 0 every rep |
| A2 | the identical prompt five times, `cache_prompt: true`, cache warm | 0/5; `cached_tokens` 197 of 198 every rep; a knowledge answer ("The current president of Chile is...") with `tool_calls: []` |
| A3 | five distinct prompts (chile, peru, norway, kenya, japan), `cache_prompt: true` | 2/5; peru and norway called the tool on partial prefix reuse (187 cached), kenya and japan answered from knowledge on the same partial reuse, chile failed on the full hit |
| A4 | A2 again on a fresh restart with `--cache-reuse 0` | 1/5; rep 0 on the empty cache called the tool, reps 1 to 4 failed exactly as A2 |

The server's own lines on every full-hit failure (A2, one block per rep):

```
W slot   operator(): id  0 | task 185 | need to evaluate at least 1 token for each active slot (n_past = 198, task.n_tokens() = 198)
W slot   operator(): id  0 | task 185 | n_past was set to 197
```

The partial-reuse failures (A3 kenya and japan) log no warning at all:
ten or eleven new tokens evaluated, then a knowledge answer. So the
defect is not the clamp line; it tracks any KV reuse on the slot, and
`--cache-reuse 0` (which only disables chunk reuse after an edit) does
not touch it. The original bench run showed the same shape: rep 0 on an
empty cache passed, four identical follow-ups on the warm cache failed.

**What this means for the hub.** The hub sends `cache_prompt: true` on
every chat call (`backend/src/lib/llm.ts`), by design (U1 made the
prompt cache-stable so that `cache_reuse_tokens` grows with the
conversation). So on the hub, the interim rule's forced search
(`backend/src/lib/turnMachine/nodes/model.ts`, `tool_choice:
"required"` over the websearch tool) is unreliable on exactly the turns
it is for: the second world question in a conversation, and any question
whose prefix the slot already holds. The always_search budget for the 8B
assumed `required` holds on this build; it does not. The reply the
engine returns instead is the model's own knowledge answer, which the
interim rule forbids showing.

**Re-check C settles the mechanism: `required` is advisory on this
build.** A grammar-enforced `required` cannot produce plain content
whatever the cache state, so the A3 split (two of four pass on the same
partial reuse) read like a near-tie flipped by numerics rather than a
cache path skipping a constraint. Re-check C tested that directly: A1's
request with `cache_prompt: false` (so `cached_tokens` 0 on every rep,
no cache anywhere in the set), temperature 0.7 and a distinct `seed` per
rep, ten reps (`results.md` "Re-check C", `logs/recheck-c.jsonl`).

| rep | seed | cached_tokens | tool call | reply |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 to 6 | 1000 to 1006 | 0 | yes | `expression: "president of chile"` |
| 7 | 1007 | 0 | no | "The current president of Chile is ..." |
| 8 | 1008 | 0 | no | the same knowledge answer |
| 9 | 1009 | 0 | yes | `expression: "president of chile"` |

8/10. Two reps answered from knowledge with no cache in play, which a
grammar would have made impossible. So on llama-server b10797 with the
Qwen3 template under `--jinja`, `tool_choice: "required"` is not
enforced by a grammar; the prompt only asks for a call, and the model
is near a tie between calling and answering. At temperature 0 the
deterministic path lands on the call from a cold cache and on the
answer once the slot's KV reuse shifts the logits (A2, A3, A4); at
temperature 0.7 sampling alone flips it on about one rep in five. The
cache-hit failures are one instance of the same near-tie, not a second
bug. The upstream draft at
`data-scratch/omlx-vs-llama/upstream-issue-llama-server-required.md`
(scratch, roster-safe) is retitled accordingly, for the coordinator to
file.

**The hub runs this request at temperature 0.7, so the miss is the
common case.** The model node passes no temperature
(`backend/src/lib/turnMachine/nodes/model.ts`, the `startCompleteStream`
call), so `chatRequestBody` in `backend/src/lib/llm.ts` applies
`CHAT_SAMPLING` (FAST-06: temperature 0.7, `min_p` 0.05, XTC and DRY
on) to every tool-calling completion, forced or offered. Re-check C's
one-in-five was measured at 0.7 without the hub's `min_p`, XTC and
DRY, so the hub's own miss rate is the nearest measurement, not a
record; ENGINE-CONTRACT-02's `required_miss` counter is that record.
FAST-06's note that the tool-calling bench "holds every positive and
every negative" with the set on was measured under `auto`; it says
nothing about `required`, which this finding now does.

**The ruling, four parts (2026-09-23).**

1. *The hub-side fix, `ENGINE-CONTRACT-02` in the backlog.* The model
   node verifies that a reply to a `required` call carries a tool call.
   On a miss it does not re-issue the call with `cache_prompt: false`
   (a second full prefill: 24.7 s at 8K on this Mac by LAT-03's
   numbers, and A3 shows partial reuse fails too, so "cache off on every
   forced request" would pay that prefill on every world question for a
   fix that only helps the identical-repeat case). It falls to the
   transition row the state record already has for a model without tool
   calling: the engine builds the query (`query_writer: builder`),
   `policy` and `tool` run the search, and the model phrases from the
   result with `tool_choice: "none"`. The miss reply's text is discarded,
   never shown, never persisted as an answer. The generation record
   gains `cached_tokens` and `prompt_tokens` from `usage`, and the trace's
   `stats.nodes[]` entry for `model` gains `required_miss: true` on such a
   turn, so `interimRuleMeasure` counts misses by cache state and the
   upstream bug has a live counter on the hub. Nothing is designed anew:
   the builder row exists; the miss is one more way into it.
2. *GROUND-01's live rerun runs now, not held.* Its harness records
   `cached_tokens`, `prompt_tokens` and `required_honored` per request. A
   row that fails only because the forced call was not honoured is
   classified "engine (ENGINE-CONTRACT-01)", counted, and excluded from
   the grounding pass bar, because the rerun measures whether the
   grounding check passes the searches the model does make. If the
   forced rows' miss share is above one third, the forced rows are rerun
   once with `cache_prompt: false` for the grounding reading, and both
   tables are reported. The interim rule's forced search is understood as
   unreliable on cache hits until ENGINE-CONTRACT-02 lands.
3. *The earlier bake-off numbers are not remeasured.* The 8B's 0/50
   false calls under `auto` stands: a numerics flip toward a call would
   have surfaced as a false call and none did. Its 19/50 fitting searches
   under `auto` is marked in its table as a lower bound with the cache
   state unrecorded. From today every tool-calling table carries
   `cached_tokens` per request, and the U6 recommendation reads only
   tables that do (U2d's rerun provides them).
4. *oMLX clears its contract subset* with thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs:
   {enable_thinking: false}`, the request shape the hub sends the 8B):
   auto-negative 5/5, required 5/5, reasoning separated, its own timing
   fields present. The original 0/5 was the bench design's own omission
   (the auto-negative row lacked the kwarg the required row had), now
   corrected in the design. The latency half is worth a quiet window once
   tonight's gates end; the rule stays warm 8K effective rate unless the
   peak breaks the p16 margin. Its 5/5 on `required` across identical
   repeats is recorded as a point in its favour for the tool-heavy path,
   not as decisive: whether its own prefix cache was warm on those reps
   is unrecorded, and its abort check's verdict is still open (it needs
   the warm short median the latency half produces).

## VOICE-LIVE-01b: the overview route only ever knew about a Stack (2026-09-23)

Live finding, same evening as VOICE-LIVE-01: Jesse reloaded 8787 (no Stack configured - this hub runs Home's own supervisors) and saw no waveform button in the composer. Traced to `backend/src/routes/engines.ts`'s overview route: `if (!isStackConfigured()) return c.json({configured: false, roles: [], engines: [], budget: null}, 200);` - `roles` was unconditionally empty whenever no Stack existed, so every frontend gate reading it (`readyRole()`, `frontend/src/apps/chat/engineRoles.ts`) could never see `stt`/`tts` as ready, no matter how healthy Home's own supervisors actually were. The identical gate silently hides `CreateImageItem` in `composerAddMenu.tsx`. VOICE-LIVE-01's own acceptance test mocked the overview response directly, so it never exercised this real code path.

**The fix.** `backend/src/lib/homeSupervisorRoles.ts` (new): `getHomeSupervisorRoles()` returns the same `RoleInfo[]` shape (`backend/src/lib/stack/types.ts`) the Stack already returns, built from Home's own supervisors instead - one shape, two sources, `readyRole()` never needs to know which answered. Wired into the overview route's existing no-Stack branch only; the Stack-configured path is untouched.

**Readiness semantics, kept to one meaning.** `llmSupervisor.ts`, `ttsSupervisor.ts` and `embedSupervisor.ts` each document the identical tier list in their own header comments: a URL override, then a real spawn, then - the last tier, always reached when nothing else applies - "start the in-process stub server. Real code path," never a failure. There is no "not installed" state for chat/tts/embed: only "hasn't answered a request yet this boot" versus "already has" - so the coordinator's own framing, "ready when installed and startable, not only while running," holds for the default case. The first version of this fix stopped there and reported `ready` unconditionally for all three. A medium-effort code review (before commit, per org standard) caught the gap: `GET /api/health` already tracks real live state for these same three engines - `probeChatEngine()`/`probeTtsEngine()`/`probeEmbedEngine()` (same files) return `kind: "stopped"` when an admin used the AI-models page's Stop control, `"failed"`/`"restarting"` mid crash-loop, and `alive: false` when a real probe came back negative - and this route could report `ready` for an engine Health was showing red for, at the same moment. `chatRole()`/`ttsRole()`/`embedRole()` now `await` those same probe functions (no new network behavior - `GET /api/health` already makes this exact call) and read `offline` for `stopped`/`failed`/`restarting`/`alive === false`, `ready` otherwise (an `alive === null` - no client yet, the common never-asked-this-boot case - is not a failure, since the guaranteed stub tier means it would answer if asked). A second re-review pass on that same fix found one more gap in the mapping: `kind: "starting"` (a JIT spawn genuinely in flight - `alive` still null because no client exists yet to probe) was falling into the same bucket as "never asked this boot" and reading `ready`, at the exact moment `GET /api/health`'s own badge reads "starting up" - the same class of cross-surface disagreement this item exists to close. `stateFromProbe()` now reads `starting` as `loaded` (the one `RoleState` value that already means "in progress, not confirmed answering yet," `NextEnginesPage.tsx`'s own `ROLE_STATE_LABEL`), so a role only reads `ready` once it is either confirmed alive or has genuinely never been asked anything with no spawn underway. `sttRole()` is the one real exception - `lib/stt.ts`'s sherpa-onnx-node recognizer is an in-process native addon with no stub tier and no probe function at all, so it is real assets on disk (`sttAssetsInstalled()`) or nothing, and reports `notInstalled` honestly until they are. `imageRole()` reports `notInstalled` too, for a different reason: nothing is implemented on the Home side yet (`modelCatalog.ts`'s two image entries are both `implemented: false`, no supervisor, no probe) - included in the roles array rather than omitted, so a caller iterating every role id gets a real answer for all five, the same "null, not silently missing" posture `dashboard.ts`'s own `engineStatusCounts()` already takes.

**Verified with real handlers, not a mocked overview** - the exact gap that let the original bug ship: `backend/tests/enginesRoutes.test.ts`'s existing "no Stack configured" test asserted the literal empty-roles shape verbatim; rewritten to assert the real five-role response instead (chat/tts/embed ready, stt/image notInstalled, in a fresh test data dir with no assets staged, nothing stopped or crashed). A second test stages real Silero+Moonshine files on disk (mirroring `stt.test.ts`'s own fixture pattern) and confirms `stt` flips to `ready` - the composer's own actual gate. A third, new test calls the real `stopChatBackend()` (the admin Stop control's own function) and confirms `chat` reads `offline` with reason "Manually stopped." here, proving this route and `GET /api/health` can no longer disagree about the same engine - the review's exact failure scenario, now a permanent regression test. The Stack-configured test (`configure({...})`, asserts `roles[0].id === "chat"` from the fixture) is untouched, proving the other path's own behavior didn't move. The `starting` gap is a different kind of test: a real spawn in flight is timing-dependent and hits real hardware/binaries, not something the deterministic per-commit suite should trigger (Testing standards, org `CLAUDE.md`) - so `stateFromProbe()` (now exported) got its own `backend/tests/homeSupervisorRoles.test.ts`, one row per `EngineHealthKind`, fabricated `EngineHealth` values, no process ever spawned.

## VOICE-LIVE-02: the live voice session, landed with the measurement still owed (2026-09-23)

Landed `906d740b`, `docs/BACKLOG.md`'s own row. Built: `frontend/src/apps/chat/liveVoiceSession.tsx` drives the shipped `VoiceConversation` Element through the real STT session (`sttSocket.ts`, `mic-capture.ts`) and the real send path (`aui.composer.setText()` + `.send()`, so the transcript lands in the thread exactly like a typed message, no second message-creation path), with `spoken: true` on the wire (`turnNext.ts`'s `TurnState.spoken`, read by `decideReasoning()` in `nodes/context.ts` the same way a non-chat surface is) and the reply spoken sentence by sentence through `chatModelAdapter.ts`'s own pre-existing `SentenceSpeechScheduler` integration, made dynamic (`speakReplies` as a getter) rather than duplicated. The level meter is a local `AnalyserNode` (`audioLevelMeter.ts`) on the mic's stream while listening and the scheduler's own playback bus while speaking, computed in the browser and sent nowhere - the owner's privacy ruling, 2026-09-23.

**Two defects caught before landing, both by code review.** (1) `isSpeaking` alone missed a reply that never spoke at all (an empty reply, or every sentence's TTS synthesis failing) - `onSpeakingChange(false)` is a same-value React update in that case, so the effect resuming listening never re-ran and the session stuck on "Thinking" forever; fixed with a `speakingEndedAt` counter, bumped on every `false` call regardless of the previous value, threaded through as its own dependency rather than relying on `isSpeaking`'s own transition. (2) Mid-build, rebasing onto a peer session's DICT-01 fix (the dictation adapter's own STT wire contract was wrong - `{type, text}` guessed, `{t, v}` real, from `@maipai/spec`) surfaced that this file's own first draft carried the identical wrong guess, never yet shipped; rewritten to the real contract before it could ship broken the same way, with a new `error` case (`{t: "error", v: string}`) this file didn't have before.

**VOICE-LIVE-03 landed concurrently** (a peer session, the composer chevron's real voice/microphone picker) touching the same three files (`composerVoiceControls.tsx`, `mic-capture.ts`, `NextChatPage.tsx`); the rebase conflicts were additive in every case (VOICE-LIVE-03's `deviceId` field beside this item's `onSource` field on `MicCaptureOptions`, `VoiceChevron`'s new `personId` prop beside the waveform's `onClick` wiring, `BoundComposerVoiceControls` beside `voiceOpen` state) and a low-effort review of the merged hunks specifically (not either feature's own logic, already reviewed separately) found nothing wrong.

**The measurement is the one acceptance line not met.** The row asks for the first spoken word under 3 seconds after the utterance ends, beside the resident 8B, measured on this Mac with `turn.pipeline.next` both on and off. This session has no real engine and no real microphone to produce that number - the same class of gap `docs/dev.md`'s "Firefox not verified" line names for a different check (2026-09-22: a check that needs real hardware this sandbox doesn't have is named honestly rather than skipped silently or fabricated). Code review, typecheck, eslint and the full test suite (`bash scripts/check.sh`, green) all pass; the row stays unticked until someone with this Mac's own hardware runs the two timed calls and records them here.

## U6: the flip verdict after the live rerun (2026-09-23)

The verdict on the tables above ("GROUND-01: the live acceptance
rerun"): **not yet.** The new path beats the old on the rows that were
broken (5 of 8 clean against 3 of 8, the diagnosed chile turn grounding
and searching on both paths, no row refusing on `category` or
`read_page` anywhere) and loses three controls the old path holds, and
the controls are the household's everyday turns. The three are not
grounding defects and not new-path design faults: read from the code
they are two integration gaps, each with a one-place fix, and the flip
waits for those two fixes and one rerun against the bar at the end of
this section.

### Regression A: a real websearch outcome with empty arguments

`control-search-mariners-explicit` repeat 3 and the hallucinated-name
follow-up's repeat 1 turn 2 both show `websearch/tool_call {}` and a
knowledge answer ("I cannot directly search the web for real-time
information ..." and "Gabriel Boric Font was born on July 24, 1989").
The chain, node by node: the engine returned a `websearch` call whose
`arguments` string did not parse (or was empty); `toolCallFromWire` in
`backend/src/lib/llm.ts` turns a parse failure into `args: undefined`;
`nodes/policy.ts` normalizes `call.args ?? {}` and `checkGrounding`
over zero entries passes, since there is nothing to refuse; `nodes/
tool.ts` runs it and `runPlugin`'s schema validation fails on the
missing required `expression`, recording the outcome as failed, via
`tool_call`, args `{}`; the machine then takes the failed outcome back
to `model` (the `moreRoundsAvailable` transition in `machine.ts`),
where round two has no tools left and answers from knowledge. So the
search "ran", produced nothing, and the person got the model's own
answer with no refusal and no source: the same near-tie as
ENGINE-CONTRACT-01, one level down (the model half-commits to a call
and never writes the query). The layer is the model node's
verification, which ENGINE-CONTRACT-02 already owns: its check becomes
"a `websearch` call whose `expression` is a non-empty string", forced
or offered (the bench judge's own definition of a pass), and a call
that fails it is a miss that takes the builder row, never runs, and is
never fed back as a failed outcome for a second round. The trace does
not keep the engine's raw `arguments` string (the generation record
holds the parsed `ToolCall` only), so ENGINE-CONTRACT-02 records it
beside `cached_tokens`; whether these two were a parse failure or a
literal `{}` is read from that field on the next run, and the fix is
the same either way.

### Regression B: `recall` instead of nothing on a negative control

`control-negative-spiderman` repeat 3 and `control-negative-feeling-down`
repeat 1 show `ran recall (source plugin)` and a fine reply, at twice
the time (10,873 ms against 5,283 and 5,176 for the clean repeats;
8,694 against 4,307 and 4,484). The layer is the offered set, not the
model and not a rule: the 8B budget in `modelCatalog.ts` offers six
tools (`recall`, `remember`, `remind`, `timer`, `weather`, `websearch`),
and the context node (`nodes/context.ts`) already calls `recall(actor,
utterance)` on every turn and places up to eight matches in the context
as `source: "memory"`. The `recall` tool is a second implementation of
a retrieval the model already holds in its context (one definition,
one implementation), so at temperature 0.7 the model reaches for it one
time in three on small talk and pays a whole round for nothing new.
The fix is `TOOLSET-01`: `recall` leaves every budget's `tools_offered`
on the new path; memory reaches the model through context only. The
old path is untouched. Not a prompt sentence, not a word rule.

### The France 60 percent, and ENGINE-CONTRACT-02's design

`interimRuleMeasure`'s France conversation (the identical question
asked twice) misses the forced call 60 percent of the time against
chile's 30. In a conversation the second identical question is not a
full-prefix cache hit (the first question and its answer now sit in the
window before it), so this is the partial-reuse case of A3 plus the
strongest possible pull toward answering: the answer is in the window,
and the answer-from-this-conversation escape is off by design. It
changes nothing in ENGINE-CONTRACT-02: the counter by cache state stays
the number, and the builder row is not preferred outright on an
identical repeat, because "identical repeat" is a word rule by another
name (RULES-AND-LEARNED-COMPONENTS.md) and the verify-and-fallback
reaches the builder on the same turn anyway at the cost of one wasted
generation. When the escape turns on, that case becomes an allowed
answer from context and the miss stops being one. Two consequences the
number does carry: `interimRuleMeasure`'s `answer_from_context` line is
renamed `required_miss` (the tool is never offered, so the heuristic was
counting misses), and the counter sits beside time-to-first-token per
outcome, so the fallback's extra generation is measured on the France
shape (15,478 ms median already), never assumed.

### The bar for the next rerun (the flip's own acceptance)

Run after ENGINE-CONTRACT-02 and TOOLSET-01 land, same fixture, three
repeats, both paths, live on the 8B:

1. Every failed row that was clean on this rerun stays clean
   (`president-of-france-repeat`, `apple-announce-this-week`,
   `search-mariners-game`, `chatgpt-6-luna`,
   `corey-feldman-michael-jackson-friendship`), and no row is classed
   engine: with ENGINE-CONTRACT-02 landed a miss takes the builder row,
   so a forced turn produces a search or a real failure, never an
   engine exclusion.
2. The three controls back to clean on every repeat
   (`control-search-mariners-explicit`, `control-negative-spiderman`,
   `control-negative-feeling-down`), and every control row's median
   time-to-first-token within 1.25 times the old path's on the same
   run, because regression B showed as latency and a "no tool" bar
   alone would not catch the next one.
3. `control-negative-stephen-king`'s expectation flips: "what's the
   latest Stephen King novel" is a world question with a fresh fact
   under the adopted interim rule, so the row expects a `websearch` with
   `expression` matching `stephen king`; both paths "over-searched"
   against a bar the legacy corpus wrote, not the design (`REPLAY-BAR-01`).
4. `president-of-chile-when-born` turn 3 ("yes") is its own row,
   `CONFIRM-01`, outside the flip's bar: a "yes" to the hub's own offer
   to look something up must run the search the offer named, and both
   paths fail it today (parity, not regression).
   `primetime-trailer-correction` and turns 1 and 2 of the chile row are
   parity failures too (the model answering from memory with no call, a
   signal question), outside the bar and named in `SIGNAL-01`.

The flip happens when 1 to 3 hold on one rerun; rows 4's items are
the next block's, not the flip's.

main and the acceptance rerun ran immediately after: same
`owner-replay.json` fixture, 3 repeats, `--hub-live`, both paths,

the next gate on this machine started at 08:43 UTC, after the new-path

**Verdict: not yet.** Two of the three bar conditions did not hold.

Two of the five regressed. `president-of-france-repeat` repeat 3 is the

All three controls did reach 3/3 clean on the new path (up from the

|---|---|---|---|

| control-negative-spiderman | 854 | 5067 | 5.9x |
| control-negative-feeling-down | 799 | 5388 | 6.7x |

itself. Reported as a confounded measurement, not a design regression:

`control-negative-dye-hair` regressed once on the new path (2/3

controls reaching 3/3) is confirmed working. What is not yet
confirmed: whether ENGINE-CONTRACT-02's fallback is reliable on every

**Voice and microphone, now one section in Settings.** `frontend/src/apps/settings/VoiceCatalogSection.tsx` ("More voices," Settings > Voice) gained a `MicrophoneSection` - the exact code `MicrophoneGroup` used to run (`useAudioInputDevices()`, `micLabel()`, `micDevicePreference.ts`'s read/write pair), moved rather than rewritten, rendered as a second control below the voice list with "The microphone choice is remembered on this device only." underneath it. RESP-04 (f)'s ruling still applies: fewer than two devices and the whole block renders nothing.

**The catalog has no name field - a real gap, not invented around.** Reading `backend/src/lib/voiceCatalog.ts`'s `VoiceCatalogEntry` and the Hugging Face tree API response it's built from confirmed the catalog carries exactly `path` and `collection`, nothing else - no name, no title, anywhere. `frontend/src/lib/voice/voiceDisplayName.ts` (new) derives a readable name from the file stem instead: strip a trailing real extension (`.safetensors`/`.wav`/`.mp3`), strip a trailing content-hash segment some donated files carry (a dot, 6+ hex characters, an optional `@<number>`), strip a real extension again if the hash sat between two of them (the donation case: `.wav.1e68beda@240.safetensors`), then turn underscores into spaces. `zerocool_enhanced.wav.1e68beda@240.safetensors` reads as `zerocool enhanced`; `p228_023_enhanced.wav` reads as `p228 023 enhanced`; a hyphenated name like `ex04-confused.wav` is untouched past its extension (only underscores become spaces - the transformation isn't evidenced for hyphens, so this session didn't extend it there). **VOICE-LIVE-02's own gear, not built here.** The live session gets a settings-gear entry point into Settings > Voice - Session B's own scope, since it owns `liveVoiceSession.tsx`. Messaged once this item landed. The gear is the only voice control outside Settings once it exists; nothing else should reach back into `tts.voice_id` or the microphone preference from outside `VoiceCatalogSection.tsx`.

**Verified:** `composerVoiceControls.test.tsx` cut to three tests (absent with no roles, absent with only one ready, present as the pill alone with no "Choose a voice" chevron); `NextChatPage.test.tsx`'s own VOICE-LIVE-01 describe simplified the same way, dropping the now-unneeded `navigator.mediaDevices`/`/api/voice/catalog`/`/api/settings` stubbing the chevron used to need. `VoiceCatalogSection.test.tsx` gained tests: the donated-hash file reads as `zerocool enhanced` in the list and in the "currently using" line (never the raw name or the hash), the microphone group is absent below two devices, and two devices list both with the second write proven through `readMicDevicePreference()` - the same assertion VOICE-LIVE-03's own now-deleted chevron test made, moved to where the control now lives. `voiceDisplayName.test.ts` (new) unit-tests the stripping rules directly against the donation example, a plain underscored name, a hyphenated name and a bare file name with no directory. **A low-effort review found two real issues, both fixed.** (1) `HASH_SUFFIX` first matched any trailing run of 6+ hex-valid letters, so a real word that happens to use only a-f (`facade`, `decade`, `deface`) would have been silently deleted as if it were a content hash - fixed by requiring at least one digit in the match (a genuine random hash is all but certain to contain one; a real word rarely does), with `voiceDisplayName.test.ts` gaining the `facade`/`decade` case directly.
